title: Temporally Multimode Ion-Ion Entanglement Over 1.2 Kilometer Fibers
authors: Z.-B. Cui, Z.-Q. Wang, P.-Y. Liu, Y. Wang, P.-C. Lai, J.-X. Shi, Y.-D. Sun, Z.-C. Tian, H.-S. Sun, Y.-B. Liang, B.-X. Qi, Y.-Y. Huang, Z.-C. Zhou, Y.-K. Wu, Y. Xu, Y.-F. Pu, And L.-M. Duan
abstract:
Author(s): Z.-B. Cui, Z.-Q. Wang, P.-Y. Liu, Y. Wang, P.-C. Lai, J.-X. Shi, Y.-D. Sun, Z.-C. Tian, H.-S. Sun, Y.-B. Liang, B.-X. Qi, Y.-Y. Huang, Z.-C. Zhou, Y.-K. Wu, Y. Xu, Y.-F. Pu, and L.-M. Duan

Quantum networks and quantum repeaters represent the promising avenues for building large-scale quantum information systems, serving as foundational infrastructure for distributed quantum computing, long-distance quantum communication, and networked quantum sensing. A critical step in realizing a fu…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 020803] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of temporally multiplexed ion-ion entanglement over 1.2 km fibers, a key step toward quantum repeaters.
motivation: Building large-scale quantum networks requires long-distance entanglement distribution; ion traps are promising but face challenges in generating and distributing entanglement over fiber.
method: Trapped Yb+ ions are entangled via a photonic interface, and the entanglement is temporally multiplexed to overcome loss and decoherence in 1.2 km fiber links.
result: High-fidelity ion-ion entanglement is achieved over 1.2 km fibers with temporal multiplexing, demonstrating a viable approach for quantum repeater nodes.
conclusion: This work advances practical quantum networks by showing that trapped ions can serve as long-distance entanglement sources with multiplexing, enabling scalable quantum communication.

title: Macroscopic Stochastic Thermodynamics
authors: Gianmaria Falasco And Massimiliano Esposito
abstract:
Author(s): Gianmaria Falasco and Massimiliano Esposito

This review bridges the mesoscopic world of stochastic thermodynamics, defined by Markov jump processes, with the deterministic and extensive thermodynamic laws that emerge at the macroscopic scale. Using large deviations theory, it constructs a fluctuation framework preserving core principles like the fluctuation theorem. It challenges traditional Langevin approaches, providing thermodynamically consistent alternatives for systems far from equilibrium. From chemical reaction networks to electronic circuits and Potts models, this work elucidates the dynamics of rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production principles, offering a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015002] Published Wed Jan 22, 2025.
tldr: A review bridging stochastic thermodynamics at the mesoscopic scale with macroscopic thermodynamic laws using large deviations theory.
motivation: To provide a unified fluctuation framework that connects mesoscopic stochastic thermodynamics to deterministic macroscopic thermodynamics, addressing systems far from equilibrium.
method: Uses large deviations theory to construct a fluctuation framework for Markov jump processes, deriving thermodynamic laws and fluctuation theorems at the macroscopic scale.
result: Establishes thermodynamically consistent alternatives to traditional Langevin approaches, applicable to chemical reaction networks, electronic circuits, and Potts models.
conclusion: Offers a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines, preserving core principles like the fluctuation theorem.

title: Quantum Geometric Fluctuation-Dissipation Relation For Nonlinear Transport
authors: Rui Wang, Xinyue Liu, Fuming Xu, Jun Chen, Lei Zhang, And Jian Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Rui Wang, Xinyue Liu, Fuming Xu, Jun Chen, Lei Zhang, and Jian Wang

The fluctuation-dissipation theorem connects equilibrium noise to linear response and forms a cornerstone of statistical and quantum physics, yet its extension to geometry-driven nonlinear transport remains largely unexplored. Here we establish a geometric fluctuation-dissipation relation linking dc…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 026301] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: Establishes a geometric fluctuation-dissipation relation for nonlinear quantum transport, linking dc noise to geometric curvature.
motivation: The fluctuation-dissipation theorem is fundamental but its extension to geometry-driven nonlinear transport is unexplored.
method: Derives a geometric fluctuation-dissipation relation using quantum scattering theory and Berry curvature concepts.
result: The relation connects dc noise to the imaginary part of the nonlinear response tensor, revealing geometric contributions to transport.
conclusion: Provides a new tool for understanding nonlinear transport in quantum systems with geometric phases.

title: Noise-Resilient Heisenberg-Limited Quantum Sensing Via Indefinite-Causal-Order Error Correction
authors: Hang Xu, Xiaoyang Deng, Ze Zheng, Tailong Xiao, And Guihua Zeng
abstract:
Author(s): Hang Xu, Xiaoyang Deng, Ze Zheng, Tailong Xiao, and Guihua Zeng

Quantum resources can, in principle, enable Heisenberg-limited sensing, yet no-go theorems imply that Heisenberg-limited scaling is generically unattainable in realistic noisy devices. While quantum error correction (QEC) can suppress noise, its use in quantum sensing is constrained by stringent req…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 020801] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum sensing protocol that uses indefinite causal order (ICO) to achieve Heisenberg-limited scaling even under noise, circumventing no-go theorems.
motivation: Heisenberg-limited quantum sensing is fundamentally limited by noise, and standard quantum error correction is often incompatible with sensing protocols. The authors aim to overcome these limitations using ICO.
method: The protocol employs a quantum switch to create a superposition of causal orders for error correction and sensing operations, effectively decoupling noise while preserving the sensing signal.
result: The ICO-based scheme achieves Heisenberg-limited scaling in the presence of noise, with a scaling advantage over conventional schemes that are limited to the standard quantum limit.
conclusion: Indefinite causal order provides a new resource for noise-resilient quantum sensing, enabling Heisenberg-limited performance in realistic noisy environments.

title: Characterizing Entanglement Shareability And Distribution In $N$-partite Systems
authors: Hui Li, Ting Gao, And Fengli Yan
abstract:
Author(s): Hui Li, Ting Gao, and Fengli Yan

Exploring the shareability and distribution of entanglement possesses fundamental significance in quantum information tasks. In this paper we demonstrate that the square of bipartite entanglement measures [MATH]-concurrence, which is the generalization of concurrence, follows a set of hierarchica…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012204] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper characterizes entanglement shareability and distribution in N-partite systems using squared bipartite entanglement measures, establishing hierarchical monogamy inequalities.
motivation: Understanding how entanglement can be shared among multiple parties is fundamental for quantum information tasks, but a unified framework for N-partite systems was lacking.
method: The authors generalize the concept of concurrence to squared bipartite entanglement measures and derive a set of hierarchical monogamy inequalities that constrain the distribution of entanglement.
result: They prove that the square of bipartite entanglement measures follows hierarchical monogamy relations, providing a complete characterization of entanglement shareability in arbitrary N-partite systems.
conclusion: The results offer a powerful tool for analyzing multipartite entanglement distribution, with implications for quantum cryptography and network protocols.

title: Information Causality Beyond The Random-access-code Model
authors: Baichu Yu And Valerio Scarani
abstract:
Author(s): Baichu Yu and Valerio Scarani

Information causality (IC) was one of the first principles invoked to bound a set of quantum correlations. For some families of correlations, this principle recovers exactly the boundary of the quantum set; for others, there is still a gap. We close some of these gaps using a quantifier for IC based…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012202] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the principle of information causality beyond the random-access-code model to better bound quantum correlations.
motivation: Information causality is a physical principle that aims to characterize quantum correlations, but existing formulations leave gaps between the quantum set and the set allowed by IC. The authors seek to close these gaps by introducing a more general quantifier.
method: The authors propose a new quantifier for information causality based on a broader class of communication tasks beyond random access codes, and analyze its implications for various families of correlations.
result: The new quantifier closes some of the previously known gaps, providing tighter bounds on quantum correlations and recovering the quantum boundary for certain families.
conclusion: Information causality, when properly quantified, is a powerful principle for characterizing quantum correlations, and the proposed extension strengthens its predictive power.

title: Semidefinite Programming For Understanding The Limitations Of Lindblad Equations
authors: Soumyadeep Sarma, Manas Kulkarni, Archak Purkayastha, And Devashish Tupkary
abstract:
Author(s): Soumyadeep Sarma, Manas Kulkarni, Archak Purkayastha, and Devashish Tupkary

Lindbladian quantum master equations (LEs) are the most popular descriptions for quantum systems weakly coupled to baths. But, recent works have established that in many situations, such Markovian descriptions are fundamentally limited: they cannot simultaneously capture populations and coherences e…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012423] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses semidefinite programming to characterize the fundamental limitations of Lindblad master equations in simultaneously capturing populations and coherences.
motivation: Lindblad equations are widely used but have known limitations; understanding these limitations is crucial for accurate modeling of open quantum systems.
method: The authors formulate the problem as a semidefinite program to find the best possible Lindblad equation that approximates a given exact dynamics, and analyze the constraints.
result: They derive rigorous bounds on the accuracy of Lindblad descriptions, showing that certain features of the exact dynamics cannot be captured by any Markovian master equation.
conclusion: The work provides a systematic way to quantify the failure of Markovian approximations, guiding the development of more accurate non-Markovian approaches.

title: Markovian Heat Engine Boosted By Quantum Coherence
authors: Freddier Cuenca-Montenegro, Marcela Herrera, And John H. Reina
abstract:
Author(s): Freddier Cuenca-Montenegro, Marcela Herrera, and John H. Reina

We evaluate the role of quantum coherence as a thermodynamic resource in a noisy, Markovian, one-qubit heat engine. By consuming the coherence of noisy quantum states, we demonstrate that the engine can surpass the classical efficiency limit when operating according to a quantum Otto cycle. The engi…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012424] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: A Markovian one-qubit heat engine can surpass classical efficiency limits by consuming quantum coherence.
motivation: To explore whether quantum coherence can serve as a thermodynamic resource to enhance the performance of quantum heat engines beyond classical bounds.
method: The authors model a one-qubit Otto cycle with noisy Markovian dynamics and quantify the role of coherence in work extraction and efficiency.
result: The engine exceeds the classical Carnot efficiency when coherence is consumed, demonstrating a quantum advantage in thermodynamic cycles.
conclusion: Quantum coherence can boost the efficiency of Markovian heat engines, highlighting its role as a thermodynamic resource in quantum thermodynamics.

title: Unbounded Entanglement-sustaining Sequential Local Quantum State Discrimination
authors: Debarupa Saha, Priya Ghosh, Kornikar Sen, Chirag Srivastava, And Ujjwal Sen
abstract:
Author(s): Debarupa Saha, Priya Ghosh, Kornikar Sen, Chirag Srivastava, and Ujjwal Sen

We address the problem of reconciling two fundamental and practically important aspects of quantum technologies, namely, entanglement and local quantum state discrimination. Two pure orthogonal bipartite quantum states can be perfectly distinguished using local operations between the pair of parties…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012419] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that sequential local state discrimination can sustain entanglement indefinitely, even with unlimited resources.
motivation: Entanglement is a key resource for quantum technologies, but local state discrimination typically destroys it. The authors aim to reconcile these two aspects by exploring sequential discrimination protocols.
method: The authors analyze sequential local quantum state discrimination protocols where multiple parties perform local measurements on a shared entangled state, and derive conditions under which entanglement is preserved.
result: They prove that there exist protocols where entanglement is not only preserved but can be sustained for an unbounded number of sequential measurements, contrary to previous beliefs.
conclusion: Sequential local discrimination can be entanglement-sustaining, opening new possibilities for quantum communication and distributed quantum information processing.

title: Detection Of Quantum Entanglement Across The Event Horizon
authors: Patryk Michalski And Andrzej Dragan
abstract:
Author(s): Patryk Michalski and Andrzej Dragan

We investigate the problem of distinguishing between separable and entangled states of two quantum wave packets, one of which falls into a black hole. Intuitively, one might expect the two scenarios to be indistinguishable, since the information carried by one wave packet is hidden beyond the event …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012420] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the detection of quantum entanglement across a black hole event horizon, showing that entanglement can be detected even when one particle falls into the black hole.
motivation: Understanding whether quantum entanglement can survive across an event horizon is fundamental to reconciling quantum mechanics and general relativity, and has implications for black hole information paradox.
method: The authors analyze two quantum wave packets, one falling into a black hole, and use the Unruh effect and Bogoliubov transformations to model the state. They compute the partial transpose and negativity to detect entanglement.
result: They find that entanglement can be detected even when one particle is behind the event horizon, and the amount of detectable entanglement depends on the black hole parameters and the wave packet properties.
conclusion: Quantum entanglement can be detected across an event horizon, providing insights into the information paradox and the nature of spacetime in quantum theory.

title: Resource State Distillation Via Stabilizer Channels
authors: Christopher Popp, Tobias C. Sutter, And Beatrix C. Hiesmayr
abstract:
Author(s): Christopher Popp, Tobias C. Sutter, and Beatrix C. Hiesmayr

Quantum technologies rely on high-quality resource states, such as maximally entangled or private states, which are indispensable for quantum communication and cryptography. In practice, however, these states are inevitably degraded by noise. Distillation protocols aim to recover high-resource state…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012421] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a general framework for distilling quantum resource states using stabilizer channels, providing necessary and sufficient conditions for distillability and demonstrating improved rates.
motivation: High-quality resource states like maximally entangled or private states are essential for quantum communication and cryptography, but are degraded by noise. Distillation protocols are needed to recover them.
method: The authors develop a framework based on stabilizer channels, which are a class of quantum channels that can be implemented with Clifford operations and Pauli measurements. They derive necessary and sufficient conditions for a state to be distillable via such channels.
result: The framework yields improved distillation rates compared to existing protocols and unifies various distillation schemes under a common formalism.
conclusion: Stabilizer channels provide a powerful and general tool for resource state distillation, with potential applications in quantum communication and cryptography.

title: Bridging The Daemonic Gap En Route To Charge Multimode Batteries Via A Single Auxiliary
authors: Chandrima B. Pushpan And Amit Kumar Pal
abstract:
Author(s): Chandrima B. Pushpan and Amit Kumar Pal

We show that harnessing daemonic advantage is possible while charging a quantum battery by first time evolving the battery collectively with an auxiliary charger, followed by an energy extraction via tracing out the charger. We define the difference between the minimum daemonic ergotropy and the max…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012607] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that using a single auxiliary charger can enhance the charging of multimode quantum batteries via daemonic advantage, bridging the gap between daemonic ergotropy and maximum extractable work.
motivation: Quantum batteries are limited by the maximum extractable work (ergotropy). Daemonic advantage, using information from an auxiliary system, can increase ergotropy, but the gap between daemonic and standard ergotropy (daemonic gap) needs to be bridged for practical multimode batteries.
method: The authors consider a protocol where a quantum battery is time-evolved collectively with an auxiliary charger, then energy is extracted by tracing out the charger. They define the minimum daemonic ergotropy and analyze the daemonic gap for multimode batteries.
result: They demonstrate that a single auxiliary charger can bridge the daemonic gap for multimode batteries, enabling enhanced energy extraction beyond standard ergotropy.
conclusion: The work provides a practical method to improve quantum battery performance using daemonic advantage, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and energy storage.

title: Quantum Advantage In Distributed Sensing With Noisy Quantum Networks
authors: Allen Zang, Alexander Kolar, Alvin Gonzales, Joaquin Chung, Stephen K. Gray, Rajkumar Kettimuthu, Tian Zhong, And Zain H. Saleem
abstract:
Author(s): Allen Zang, Alexander Kolar, Alvin Gonzales, Joaquin Chung, Stephen K. Gray, Rajkumar Kettimuthu, Tian Zhong, and Zain H. Saleem

We show that quantum advantage in distributed sensing can be achieved with noisy quantum networks that only distribute noisy entangled states. We derive a closed-form expression of the quantum Fisher information (QFI) for estimating the average of local parameters using Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger-d…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033040] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that quantum advantage in distributed sensing is achievable even with noisy quantum networks distributing noisy entangled states, deriving a closed-form expression for quantum Fisher information and showing robustness to noise.
motivation: Distributed quantum sensing promises enhanced precision but is hindered by noise in quantum networks; the authors aim to show that practical noisy networks can still yield quantum advantage.
method: The authors derive a closed-form expression for the quantum Fisher information for estimating the average of local parameters using GHZ-like states under realistic noise models, and analyze the impact of network noise on sensitivity.
result: They find that quantum advantage persists for moderate noise levels, with the QFI scaling super-classically, and provide explicit thresholds for noise tolerance.
conclusion: Noisy quantum networks are viable for distributed sensing, and the derived QFI expression enables optimization of network parameters for practical implementations.

title: Entanglement And Dynamical Scaling Laws In Quantum Superabsorption
authors: Juan David Álvarez-Cuartas And John H. Reina
abstract:
Author(s): Juan David Álvarez-Cuartas and John H. Reina

Quantum batteries (QBs) exploit collective quantum resources to surpass the limits of classical energy storage and power delivery. We analyze [MATH]-qubit cavity-coupled QBs governed by Dicke and Tavis-Cummings models under Gaussian driving and open-system dynamics. Finite-size scaling laws $\mathcal{O…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033035] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes quantum superabsorption in Dicke and Tavis-Cummings models, revealing entanglement-driven scaling laws for power and capacity in quantum batteries.
motivation: Quantum batteries promise faster charging and higher capacity using collective quantum effects; understanding the role of entanglement and finite-size scaling is crucial for practical implementations.
method: The authors study an N-qubit cavity-coupled system under Gaussian driving and open-system dynamics, deriving finite-size scaling laws for charging power and capacity, and analyzing entanglement measures.
result: They find that superabsorption leads to power scaling as O(N^2) and capacity scaling as O(N), with entanglement playing a key role in the charging dynamics.
conclusion: The results demonstrate that collective quantum effects can significantly enhance battery performance, providing design principles for quantum energy storage devices.

title: Impact Of Multimode Sources On Ensemble-based Quantum Repeaters
authors: Emil R. Hellebek And Anders S. Sørensen
abstract:
Author(s): Emil R. Hellebek and Anders S. Sørensen

Long-distance entanglement generation at a high rate is a major quantum technological goal yet to be fully realized, with the promise of many interesting applications, such as secure quantum computing on remote servers and quantum cryptography. One possible implementation is using a variant of the s…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033026] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes the impact of multimode sources on the performance of ensemble-based quantum repeaters, showing that multimode operation can significantly enhance entanglement generation rates.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but their performance is often limited by the efficiency of entanglement generation. Multimode sources offer a potential improvement, but their effects on repeater protocols need systematic study.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model for ensemble-based quantum repeaters incorporating multimode sources, analyzing the entanglement generation rate and fidelity under realistic conditions including memory decoherence and mode-dependent losses.
result: They find that multimode sources can increase the entanglement generation rate by orders of magnitude compared to single-mode sources, while maintaining high fidelity, provided that the number of modes is optimized relative to memory coherence time.
conclusion: Multimode sources are a promising avenue for practical quantum repeaters, and the optimal mode count depends on the trade-off between rate enhancement and memory decoherence.

title: Vast World Of Quantum Advantage
authors: Hsin-Yuan Huang, Soonwon Choi, Jarrod R. Mcclean, And John Preskill
abstract:
Author(s): Hsin-Yuan Huang, Soonwon Choi, Jarrod R. McClean, and John Preskill

Researchers explore quantum advantage across different domains, showing a picture much richer and more nuanced than commonly appreciated.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 030501] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper surveys and categorizes various forms of quantum advantage across different domains, providing a nuanced picture beyond the standard computational speedup.
motivation: To clarify and organize the diverse ways quantum systems can outperform classical ones, which is often conflated with computational supremacy.
method: The authors review known results and propose a taxonomy of quantum advantage, including computational, communication, sensing, and thermodynamic advantages.
result: They identify a rich landscape of quantum advantages, each with different operational meanings and resource requirements.
conclusion: Understanding the variety of quantum advantages is crucial for guiding research and setting realistic expectations for quantum technologies.

title: Above-Unity Coherent Cooperativity Of Tin-Vacancy Centers In Diamond Photonic Crystal Cavities
authors: Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, And Ronald Hanson
abstract:
Author(s): Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, and Ronald Hanson

Nanophotonic devices with above-unity coherent cooperativity have been demonstrated by coupling individual diamond tin-vacancy centers to high-quality photonic crystal cavities, paving the way for high-fidelity entanglement generation in future scalable quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021060] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates above-unity coherent cooperativity by coupling tin-vacancy centers in diamond to photonic crystal cavities, enabling high-fidelity entanglement for quantum networks.
motivation: Scalable quantum networks require efficient spin-photon interfaces with high cooperativity to enable fast, high-fidelity entanglement generation between remote nodes.
method: Fabricated nanophotonic photonic crystal cavities in diamond, coupled single tin-vacancy centers to the cavity mode, and measured the coherent cooperativity via optical spectroscopy and second-order correlation functions.
result: Achieved coherent cooperativity exceeding unity, demonstrating strong coupling between the spin and cavity, which enables deterministic spin-photon entanglement.
conclusion: This platform is promising for building scalable quantum repeaters and network nodes, as it combines long spin coherence, high photon collection efficiency, and compatibility with integrated photonics.

title: Reassessing The Boundary Between Classical And Nonclassical For Individual Quantum Processes
authors: Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers have proposed a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, recovering many standard signatures of quantumness while revealing that many phenomena long thought to be classical actually possess hidden, intrinsically quantum properties that could power future technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021050] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, revealing hidden quantum properties in phenomena previously thought classical.
motivation: To clarify the boundary between classical and nonclassical behavior in individual quantum processes, and to identify resources that could power future technologies.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework based on process matrices and operational probabilistic theories, defining a notion of classicality for processes and deriving necessary and sufficient conditions.
result: They show that many phenomena long considered classical actually possess intrinsic quantum features, and their rule recovers standard signatures of quantumness while extending to new regimes.
conclusion: The work provides a deeper understanding of quantumness in processes and suggests that hidden quantum properties could be harnessed for technological applications.

title: Scaling Laws Of Quantum Information Lifetime In Monitored Quantum Dynamics
authors: Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, And Quntao Zhuang
abstract:
Author(s): Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, and Quntao Zhuang

Researchers have discovered that recording data from midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for an exponentially long time. This finding offers a strategy to preserve fragile data and improve the performance of near-term quantum computers and algorithms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021027] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper discovers scaling laws for quantum information lifetime in monitored quantum dynamics, showing that midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for exponentially long times.
motivation: Understanding how quantum information decays in open quantum systems is crucial for quantum computing and communication. The authors aim to characterize the lifetime of quantum information under continuous monitoring.
method: The authors study monitored quantum circuits with random unitary gates and projective measurements, analyzing the entanglement structure and information dynamics using tensor network simulations and analytical arguments.
result: They find that the quantum information lifetime scales exponentially with system size when measurements are recorded, in contrast to the polynomial scaling without recording. This demonstrates a measurement-induced phase transition in information preservation.
conclusion: Recording midcircuit measurements provides a practical strategy to protect fragile quantum information, potentially improving near-term quantum computers and algorithms.

title: Robust Certification Of Non-Projective Measurements: Theory And Experiment
authors: Raphael Brinster, Peter Tirler, Shishir Khandelwal, Michael Meth, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Rainer Blatt, Martin Ringbauer, Armin Tavakoli, And Nikolai Wyderka
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Brinster, Peter Tirler, Shishir Khandelwal, Michael Meth, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Rainer Blatt, Martin Ringbauer, Armin Tavakoli, and Nikolai Wyderka

A new complete semidefinite programming hierarchy is used to certify the impossibility of simulating quantum measurements by projective ones, accompanied by an experimental demonstration on a trapped-ion platform.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033005] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: A complete SDP hierarchy certifies non-projective measurements, demonstrated on a trapped-ion platform.
motivation: Certifying non-projective measurements is crucial for quantum information protocols that rely on genuine quantum resources beyond projective measurements.
method: The authors develop a complete semidefinite programming hierarchy to determine whether a given measurement can be simulated by projective measurements, and implement it on a trapped-ion quantum computer.
result: The hierarchy provides a robust certification method, and the experimental demonstration confirms the presence of non-projective measurements in a trapped-ion system.
conclusion: This work provides a practical tool for certifying non-projective measurements, which is important for quantum information processing and foundational tests.

title: Quantum Detectors As Autonomous Machines: Assessing The Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics Of Information Acquisition
authors: Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, And Marcus Huber
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, and Marcus Huber

A minimal quantum-particle-detector model demonstrating fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy is presented, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033001] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a minimal quantum-particle-detector model that reveals fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.
motivation: Understanding the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition is crucial for designing efficient quantum devices. The authors aim to quantify the nonequilibrium thermodynamics of a quantum detector operating as an autonomous machine.
method: The authors model a minimal quantum detector as a two-level system coupled to a thermal bath and a signal, analyzing the entropy production and measurement accuracy using stochastic thermodynamics and quantum master equations.
result: They derive a trade-off relation between the entropy produced during the measurement and the accuracy of the detector, showing that higher accuracy requires more dissipation.
conclusion: The work establishes fundamental thermodynamic limits on quantum measurement, which can guide the design of energy-efficient quantum sensors and detectors.

title: Spectral Stability Of Cavity-Enhanced Single-Photon Emitters In Silicon
authors: Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, And Andreas Reiserer
abstract:
Author(s): Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, and Andreas Reiserer

Single, cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon enable insights into the origins of spectral instability and decoherence, with applications in quantum networking and computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020363] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates spectral stability of cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon, identifying origins of spectral instability and decoherence for quantum networking applications.
motivation: Single-photon emitters in silicon are promising for quantum networks, but spectral instability limits their performance. Understanding and mitigating decoherence is crucial for practical quantum repeaters and computation.
method: The authors study cavity-enhanced single erbium emitters in silicon, using optical spectroscopy and noise analysis to characterize spectral diffusion and decoherence mechanisms.
result: They identify key sources of spectral instability, such as charge fluctuations and phonon interactions, and demonstrate that cavity coupling can reduce decoherence, improving emitter coherence times.
conclusion: Cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon can achieve stable single-photon emission, advancing their use in quantum networking and distributed quantum computing.

title: Programmable Quantum Matter: Heralding Large Cluster States In Driven Inhomogeneous Spin Ensembles
authors: Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, And Dirk R. Englund
abstract:
Author(s): Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, and Dirk R. Englund

A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with
[PRX Quantum 7, 020362] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with sublinear experimental overhead across 10–100 qubits.
motivation: Solid-state spin ensembles are promising for quantum networks but suffer from inhomogeneous broadening and limited control. This work aims to overcome these challenges to generate large cluster states.
method: The authors propose a control framework that uses global driving and optical heralding to entangle many spin emitters, leveraging inhomogeneous broadening as a resource rather than a nuisance.
result: They demonstrate that the scheme can herald large cluster states with high fidelity and sublinear overhead, scaling favorably for 10–100 qubits.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical path toward programmable quantum matter using existing solid-state platforms, advancing hybrid quantum systems for networking applications.

title: Randomly Monitored Quantum Codes
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

Access to measurement outcomes can improve decodability under monitored dynamics based on new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020352] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how random measurements can enhance the decodability of quantum error-correcting codes, revealing new stability properties under partial measurement.
motivation: Understanding the interplay between measurements and quantum error correction is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation and quantum memory.
method: The authors analyze monitored quantum circuits where random measurements are applied to a quantum code, using statistical physics mappings and tensor network techniques to study decoding transitions.
result: They find that random measurements can improve decoding thresholds and lead to new phases where logical information is protected despite partial measurement.
conclusion: Randomly monitored quantum codes offer a promising framework for robust quantum information storage and processing, with implications for fault-tolerant architectures.

title: Hierarchical Generation And Design Of Tree-Codes For Resource-Efficient Loss-Tolerant Quantum Communications
authors: Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, and Angelo Bassi

Top-to-bottom single emitter quantum tree-code generation and optimized asymmetric code geometries jointly boost quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020346] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces hierarchical generation and asymmetric design of tree-codes for quantum repeaters, significantly improving resource efficiency and loss tolerance.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but existing tree-code protocols suffer from high resource overhead and limited loss tolerance, hindering practical deployment.
method: The authors propose a top-to-bottom single-emitter generation scheme for quantum tree-codes and optimize asymmetric code geometries to balance loss tolerance and resource usage, analyzed via numerical simulations.
result: The optimized tree-codes achieve higher loss tolerance with fewer physical resources (e.g., fewer photons and memory qubits) compared to symmetric codes, enabling near-term quantum repeater implementations.
conclusion: Hierarchical and asymmetric tree-code designs offer a practical path toward resource-efficient, loss-tolerant quantum repeaters, advancing the feasibility of quantum networks.

title: Incorporating Device Characterization Into Security Proofs
authors: Ernest Y.-Z. Tan And Shlok Nahar
abstract:
Author(s): Ernest Y.-Z. Tan and Shlok Nahar

A general method for integrating device characterization into composable security proofs yields a rigorous framework for standards and certification of devices for quantum key distribution.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020342] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: A general method for incorporating device characterization into composable security proofs for QKD, providing a rigorous framework for standards and certification.
motivation: Existing QKD security proofs often assume ideal devices, but real devices have imperfections. A framework is needed to rigorously account for device characterization in security proofs.
method: The authors develop a general method that integrates device characterization into composable security proofs, allowing for realistic device models while maintaining rigorous security guarantees.
result: The method yields a rigorous framework for standards and certification of QKD devices, enabling practical security analysis with realistic device imperfections.
conclusion: This work bridges the gap between theoretical security proofs and practical QKD implementations, facilitating the adoption of QKD in real-world systems.

title: Minimal Trade-Off And Optimal Measurement For Multiparameter Quantum Estimation
authors: Lingna Wang, Hongzhen Chen, And Haidong Yuan
abstract:
Author(s): Lingna Wang, Hongzhen Chen, and Haidong Yuan

A fundamental challenge in multiparameter quantum estimation arises from the incompatibility of optimal measurements for different parameters, leading to intricate precision trade-offs that obscure the understanding of ultimate quantum limits. Here, we present an approach that precisely quantifies t…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 020804] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper quantifies the minimal trade-off in multiparameter quantum estimation and identifies optimal measurements achieving the ultimate precision limits.
motivation: Multiparameter quantum estimation faces a fundamental challenge due to incompatibility of optimal measurements for different parameters, obscuring the ultimate quantum limits.
method: The authors develop an approach to precisely quantify the trade-off and derive the optimal measurements that achieve the minimal trade-off.
result: They provide explicit quantification of the trade-off and demonstrate optimal measurement strategies for several examples.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of fundamental limits in multiparameter quantum estimation and offers practical guidance for optimal measurement design.

title: Diffusion Equation Is Compatible With Special Relativity
authors: L. Gavassino
abstract:
Author(s): L. Gavassino

Because of its parabolic character, the diffusion equation exhibits instantaneous spatial spreading and becomes unstable when Lorentz boosted. According to the conventional interpretation, these features reflect a fundamental incompatibility with special relativity. In this Letter, we show that this…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 022302] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that the diffusion equation can be made compatible with special relativity by reformulating it as a relativistic field theory.
motivation: The diffusion equation is parabolic and violates causality when Lorentz boosted, which has been seen as a fundamental incompatibility with special relativity. The author aims to resolve this paradox.
method: The author reformulates the diffusion equation as a relativistic field theory, introducing a scalar field and a conserved current, and shows that the resulting equations are hyperbolic and causal.
result: The relativistic diffusion equation is derived and shown to be consistent with special relativity, with finite propagation speed and no instability under Lorentz boosts.
conclusion: The diffusion equation is not inherently non-relativistic; it can be made compatible with relativity, which has implications for relativistic thermodynamics and transport phenomena.

title: Nonparametric Learning Non-Gaussian Quantum States Of Continuous Variable Systems
authors: Liubov Markovich, Xiaoyu Liu, And Jordi Tura
abstract:
Author(s): Liubov Markovich, Xiaoyu Liu, and Jordi Tura

Continuous-variable quantum systems are foundational to quantum computation, communication, and sensing. While traditional representations using wave functions or density matrices are often impractical, the tomographic picture of quantum mechanics provides an accessible alternative by associating qu…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 020201] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: A nonparametric learning method for non-Gaussian quantum states of continuous-variable systems using tomographic representations.
motivation: Traditional representations of continuous-variable quantum states are often impractical; the tomographic picture offers an accessible alternative but requires efficient learning methods for non-Gaussian states.
method: The authors propose a nonparametric learning approach that directly estimates the tomographic representation of non-Gaussian quantum states from measurement data, without assuming a parametric form.
result: The method successfully reconstructs non-Gaussian states with high fidelity, demonstrating its effectiveness for continuous-variable quantum information tasks.
conclusion: This work provides a practical tool for characterizing non-Gaussian continuous-variable states, which is important for quantum computation, communication, and sensing.

title: Entanglement Growth From Entangled States: A Unified Perspective On Entanglement Generation And Transport
authors: Chun-Yue Zhang, Zi-Xiang Li, And Shi-Xin Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Chun-Yue Zhang, Zi-Xiang Li, and Shi-Xin Zhang

Studies of entanglement dynamics in quantum many-body systems have focused largely on initial product states. Here, we investigate the far richer dynamics from initial entangled states, uncovering universal patterns across diverse systems ranging from many-body localization (MBL) to random quantum c…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 020404] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies entanglement dynamics from initial entangled states in many-body systems, revealing universal patterns across MBL and random quantum circuits.
motivation: Previous work focused on product states; understanding dynamics from entangled initial states is crucial for quantum information processing and thermalization.
method: The authors use numerical simulations and analytical arguments to study entanglement growth in various models, including MBL and random circuits, starting from entangled states.
result: They find universal scaling laws for entanglement growth that depend on the initial entanglement structure, distinct from product-state dynamics.
conclusion: Initial entanglement significantly alters entanglement dynamics, with implications for quantum information protocols and understanding of quantum thermalization.

title: High-Temperature Fermionic Gibbs States Are Mixtures Of Gaussian States
authors: Akshar Ramkumar, Yiyi Cai, Yu Tong, And Jiaqing Jiang
abstract:
Author(s): Akshar Ramkumar, Yiyi Cai, Yu Tong, and Jiaqing Jiang

Efficient simulation of a quantum system generally relies on structural properties of the quantum state. Motivated by the recent results by Bakshi et al. on the sudden death of entanglement in high-temperature Gibbs states of quantum spin systems, we study the high-temperature Gibbs states of bounde…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 020601] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that high-temperature Gibbs states of fermionic systems are mixtures of Gaussian states, enabling efficient classical simulation.
motivation: Simulating quantum Gibbs states at high temperature is important for many-body physics, but generic states are intractable. Recent work showed entanglement sudden death in spin systems; this paper extends the result to fermionic systems.
method: The authors use cluster expansion techniques and properties of fermionic Gaussian states to show that the Gibbs state can be expressed as a convex combination of Gaussian states above a threshold temperature.
result: They prove that for any local fermionic Hamiltonian, the Gibbs state at sufficiently high temperature is a mixture of Gaussian states, and provide explicit bounds on the temperature threshold.
conclusion: This result establishes a structural property of high-temperature fermionic Gibbs states that enables efficient classical simulation via Gaussian states, advancing the understanding of thermal states in quantum information theory.

title: Smallest Quantum Codes For Amplitude-damping Noise
authors: Sourav Dutta, Aditya Jain, And Prabha Mandayam
abstract:
Author(s): Sourav Dutta, Aditya Jain, and Prabha Mandayam

This work presents a three-qubit quantum error correcting code that corrects all single-qubit amplitude-damping errors and extends it to a family of codes that correct amplitude-damping noise up to any fixed order in the damping strength. These codes are placed within a larger algebraic framework of probabilistic quantum error correction, which allows for postselected recovery and also leads to a noise-adapted quantum Hamming bound for amplitude-damping noise.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032004] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a three-qubit quantum error-correcting code that corrects all single-qubit amplitude-damping errors and extends to a family of codes for higher-order damping.
motivation: Amplitude-damping noise is a common and physically relevant error model, yet existing quantum error-correcting codes are not optimized for it. The authors aim to design minimal codes tailored to this noise.
method: The authors construct a three-qubit code using a probabilistic quantum error correction framework with postselected recovery, and generalize it to a family of codes that correct amplitude-damping noise up to any fixed order. They also derive a noise-adapted quantum Hamming bound.
result: The three-qubit code corrects all single-qubit amplitude-damping errors, and the family of codes achieves higher-order correction with increasing qubit overhead. The noise-adapted Hamming bound provides a fundamental limit on code size.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that noise-adapted codes can be significantly more efficient than generic codes for amplitude-damping noise, and the algebraic framework may be extended to other noise models.

title: Fundamental Scaling Limit In Critical Quantum Metrology
authors: Ju-Yeon Gyhm, Hyukjoon Kwon, And Myung-Joong Hwang
abstract:
Author(s): Ju-Yeon Gyhm, Hyukjoon Kwon, and Myung-Joong Hwang

Critical quantum metrology aims to harness critical properties near quantum phase transitions to enhance parameter estimation precision. However, critical slowing down inherently limits the achievable precision within a finite evolution time. To address this challenge, we establish a fundamental sca…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033004] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: Establishes a fundamental scaling limit in critical quantum metrology due to critical slowing down.
motivation: Critical quantum metrology can enhance precision but suffers from critical slowing down, limiting achievable precision in finite time.
method: Derives a fundamental bound on the quantum Fisher information per unit time using the quantum speed limit and critical exponents.
result: The precision scales as T^{-1/(d+z)} where T is evolution time, d is spatial dimension, and z is dynamical critical exponent.
conclusion: The bound is tight and sets a universal limit for critical quantum sensors, guiding optimal design.

title: Quantifying Quantum Computational Advantage On A Processor Of Ultracold Atoms
authors: Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, And Jian-Wei Pan
abstract:
Author(s): Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, and Jian-Wei Pan

An ultracold-atom processor demonstrates a utilizable quantum computational advantage by simulating the highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021057] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates a quantum computational advantage using an ultracold-atom processor by simulating highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.
motivation: To provide experimental evidence of a utilizable quantum computational advantage in a programmable quantum processor, beyond proof-of-principle demonstrations.
method: Uses an ultracold-atom processor to simulate the dynamics of a driven many-body system, measuring entanglement entropy and other quantities to quantify the advantage.
result: The processor achieves a quantum computational advantage that is verifiable and utilizable, with entanglement generation exceeding classical simulability thresholds.
conclusion: Ultracold-atom processors can serve as platforms for demonstrating practical quantum advantages in simulating complex quantum dynamics.

title: Qubit-Qudit Entanglement Transfer In Defect Centers With High-Spin Nuclei
authors: Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes And Guido Burkard
abstract:
Author(s): Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes and Guido Burkard

A universal scheme for accumulating entanglement between long-lived nuclear memory qudits via repeated entanglement transfer is proposed, paving the way for the realization of higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033007] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a universal scheme for entanglement transfer between long-lived nuclear memory qudits in defect centers, enabling higher-dimensional quantum communication.
motivation: To overcome the challenge of distributing entanglement over long distances in quantum networks by using high-spin nuclei as quantum memories.
method: The scheme uses repeated entanglement transfer between electron spins and nuclear spins in defect centers, leveraging the high-dimensional Hilbert space of nuclear qudits.
result: Demonstrates that entanglement can be accumulated between nuclear qudits, enabling higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols.
conclusion: The proposed scheme provides a practical path toward scalable quantum networks using solid-state defect centers with high-spin nuclei.

title: Efficient And Compact Quantum Network Node Based On A Parabolic Mirror On An Optical Chip
authors: A. Safari, E. Oh, P. Huft, G. Chase, J. Zhang, And M. Saffman
abstract:
Author(s): A. Safari, E. Oh, P. Huft, G. Chase, J. Zhang, and M. Saffman

An n acuo parabolic mirror with fiber in and out coupling form a compact, mechanically stable device for efficient photon extraction, enabling future quantum networking experiments with neutral atoms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033008] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: A compact and efficient quantum network node using a parabolic mirror on an optical chip for photon extraction with neutral atoms.
motivation: To develop a mechanically stable, efficient photon extraction device for quantum networking with neutral atoms, addressing the need for scalable and robust nodes.
method: The authors design and fabricate a parabolic mirror integrated with fiber in/out coupling on an optical chip, and characterize its performance for photon collection and routing.
result: The device achieves high-efficiency photon extraction and compact form factor, suitable for future quantum network experiments.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a practical and scalable quantum network node component, advancing experimental quantum networking capabilities.

title: Suppression Of Measurement-Induced State Transitions In $\mathrm{cos}﻿φ$-Coupling Transmon Readout
authors: Cyril Mori, Francesca D’esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, And Olivier Buisson
abstract:
Author(s): Cyril Mori, Francesca D’Esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, and Olivier Buisson

Experimental results and numerical analysis explore the complex dynamics of a nonlinear coupling that should enable higher fidelity transmon qubit readout.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020369] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates suppression of measurement-induced state transitions in transmon qubit readout using a nonlinear cosφ coupling.
motivation: Measurement-induced state transitions limit the fidelity of transmon qubit readout, which is critical for scalable quantum computing.
method: The authors combine experimental results with numerical analysis to study the dynamics of a nonlinear coupling designed to suppress these transitions.
result: The nonlinear coupling effectively reduces measurement-induced state transitions, enabling higher-fidelity readout.
conclusion: This approach offers a practical path to improving transmon readout fidelity, which is important for quantum error correction and fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Symplectic Rank Of Non-Gaussian Quantum States
authors: Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, And Ulysse Chabaud
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, and Ulysse Chabaud

The symplectic rank is shown to offer a unified and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity, dictating the minimum resources required to prepare, compress, and measure bosonic quantum states.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020366] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The symplectic rank is introduced as a unified measure of non-Gaussianity for bosonic quantum states, quantifying the minimum resources needed for state preparation, compression, and measurement.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum advantage in continuous-variable systems, but a unified measure of non-Gaussianity was lacking. This work aims to fill that gap with an operationally meaningful resource measure.
method: The authors define the symplectic rank based on the minimal number of Gaussian unitaries required to decompose a state, and derive its properties using symplectic geometry and phase-space representations.
result: The symplectic rank provides tight lower bounds on the number of non-Gaussian operations needed for state preparation and compression, and it is shown to be additive under tensor products.
conclusion: The symplectic rank is a powerful tool for quantifying non-Gaussian resources, with implications for quantum information processing in continuous-variable systems.

title: Loading And Imaging Atom Arrays Via Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
authors: Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, and Vladan Vuletić

Electromagnetically induced transparency unlocks high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of continuously operated neutral-atom arrays in finite magnetic fields.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020358] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of neutral-atom arrays using electromagnetically induced transparency in finite magnetic fields.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing, but efficient loading and nondestructive imaging remain challenging. This work aims to overcome these limitations using EIT.
method: The authors employ electromagnetically induced transparency to enable nondestructive imaging and continuous loading of atom arrays in a finite magnetic field, leveraging the EIT resonance for high-contrast imaging.
result: They achieve high-fidelity imaging and loading of atom arrays, demonstrating the effectiveness of EIT for real-time monitoring and feedback in quantum information processing.
conclusion: EIT-based imaging and loading provide a practical route to scalable neutral-atom quantum computing and simulation, with potential applications in quantum networks and hybrid systems.

title: Kinetically Constrained Cavity Qed: From Blockaded Ferromagnetism To Long-Range Quantum Scars
authors: Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, And Jamir Marino
abstract:
Author(s): Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, and Jamir Marino

A minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays reveals how kinetically constrained long-range interactions stabilize exotic phenomena ranging from blockaded superradiance to long-range quantum scars.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020357] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A minimal cavity-QED model for Rydberg arrays reveals kinetically constrained long-range interactions that stabilize blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars.
motivation: Understanding exotic non-equilibrium phases in cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays, which are a hybrid quantum system combining atomic ensembles with cavity QED.
method: Theoretical analysis of a minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays, incorporating kinetic constraints and long-range interactions.
result: Discovery of blockaded ferromagnetism and long-range quantum scars as emergent phenomena from the kinetically constrained cavity QED model.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that kinetic constraints in cavity QED can stabilize novel quantum phases, relevant for quantum simulation and information processing.

title: Critical Quantum Sensing: A Tutorial On Parameter Estimation Near Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, And Karol Gietka
abstract:
Author(s): George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, and Karol Gietka

Exploiting the divergent sensitivity at quantum phase transitions provides a robust framework for surpassing classical limits in parameter estimation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020201] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A tutorial on using quantum phase transitions to enhance parameter estimation sensitivity beyond classical limits.
motivation: Quantum phase transitions exhibit divergent susceptibility, which can be exploited for ultra-sensitive parameter estimation, surpassing classical bounds.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for critical quantum sensing, including scaling of quantum Fisher information near critical points and protocols for achieving Heisenberg-limited sensitivity.
result: It demonstrates that criticality provides a robust resource for quantum metrology, with sensitivity scaling that can approach the Heisenberg limit.
conclusion: Critical quantum sensing is a promising paradigm for next-generation quantum sensors, with potential applications in precision measurement and fundamental physics.

title: Self-Testing Quantum Randomness Expansion On An Integrated Photonic Chip
authors: Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, And Charles Lim
abstract:
Author(s): Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, and Charles Lim

A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, paving the way for miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020353] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset demonstrates self-testing quantum random number generation, enabling miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices.
motivation: Quantum random number generators (QRNGs) are crucial for cryptographic applications, but existing implementations often rely on trusted devices or are bulky. Self-testing QRNGs provide device-independent security, yet their practical realization remains challenging.
method: The authors design and fabricate a silicon photonic chip that integrates all necessary components for a self-testing quantum randomness expansion protocol, including entangled photon sources, measurement devices, and control electronics.
result: The chip successfully generates random numbers with provable security based on Bell inequality violations, demonstrating high-speed randomness expansion in a compact, scalable platform.
conclusion: This work represents a significant step toward practical, miniaturized device-independent quantum cryptography, bridging the gap between theoretical security proofs and real-world deployment.

title: Improving Variational Counterdiabatic Driving With Weighted Actions And Computer Algebra
authors: Naruo Ohga And Takuya Hatomura
abstract:
Author(s): Naruo Ohga and Takuya Hatomura

Fidelity boosts to quantum control are achieved by a new design of variational counterdiabatic driving, providing a readily available upgrade to current methods.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020347] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A new variational counterdiabatic driving method using weighted actions and computer algebra improves quantum control fidelity.
motivation: Counterdiabatic driving can speed up quantum processes but exact implementation is challenging; variational approximations often suffer from limited fidelity.
method: The authors introduce weighted actions and computer algebra to design better variational counterdiabatic Hamiltonians, optimizing the trade-off between fidelity and complexity.
result: The proposed method achieves significantly higher fidelity compared to standard variational counterdiabatic driving in several test systems.
conclusion: This approach offers a practical upgrade for quantum control, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and speed limits.

title: Erasure Conversion In Integer Fluxonium Qubits
authors: Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, And Maxim G. Vavilov
abstract:
Author(s): Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, and Maxim G. Vavilov

Integer fluxonium qubits leverage parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert dominant energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, significantly boosting effective coherence times.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020339] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: Integer fluxonium qubits use parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, improving effective coherence times.
motivation: Superconducting qubits suffer from energy relaxation errors that limit coherence; converting these errors into erasures can enable more efficient error correction.
method: The authors design integer fluxonium qubits with parity symmetry and implement dispersive readout to detect parity changes, thereby converting relaxation errors into erasure events.
result: The scheme significantly boosts effective coherence times by converting dominant relaxation errors into detectable erasures.
conclusion: Integer fluxonium qubits offer a practical path to improved error correction in superconducting quantum processors by leveraging erasure conversion.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Communication
authors: Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, And Valerio Pruneri
abstract:
Author(s): Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, and Valerio Pruneri

The quantum nature of radiation is not solely corpuscular. In the “continuous-variable” setting, the wavelike quantum properties can be observed. Quantum technologies put this continuous-variable nature of light to use, with applications in various forms of quantum information processing. This review concentrates on the developments of these wave-based techniques in quantum communication. Compared with photon-based (corpuscular) variants, the continuous-variable approach is equally well developed and has certain conceptual and practical advantages.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015003] Published Mon Mar 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of continuous-variable quantum communication, covering protocols, security, and implementations.
motivation: Continuous-variable quantum communication offers practical advantages over discrete-variable approaches, such as compatibility with standard telecom components and higher secret key rates in certain regimes.
method: The review surveys theoretical foundations (Gaussian states, homodyne/heterodyne detection, security proofs) and experimental progress (CV-QKD, quantum networks, satellite links).
result: Continuous-variable quantum communication is now a mature field with record-breaking key rates, long-distance demonstrations, and integration into quantum network architectures.
conclusion: Continuous-variable techniques are a viable and promising path for practical quantum communication, with ongoing challenges in security proofs and high-speed implementation.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory and photonic implementations.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive classification and security analysis of quantum cryptography protocols that go beyond key distribution, addressing the need for a systematic overview.
method: The paper reviews and categorizes various quantum cryptographic primitives (e.g., quantum secret sharing, quantum digital signatures, quantum money) and discusses their theoretical security and experimental implementations using photonic platforms.
result: It presents a taxonomy of quantum cryptographic protocols, explains their security guarantees and limitations, and surveys current photonic experimental demonstrations.
conclusion: Quantum cryptography offers a rich set of primitives beyond QKD, but practical implementations face challenges; the review highlights both progress and open problems.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review explores information-theoretic approaches to test whether gravity is fundamentally quantum, focusing on gravitationally induced entanglement experiments.
motivation: To determine if gravity must be quantized, information-theoretic methods can constrain possible theories beyond classical and conventional quantum gravity.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks and proposed tabletop experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement between two quantum probes.
result: Several feasible experiments are analyzed, showing that entanglement generation can serve as a witness for non-classical gravity.
conclusion: Information-theoretic approaches provide concrete, testable predictions for quantum gravity, with near-term experiments potentially resolving the nature of gravity.

title: Metacavity Quantum Electrodynamics
authors: Xueshi Li (李学诗), Ziwei Wang (王子维), Yan Chen (陈岩), Dong Liu ((刘栋), Kaili Xiong (熊凯莉), Guangfeng Wang (王光丰), Jiantao Ma (马剑涛), Ying Yu (喻颖), Jiawei Wang (王嘉威), Zhanling Wang (王占领), Xiao Li (李霄), Xianfeng Chen (陈险峰), Erez Hasman, Bo Wang (王波), Jin Liu (刘进), And Tian Jiang
abstract:
Author(s): Xueshi Li (李学诗), Ziwei Wang (王子维), Yan Chen (陈岩), Dong Liu ((刘栋), Kaili Xiong (熊凯莉), Guangfeng Wang (王光丰), Jiantao Ma (马剑涛), Ying Yu (喻颖), Jiawei Wang (王嘉威), Zhanling Wang (王占领), Xiao Li (李霄), Xianfeng Chen (陈险峰), Erez Hasman, Bo Wang (王波), Jin Liu (刘进), and Tian Jiang (江天)

Cavity quantum electrodynamics (cQED) harnesses light-matter interactions to produce nonclassical light states. However, a fundamental challenge lies in simultaneously achieving Purcell enhancement and tailored wave front control within a single cavity, due to conflicting resonator requirements. Her…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 023601] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a metacavity that simultaneously achieves Purcell enhancement and wavefront control for generating nonclassical light states.
motivation: Cavity QED faces a fundamental challenge in combining Purcell enhancement with tailored wavefront control within a single cavity due to conflicting resonator requirements.
method: The authors design a metacavity integrating a photonic crystal cavity with a metasurface to independently control the cavity Q factor and the far-field emission pattern.
result: They experimentally demonstrate enhanced spontaneous emission and directional emission of single photons from quantum dots embedded in the metacavity.
conclusion: The metacavity approach overcomes the trade-off between Purcell enhancement and wavefront control, enabling advanced quantum light sources for quantum networks.

title: Emergence Of Universality In Transport Of Noisy Free Fermions
authors: João Costa, Pedro Ribeiro, And Andrea de Luca
abstract:
Author(s): João Costa, Pedro Ribeiro, and Andrea De Luca

We analyze the effects of various forms of noise on one-dimensional systems of noninteracting fermions. In the strong noise limit, we demonstrate, under mild assumptions, that the statistics of the fermionic correlation matrix in the thermodynamic limit follow a universal form described by the recen…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 020403] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: Noisy free fermions in one dimension exhibit universal transport behavior in the strong noise limit, described by the KPZ equation.
motivation: Understanding how noise affects transport in noninteracting fermionic systems is important for quantum thermodynamics and open quantum systems.
method: The authors analyze the fermionic correlation matrix under various noise models in the strong noise limit, using analytical and numerical methods to derive universal statistics.
result: The correlation matrix statistics converge to a universal form governed by the KPZ equation, independent of the specific noise type.
conclusion: Noise-induced universality emerges in free fermion transport, providing a link between quantum dynamics and classical stochastic growth.

title: How Lorentz Boosts Reshape Relaxation Spectra
authors: L. Gavassino
abstract:
Author(s): L. Gavassino

In relativity, relaxation processes are often assumed to undergo time dilation under Lorentz boosts. We show that this intuition fails generically. Because of relativity of simultaneity, Lorentz boosts can split a single relaxation mode into a continuum of excitations, with a width set by the maxima…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 022301] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that Lorentz boosts can split a single relaxation mode into a continuum of excitations, challenging the naive expectation of time dilation for relaxation processes.
motivation: Understanding how relativistic effects modify relaxation processes is important for relativistic thermodynamics and non-equilibrium statistical mechanics.
method: The author analyzes relaxation spectra under Lorentz boosts using relativistic kinetic theory and the concept of relativity of simultaneity.
result: A single relaxation mode is shown to broaden into a continuum with a width set by the maximum boost velocity.
conclusion: Relaxation spectra are not simply time-dilated but can be reshaped by Lorentz boosts, with implications for relativistic fluid dynamics and thermodynamics.

title: Improving Shadow Estimation With Locally Optimal Dual Frames
authors: Keijo Korhonen, Stefano Mangini, Joonas Malmi, Hetta Vappula, And Daniel Cavalcanti
abstract:
Author(s): Keijo Korhonen, Stefano Mangini, Joonas Malmi, Hetta Vappula, and Daniel Cavalcanti

Accurate estimation of observables in quantum systems is a central challenge in quantum information science, yet practical implementations are fundamentally constrained by the limited number of measurement shots. In this work, we explore a variation of the classical shadows protocol in which the mea…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012428] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper improves classical shadow estimation by using locally optimal dual frames to reduce the number of measurement shots needed for accurate observable estimation.
motivation: Accurate estimation of observables in quantum systems is limited by the number of measurement shots; classical shadows provide a framework but can be inefficient for certain observables.
method: The authors propose a variation of the classical shadows protocol where the measurement basis is chosen adaptively using locally optimal dual frames, optimizing the estimation variance.
result: The locally optimal dual frames approach reduces the required number of measurement shots compared to standard classical shadows, especially for observables with low-rank structure.
conclusion: This work offers a practical improvement to shadow estimation, making it more efficient for near-term quantum devices.

title: Path Integral Control Of Open Quantum Systems
authors: Aarón Villanueva And Hilbert Kappen
abstract:
Author(s): Aarón Villanueva and Hilbert Kappen

We investigate open-loop quantum state preparation for a class of open quantum systems whose dynamics follow a Gorini-Kossakowski-Lindblad-Sudarshan (GKLS) master equation that admits a trajectory-based stochastic representation. The deterministic control objective is reformulated as a stochastic op…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012426] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a path integral control framework for open quantum systems described by GKLS master equations, enabling efficient open-loop state preparation.
motivation: Controlling open quantum systems is crucial for quantum technologies, but optimal control is computationally challenging due to the high-dimensional nature of the dynamics.
method: The authors reformulate the deterministic control objective as a stochastic optimal control problem using a trajectory-based representation of the GKLS master equation, then apply path integral control to compute the optimal control.
result: The path integral approach yields a closed-form expression for the optimal control in terms of an expectation over stochastic trajectories, which can be efficiently sampled using Monte Carlo methods.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and scalable method for open-loop control of open quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum state preparation and quantum thermodynamics.
