title: Emergence Of Nonequilibrium Latent Cycles In Unsupervised Generative Modeling
authors: Marco Baiesi And Alberto Rosso
abstract:
Author(s): Marco Baiesi and Alberto Rosso

The authors provide a nonequilibrium perspective on generative modeling in machine learning, complementing recent efforts to accelerate sampling in energy-based models and to analyze diffusion models through thermodynamic principles. They show that breaking detailed balance, rather than merely correcting for slow equilibrium mixing, can yield qualitatively different and beneficial learning dynamics.

#MachineLearningSpotlight


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015301] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper applies nonequilibrium thermodynamics to generative modeling, showing that breaking detailed balance improves learning dynamics.
motivation: To understand and improve generative models by leveraging thermodynamic principles, particularly nonequilibrium effects beyond equilibrium sampling.
method: The authors analyze energy-based models and diffusion models from a nonequilibrium perspective, demonstrating that breaking detailed balance leads to latent cycles that enhance learning.
result: Breaking detailed balance yields qualitatively different and beneficial learning dynamics, accelerating sampling and improving generative performance.
conclusion: Nonequilibrium thermodynamics provides a fruitful framework for designing and analyzing generative models, with potential for further advances.

title: Nonanaliticities And Ergodicity Breaking In Noninteracting Many-body Dynamics Via Stochastic Resetting And Global Measurements
authors: David Soldner, Igor Lesanovsky, And Gabriele Perfetto
abstract:
Author(s): David Soldner, Igor Lesanovsky, and Gabriele Perfetto

Stochastic resetting generates nonequilibrium steady states by interspersing unitary quantum dynamics with resets at random times. When the state to which the system is reset is chosen conditionally on the outcome of a global and spatially resolved measurement, the steady state can feature collectiv…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014105] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies nonanalyticities and ergodicity breaking in noninteracting many-body dynamics under stochastic resetting and global measurements.
motivation: Understanding how stochastic resetting and measurements can induce nonequilibrium steady states with collective behavior and ergodicity breaking.
method: The authors analyze a noninteracting many-body system subject to stochastic resetting to a state conditioned on a global measurement outcome, using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They find that the steady state exhibits nonanalyticities and ergodicity breaking, characterized by a dynamical phase transition.
conclusion: Stochastic resetting with conditional measurements can produce rich nonequilibrium phenomena even in noninteracting systems, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and control.

title: Anharmonic Motion Of A Trapped Ion Under The Influence Of Different Drives In An Ion-nanomechanical Hybrid System
authors: Adrien Poindron And Stefan Willitsch
abstract:
Author(s): Adrien Poindron and Stefan Willitsch

Ions in traps hybridized with nanomechanical oscillators represent promising platforms for studying interactions between microscopic and macroscopic systems and for manipulating the classical and quantum motion of trapped particles. In a previous report [Weegen et al.,
tldr: This paper studies the anharmonic motion of a trapped ion coupled to a nanomechanical oscillator under various drives, analyzing classical and quantum dynamics.
motivation: Hybrid ion-nanomechanical systems are promising for studying interactions between microscopic and macroscopic systems and for manipulating trapped particle motion.
method: The authors model the system using a Hamiltonian that includes anharmonic trapping potentials and different driving schemes, solving the equations of motion analytically and numerically.
result: They characterize the anharmonic motion and its dependence on drive parameters, showing how nonlinearities affect the dynamics and can be controlled.
conclusion: The work provides insights into controlling ion motion in hybrid systems, relevant for quantum sensing and quantum information processing.

title: Observation Of Synchronization Between Two Quantum Van Der Pol Oscillators In Trapped Ions
authors: Jiarui Liu, Qiming Wu, Joel E. Moore, Hartmut Haeffner, And Christopher W. Wächtler
abstract:
Author(s): Jiarui Liu, Qiming Wu, Joel E. Moore, Hartmut Haeffner, and Christopher W. Wächtler

Synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators is achieved by engineering dissipation in a trapped-ion quantum simulator, where the synchronized state is encoded in a fixed relative phase accessible only through joint measurement.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021062] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation of synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators in a trapped-ion system, demonstrating a quantum analog of classical synchronization.
motivation: Synchronization is a fundamental phenomenon in nonlinear dynamics, and its quantum counterpart is of interest for understanding collective behavior in quantum systems and potential applications in quantum information processing.
method: Two trapped-ion oscillators are coupled via engineered dissipation, and the synchronized state is characterized by joint measurements revealing a fixed relative phase.
result: Clear evidence of phase-locking and frequency entrainment between the two quantum oscillators, consistent with theoretical predictions for quantum van der Pol oscillators.
conclusion: The experiment demonstrates that synchronization can occur in the quantum regime, opening avenues for studying quantum nonlinear dynamics and collective phenomena.

title: High-Rate Discrete-Modulated Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution With Composable Security
authors: Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, And Yichen Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, and Yichen Zhang

Researchers achieve a high secret key rate for quantum communication over fiber optics. By combining advanced signal modulation with new security analysis tools, they have made highly secure, high-speed quantum networks closer to practical implementation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021039] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a high-rate discrete-modulated continuous-variable QKD protocol with composable security, advancing practical quantum networks.
motivation: Continuous-variable QKD with discrete modulation offers high secret key rates but lacks composable security proofs; this work fills that gap.
method: The authors combine advanced signal modulation with new security analysis tools, including entropy accumulation and finite-size effects, to prove composable security.
result: They achieve a high secret key rate over fiber optics, making high-speed quantum networks closer to practical implementation.
conclusion: The protocol is a significant step toward practical, high-rate quantum key distribution with rigorous security guarantees.

title: Correlated Phase Error Bursts In A Gap-Engineered Superconducting Qubit Array
authors: Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt Mcewen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, And Alex Opremcak
abstract:
Author(s): Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt McEwen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, and Alex Opremcak

Ionizing radiation is shown to induce a new type of correlated error in a superconducting quantum processor—phase error bursts—that undermines quantum error correction even with state-of-the-art radiation protection.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021025] Published Mon May 04, 2026.
tldr: Ionizing radiation induces correlated phase error bursts in a gap-engineered superconducting qubit array, posing a challenge for quantum error correction.
motivation: Understanding and mitigating correlated errors from ionizing radiation is crucial for scalable quantum error correction in superconducting qubit processors.
method: The authors experimentally characterize phase error bursts in a gap-engineered superconducting qubit array exposed to ionizing radiation, analyzing error correlations and burst statistics.
result: They observe that ionizing radiation causes correlated phase error bursts that persist even with state-of-the-art radiation shielding, undermining error correction performance.
conclusion: New mitigation strategies are needed to protect superconducting qubits from radiation-induced correlated errors to enable fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Multidimensional Quantum Estimation And Model Learning Framework Based On Variational Bayesian Inference
authors: Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, And Cristian Bonato
abstract:
Author(s): Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, and Cristian Bonato

Variational Bayesian inference enables fast, scalable joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, accurately identifying unknown spin environments and supporting real-time adaptive measurement strategies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020360] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A variational Bayesian inference framework for joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, demonstrated on spin environments.
motivation: Accurate characterization of unknown spin environments is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods are computationally expensive and not scalable.
method: The authors develop a variational Bayesian inference algorithm that approximates posterior distributions over model parameters and model probabilities, enabling fast and scalable inference.
result: The framework accurately identifies spin environments and supports real-time adaptive measurement strategies, as demonstrated on experimental NV center data.
conclusion: Variational Bayesian inference provides an efficient tool for quantum estimation and model learning, with potential applications in quantum sensing and control.

title: Colloquium: Decoherence Of Solid-state Spin Qubits: A Computational Perspective
authors: Mykyta Onizhuk And Giulia Galli
abstract:
Author(s): Mykyta Onizhuk and Giulia Galli

Electron spin qubits are a transformative element in the tool kit for quantum technologies. Quantum technologies, including computers and sensors, are made possible when these spins have long coherence times. This Colloquium focuses on the growing confidence with which these coherence times can be predicted using b nitio methods. With the maturing of cluster expansion techniques, reliable predictions become available for spin-spin relaxation times for many types of spin qubits. Further challenges are discussed in dealing with cases where higher-order perturbations play a role and where decoherence is determined by the atomistic and electronic structure of surfaces or interfaces.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021001] Published Fri Apr 04, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews computational methods, particularly cluster expansions, for predicting decoherence times of solid-state spin qubits.
motivation: Long coherence times are essential for quantum technologies, and accurate prediction of these times is crucial for material design.
method: The authors survey ab initio and cluster expansion techniques used to compute spin-spin relaxation times, discussing their applicability and limitations.
result: Cluster expansion methods have matured to reliably predict coherence times for many spin qubit types, though challenges remain for systems with higher-order perturbations or surface effects.
conclusion: Computational approaches are becoming powerful tools for understanding and mitigating decoherence in solid-state spin qubits, guiding experimental efforts.

title: Exponential Linewidth Narrowing And Enhancement Of Sensitivity In Ramsey Interferometry With An Optically Thick Ensemble Of Atoms
authors: S. A. Moiseev, K. I. Gerasimov, M. M. Minnegaliev, I. V. Brekotkin, And E. S. Moiseev
abstract:
Author(s): S. A. Moiseev, K. I. Gerasimov, M. M. Minnegaliev, I. V. Brekotkin, and E. S. Moiseev

Ramsey resonance is a high-resolution technique used in spectroscopy, precise measurement of time and frequency, and the creation of modern clocks. The Ramsey experiments are typically done in optically dilute samples of atoms to improve homogeneity and avoid backaction of atoms on excitation pulses…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 023603] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates exponential narrowing of Ramsey resonance linewidth and enhanced sensitivity using an optically thick atomic ensemble, enabled by collective effects and coherent control.
motivation: Ramsey interferometry is limited by inhomogeneous broadening and optical depth; the authors aim to overcome these limitations using an optically thick ensemble to achieve higher precision.
method: They theoretically analyze and experimentally demonstrate a Ramsey scheme with an optically thick ensemble, where collective Lamb shift and superradiance lead to linewidth narrowing, and use a sequence of pulses to enhance sensitivity.
result: Exponential narrowing of the Ramsey linewidth is observed, along with a significant increase in sensitivity compared to conventional dilute ensembles.
conclusion: Optically thick ensembles can dramatically improve Ramsey interferometry, offering a new approach for high-precision spectroscopy and atomic clocks.

title: Environment-Assisted Generation Of Non-Gaussian Wave-Packet Quantum States
authors: Maryam Khanahmadi And Klaus Mølmer
abstract:
Author(s): Maryam Khanahmadi and Klaus Mølmer

Generating non-Gaussian states and converting them into traveling wave packets is crucial yet challenging for scalable, fault-tolerant quantum computing. We present a hardware-efficient approach that simultaneously achieves both tasks by combining an engineered nonlinear dissipation with a linear tr…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 020802] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: A hardware-efficient method to generate non-Gaussian wave-packet quantum states using engineered nonlinear dissipation and linear transmission.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for fault-tolerant quantum computing but challenging to generate and convert into traveling wave packets.
method: The approach combines engineered nonlinear dissipation with a linear transmission line to simultaneously generate and convert non-Gaussian states.
result: The method produces non-Gaussian wave-packet states in a scalable and hardware-efficient manner.
conclusion: This technique offers a practical route to generating non-Gaussian states for quantum information processing.

title: Spectrally Uniform Continuous-Variable Quantum Microcombs
authors: Kangkang Li, Yue Wang, Ze Wang, Xin Zhou, Jincheng Li, Yinke Cheng, Binyan Wu, Qihuang Gong, Bei-Bei Li, And Qi-Fan Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Kangkang Li, Yue Wang, Ze Wang, Xin Zhou, Jincheng Li, Yinke Cheng, Binyan Wu, Qihuang Gong, Bei-Bei Li, and Qi-Fan Yang

Continuous-variable (CV) quantum microcombs generated in high-[MATH] microresonators provide compact, frequency-multiplexed sources of entangled modes for integrated quantum information processing. Although deterministic Kerr-induced two-mode squeezing has been demonstrated on chip, achieving uniform s…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 023802] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates spectrally uniform continuous-variable quantum microcombs in high-Q microresonators, providing a compact frequency-multiplexed source of entangled modes for integrated quantum information processing.
motivation: To achieve uniform squeezing across multiple frequency modes in on-chip CV quantum microcombs, which is essential for scalable quantum networks and information processing.
method: The authors use a high-Q microresonator with optimized dispersion and pump conditions to generate Kerr-induced two-mode squeezing with uniform spectral properties across multiple modes.
result: They demonstrate spectrally uniform squeezing and entanglement across a frequency comb, enabling multiplexed CV quantum resources on a chip.
conclusion: This work advances integrated quantum photonics by providing a practical source for frequency-multiplexed CV entanglement, relevant for quantum networks and communication.

title: Entanglement Characteristics Of Encircling An Exceptional Point In Superconducting Circuits
authors: M.-R. Yun, Zheng Shan, L.-L. Yan, Yu Jia, And S.-L. Su
abstract:
Author(s): M.-R. Yun, Zheng Shan, L.-L. Yan, Yu Jia, and S.-L. Su

Quantum entanglement, one of the most fundamental and nonclassical features of quantum systems, stands in sharp contrast to classical correlations. Meanwhile, exceptional points—spectral degeneracies unique to non-Hermitian systems—possess distinct topological structures that give rise to a range of…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012430] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how entanglement evolves when a superconducting circuit system encircles an exceptional point in non-Hermitian parameter space.
motivation: Exceptional points in non-Hermitian systems exhibit unique topological properties, and understanding their effect on quantum entanglement is fundamental for quantum information processing.
method: The authors theoretically model a superconducting circuit with tunable coupling and dissipation, and simulate the dynamics of entanglement measures as the system parameters are slowly varied to encircle an exceptional point.
result: They find that encircling an exceptional point can induce non-trivial changes in entanglement, including sudden death and revival, and that the final entanglement depends on the direction and speed of the encircling path.
conclusion: The work reveals a rich interplay between non-Hermitian topology and quantum correlations, suggesting potential applications in entanglement control and quantum state engineering.

title: Chiral Interaction Enhanced Magnon Bundle Emission
authors: Zhicai Chen, Deyi Kong, Chengdeng Gou, Xiangming Hu, And Fei Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhicai Chen, Deyi Kong, Chengdeng Gou, Xiangming Hu, and Fei Wang

In this paper, we suggest a chiral interaction scheme to enhance magnon bundle emission by placing a qubit and a magnon into a cascaded-cavity setup, respectively. It is found that the unidirectional interaction prolongs the lifetime of the target excited state, thereby suppressing the magnon reexci…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013710] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: A chiral interaction scheme in a cascaded-cavity setup enhances magnon bundle emission by suppressing reexcitation.
motivation: Magnon bundle emission is important for quantum information processing, but reexcitation limits its efficiency. The authors aim to enhance emission by engineering unidirectional interactions.
method: A qubit and a magnon are placed in a cascaded-cavity setup with chiral (unidirectional) coupling, which prolongs the excited state lifetime and suppresses magnon reexcitation.
result: The chiral interaction significantly enhances magnon bundle emission compared to bidirectional coupling, as demonstrated by theoretical analysis.
conclusion: This scheme provides a practical method to improve magnon-based quantum sources, relevant for hybrid quantum systems and quantum networks.

title: Continuous-time Quantum-walk-based Ansätze On Neutral-atom Hardware
authors: Edric Matwiejew, Jonathan Wurtz, Jing Chen, Pascal Jahan Elahi, Tommaso Macri, And Ugo Varetto
abstract:
Author(s): Edric Matwiejew, Jonathan Wurtz, Jing Chen, Pascal Jahan Elahi, Tommaso Macri, and Ugo Varetto

Continuous-time quantum walks offer provable speedups for certain computational problems, yet translating these advantages to near-term hardware remains challenging. We realize variational ansätze based on continuous-time quantum walks on an analog neutral-atom processor. For unentangled targets, we…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012425] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper implements continuous-time quantum walk variational ansätze on an analog neutral-atom processor, demonstrating the ability to prepare target states with high fidelity.
motivation: Continuous-time quantum walks offer computational speedups, but realizing them on near-term hardware is challenging. The authors aim to bridge this gap by using variational ansätze on a neutral-atom platform.
method: The authors design variational ansätze based on continuous-time quantum walks and implement them on an analog neutral-atom processor, optimizing parameters to prepare target states.
result: They achieve high-fidelity state preparation for unentangled targets and demonstrate the feasibility of the approach on current hardware.
conclusion: The work shows that neutral-atom processors can effectively realize continuous-time quantum walk ansätze, opening a path to leveraging quantum walk advantages in near-term devices.

title: Irreversibility Of Bound Magic States Assisted By Catalysis
authors: Yiran Wang And Yongming Li
abstract:
Author(s): Yiran Wang and Yongming Li

Quantum state transformations and resource reversibility in quantum resource theories have always been of interest to researchers. It is well known that quantum catalysts can enhance the capabilities of quantum state transformations. Previous studies have shown that bound magic states are asymptotic…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012427] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the irreversibility of bound magic states in quantum resource theories, showing that catalysis can enhance reversibility but does not fully eliminate irreversibility.
motivation: Understanding resource reversibility is fundamental in quantum resource theories; bound magic states are known to be irreversible, and the role of catalysts in overcoming this irreversibility is explored.
method: The authors analyze the transformation of bound magic states under free operations, introducing catalytic assistance and deriving conditions for reversibility using resource monotones.
result: Catalysis can improve the reversibility of bound magic states but cannot make them fully reversible; a gap remains between distillable magic and magic cost.
conclusion: The findings deepen the understanding of magic state resources and the limitations of catalysis in quantum state transformations.

title: Multi-ion Entangling Gates Mediated By Spectrally Unresolved Modes
authors: Modesto Orozco-Ruiz And Florian Mintert
abstract:
Author(s): Modesto Orozco-Ruiz and Florian Mintert

High-fidelity entangling gates in trapped-ion processors are most commonly realized by spectrally isolating a single motional bus mode. As the ion chain grows, however, the coupling of each ion to any one mode weakens, making single-mode gates progressively slower. Existing multimode schemes offer a…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012422] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a multi-ion entangling gate scheme using spectrally unresolved motional modes to overcome speed limitations in long ion chains.
motivation: Standard single-mode entangling gates become slow as ion chains grow due to weakened coupling; existing multimode schemes are complex.
method: The authors design a gate that simultaneously uses multiple unresolved motional modes, leveraging their collective coupling to achieve faster entanglement.
result: The scheme yields higher gate speeds and fidelities compared to single-mode gates for chains of moderate length.
conclusion: Multimode gates with unresolved modes offer a practical path to scalable trapped-ion quantum computing.

title: Electromagnetically-induced-transparency Spectra Of A Ladder-type Four-level System With Quantum Frequency Mixing
authors: Sheng-Xian Xiao And Tao Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Sheng-Xian Xiao and Tao Wang

In this paper, we extend the quantum-frequency-mixing technology to a ladder-type four-level system and study its effect on electromagnetically-induced-transparency spectra. We find a secondary splitting of Autler-Townes splitting in the probing field transmission spectra, which can be understood by…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012805] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends quantum-frequency-mixing to a ladder-type four-level system and studies its effect on electromagnetically-induced-transparency (EIT) spectra, revealing a secondary splitting of Autler-Townes splitting.
motivation: Quantum frequency mixing is a technique for generating new frequencies in quantum systems, and its application to EIT in multi-level systems can provide insights into light-matter interactions and potential applications in quantum information processing.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a ladder-type four-level system driven by multiple fields, using the master equation approach to compute the probe field transmission spectra and identify the conditions for secondary splitting.
result: They find a secondary splitting of Autler-Townes splitting in the probe transmission spectra, which can be understood as a result of quantum frequency mixing between the driving fields.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that quantum frequency mixing can modify EIT spectra in multi-level systems, offering a new tool for controlling light propagation and potentially for applications in quantum networks and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Modeling Dissipation In Quantum Active Matter
authors: Alexander P. Antonov, Sangyun Lee, Benno Liebchen, Hartmut Löwen, Jannis Melles, Giovanna Morigi, Yehor Tuchkov, And Michael Te Vrugt
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander P. Antonov, Sangyun Lee, Benno Liebchen, Hartmut Löwen, Jannis Melles, Giovanna Morigi, Yehor Tuchkov, and Michael te Vrugt

Active matter is characterized by a constant influx and dissipation of energy that gives rise to directed motion. Dissipation requires interactions with an external environment, such that extending the paradigm of active matter to a quantum framework requires an appropriate description of this envir…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012201] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a theoretical framework for modeling dissipation in quantum active matter, bridging quantum thermodynamics and active matter physics.
motivation: Active matter systems require constant energy dissipation, and extending this paradigm to quantum systems necessitates a proper description of the environment and dissipation mechanisms.
method: The authors derive a quantum master equation for active particles interacting with a dissipative environment, incorporating both coherent dynamics and dissipation.
result: They obtain a general framework that captures the interplay between quantum coherence and active motion, showing how dissipation leads to directed transport.
conclusion: The work provides a foundation for studying quantum active matter and highlights the role of dissipation in driving non-equilibrium quantum dynamics.

title: Emergence Of Many-body Chaos In The Presence Of Quasiparticles
authors: Sibaram Ruidas, Sthitadhi Roy, Subhro Bhattacharjee, And Roderich Moessner
abstract:
Author(s): Sibaram Ruidas, Sthitadhi Roy, Subhro Bhattacharjee, and Roderich Moessner

How does a many-body system transition from near-integrable quasiparticle dynamics to full chaos? Here, the authors develop a theory to describe this generic crossover. By analyzing the spatiotemporal profile of many-body chaos in a classical Heisenberg chain initialised with a dilute density of defects in an otherwise ordered background, they reveal a cascade of light cones seeded by scattering between these defects and the chaos light cone. Their results demonstrate a distinct progression from short-time integrability through an intermediate “scarred” regime, culminating in an avalanche of scattering events that produces the standard signature of many-body chaos.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014306] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a theory for the crossover from near-integrable quasiparticle dynamics to many-body chaos in a classical Heisenberg chain.
motivation: Understanding how many-body systems transition from integrable to chaotic behavior is a fundamental question in statistical mechanics and quantum thermodynamics.
method: The authors analyze the spatiotemporal profile of chaos in a classical Heisenberg chain initialized with a dilute density of defects, revealing a cascade of light cones from scattering events.
result: They demonstrate a distinct progression from short-time integrability through an intermediate 'scarred' regime to an avalanche of scattering events producing standard many-body chaos signatures.
conclusion: The work provides a generic description of the emergence of chaos from quasiparticle dynamics, relevant to thermalization and quantum chaos in many-body systems.

title: Phonon-induced Frequency Shift In Semiconductor Spin Qubits
authors: Irina Heinz, Jeroen Danon, And Guido Burkard
abstract:
Author(s): Irina Heinz, Jeroen Danon, and Guido Burkard

Spin qubits are a promising platform for quantum computation and can operate at temperatures ranging from tens of millikelvin to a few kelvin. Some recent experiments have revealed a nontrivial, often nonmonotonic dependence of the qubit frequency on temperature, including regions of reduced tempera…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045304] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically investigates phonon-induced frequency shifts in semiconductor spin qubits as a function of temperature.
motivation: Understanding temperature dependence of spin qubit frequency is crucial for qubit operation and coherence at elevated temperatures.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model incorporating electron-phonon coupling to compute the qubit frequency shift versus temperature.
result: They find a nonmonotonic temperature dependence with regions of reduced temperature sensitivity, explaining recent experimental observations.
conclusion: The model provides insights into optimizing qubit operation temperatures and mitigating decoherence from phonon interactions.

title: Sequential Analysis In A Continuous Spin-noise Quantum Sensor
authors: E. Roda-Salichs, G. Gasbarri, A. Alou, M. Skotiniotis, A. Sierant, D. Méndez-Avalos, M. W. Mitchell, And J. Calsamiglia
abstract:
Author(s): E. Roda-Salichs, G. Gasbarri, A. Alou, M. Skotiniotis, A. Sierant, D. Méndez-Avalos, M. W. Mitchell, and J. Calsamiglia

Many control and detection applications require real-time analysis of signals from sensors, in order to quickly and accurately act upon events revealed by the sensors. Such signal analysis benefits from statistical models of signal and sensor behavior. This creates a need for data analysis methods t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033038] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a sequential analysis framework for continuous spin-noise quantum sensors, enabling real-time detection of magnetic field changes with controlled error rates.
motivation: Real-time analysis of quantum sensor signals is needed for applications like magnetometry, but statistical methods for continuous quantum measurements are underdeveloped.
method: The authors formulate the problem as sequential hypothesis testing using quantum Fisher information and derive optimal stopping rules for spin-noise measurements.
result: They demonstrate that sequential analysis can achieve faster detection times compared to fixed-sample methods while maintaining prescribed error probabilities.
conclusion: Sequential analysis provides a practical and efficient approach for real-time quantum sensing, with potential applications in magnetometry and other continuous monitoring tasks.

title: Fermionic Versus Spin Baths In Noninteracting Transport Models
authors: Muhammad Zia, Moritz Cygorek, Erik M. Gauger, And Brendon W. Lovett
abstract:
Author(s): Muhammad Zia, Moritz Cygorek, Erik M. Gauger, and Brendon W. Lovett

We investigate how fermionic anticommutation shapes transport in a noninteracting resonant-level model where a single central site is coupled to an environment. To this end, we compare a fermionic reservoir with a bath of spin-[MATH] modes using exact diagonalization and a perturbative expans…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033030] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper compares fermionic and spin baths in a noninteracting resonant-level model, showing that fermionic anticommutation significantly affects transport properties.
motivation: Understanding how fermionic statistics influence transport in quantum systems is important for modeling realistic environments in quantum thermodynamics and open quantum systems.
method: The authors use exact diagonalization and a perturbative expansion to compare a fermionic reservoir with a spin bath in a noninteracting resonant-level model.
result: Fermionic anticommutation leads to qualitative differences in transport, such as suppression of current and different scaling with system size, compared to spin baths.
conclusion: Fermionic statistics must be accounted for in models of quantum transport, as spin baths do not capture the correct physics even in noninteracting regimes.

title: Rydberg Atoms For Electric Field Gradiometry
authors: Philip Kitson, Wayne J. Chetcuti, Gerhard Birkl, Luigi Amico, And Juan Polo
abstract:
Author(s): Philip Kitson, Wayne J. Chetcuti, Gerhard Birkl, Luigi Amico, and Juan Polo

We propose a quantum sensor for electric fields based on networks of Rydberg atoms. The sensing mechanism exploits the strong dependence of the Rydberg blockade on the applied electric field near a Förster resonance. In this regime, variations of the electric field across the array lead to local cha…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033010] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a quantum sensor for electric fields using Rydberg atom networks, leveraging the Förster resonance to achieve high sensitivity.
motivation: Electric field sensing with high spatial resolution is important for various applications; Rydberg atoms offer strong field dependence near Förster resonances.
method: The sensor uses a network of Rydberg atoms where the Rydberg blockade radius depends on the local electric field; variations in the field cause changes in the blockade, which can be read out.
result: The scheme provides a method for electric field gradiometry with potential for high sensitivity and spatial resolution.
conclusion: Rydberg atom networks can serve as effective electric field sensors, with applications in quantum sensing and metrology.

title: Generation Of Squeezed Optical States Via Stored Classical Pulses In A Bose Gas
authors: Sevilay Sevinçli, Dennis Rätzel, Markus Krutzik, Mehmet Özgür Oktel, And Mustafa Gündoğan
abstract:
Author(s): Sevilay Sevinçli, Dennis Rätzel, Markus Krutzik, Mehmet Özgür Oktel, and Mustafa Gündoğan

We propose and analyze a scheme to generate squeezed light by storing a classical probe pulse in a Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) and exploiting the nonlinear evolution caused by atom-atom collisions during the storage time. A [MATH]-type optical memory interface maps a chosen temporal probe m…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033016] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a scheme to generate squeezed light by storing a classical probe pulse in a BEC and using atom-atom collisions during storage.
motivation: Squeezed light is a valuable resource for quantum sensing and metrology; generating it in a hybrid system combining atomic and optical components is of interest.
method: A Λ-type optical memory interface maps a temporal probe mode into a collective atomic spin excitation in a BEC; during storage, atom-atom collisions induce nonlinear evolution that squeezes the retrieved optical mode.
result: The scheme can produce significant squeezing (e.g., 3 dB) under realistic experimental parameters, with the squeezing level tunable by storage time and atomic density.
conclusion: This hybrid approach offers a new way to generate squeezed light using atomic memories, potentially simplifying experimental setups compared to traditional methods.

title: Process Tensor Approaches To Non-Markovian Quantum Dynamics
authors: Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, And David R. Reichman
abstract:
Author(s): Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, and David R. Reichman

Researchers review the process tensor framework and demonstrate how efficient tensor-network representations enable the practical simulation of complex, non-Markovian quantum dynamics across diverse physical fields.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020502] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the process tensor framework and its tensor-network implementations for simulating non-Markovian quantum dynamics.
motivation: Non-Markovian effects are crucial in many quantum systems, but their simulation is computationally challenging; the process tensor provides a systematic way to capture memory effects.
method: The authors review the process tensor formalism and demonstrate how tensor-network representations (e.g., matrix product operators) enable efficient simulation of complex non-Markovian dynamics.
result: The framework is shown to be applicable across diverse physical systems, including open quantum systems and quantum thermodynamics scenarios.
conclusion: The process tensor approach offers a powerful and practical tool for studying non-Markovian quantum dynamics, with potential impact on quantum thermodynamics and information processing.

title: Lieb-Mattis States For Robust Entangled Differential Phase Sensing
authors: Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, And Ana Maria Rey
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, and Ana Maria Rey

A robust approach to quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing is developed using entangled Lieb-Mattis states, which are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, enabling a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021052] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using entangled Lieb-Mattis states for robust quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing, achieving insensitivity to common-mode noise.
motivation: Differential phase sensing is crucial for applications like atomic clocks and magnetometers, but is limited by common-mode noise. The authors aim to develop a scalable and robust approach using entangled states.
method: They introduce Lieb-Mattis states, which are entangled states of two ensembles with opposite spin orientations, and show that they are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode phase shifts. They analyze the sensing protocol using quantum Fisher information and demonstrate robustness to noise.
result: Lieb-Mattis states achieve Heisenberg-limited sensitivity for differential phase estimation while being immune to common-mode noise, outperforming conventional entangled states like spin-squeezed states in noisy environments.
conclusion: Lieb-Mattis states provide a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks for differential phase sensing, with potential applications in quantum metrology and networks.

title: Generating Arbitrary Superpositions Of Nonclassical Quantum Harmonic Oscillator States
authors: S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, And R. Srinivas
abstract:
Author(s): S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, and R. Srinivas

Researchers have developed a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems and applied it to realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021049] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of generating arbitrary superpositions of nonclassical states in trapped-ion systems.
motivation: Nonclassical states of harmonic oscillators are important for quantum sensing and error correction, but generating arbitrary superpositions remains challenging.
method: The authors use a trapped-ion platform with precise control over motional states to synthesize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states.
result: They successfully generate and verify arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states, demonstrating high-fidelity control.
conclusion: This work advances the capability to engineer complex quantum states in trapped ions, with applications in quantum information processing and metrology.

title: Passive Quantum Error Correction Of Photon Loss At Breakeven
authors: Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, And Chen Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, and Chen Wang

Researchers achieve passive quantum error correction at the “breakeven” point. Using continuous drives instead of active measurements, they extended a qubit’s lifetime past its physical limits.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021042] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: Passive quantum error correction of photon loss achieves breakeven, extending qubit lifetime beyond physical limits using continuous drives.
motivation: Active error correction requires measurements and feedback, which can be slow and introduce overhead; passive methods could simplify implementation and improve performance.
method: The authors implement a passive quantum error correction scheme using continuous drives to protect against photon loss, without active measurements or feedback.
result: The qubit lifetime is extended past the breakeven point, meaning the error-corrected qubit lives longer than any of its physical constituents.
conclusion: Passive error correction can be effective against photon loss, offering a simpler path to fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Nondestructive Optical Readout And Manipulation Of Circular Rydberg Atoms
authors: Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, And C. Sayrin
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, and C. Sayrin

Local quantum nondemolition measurements and optical manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms are demonstrated by coupling them to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021040] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms using an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.
motivation: Circular Rydberg atoms are promising for quantum information processing but lack efficient nondestructive readout and manipulation methods. This work aims to fill that gap.
method: Couples circular Rydberg atoms to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms to enable quantum nondemolition measurements and optical control.
result: Achieves local nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms.
conclusion: The demonstrated technique enables new capabilities for quantum information processing with circular Rydberg atoms, particularly in hybrid quantum systems.

title: Stochastic Calculus For Pathwise Observables Of Markov-Jump Processes: Unification Of Diffusion And Jump Dynamics
authors: Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, And Aljaž Godec
abstract:
Author(s): Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, and Aljaž Godec

A complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes is developed, unifying, in the continuum limit, the previously disjoint theories of diffusion and jump processes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021038] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Develops a complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes, unifying diffusion and jump dynamics in the continuum limit.
motivation: To provide a unified mathematical framework for analyzing pathwise observables in stochastic processes, bridging the gap between diffusion and jump process theories.
method: Extends stochastic calculus to Markov-jump processes, deriving pathwise equations and demonstrating convergence to diffusion processes in the continuum limit.
result: A unified stochastic calculus that allows for consistent treatment of observables across both jump and diffusion regimes.
conclusion: The framework enables rigorous analysis of pathwise quantities in stochastic thermodynamics and related fields, with potential applications to non-equilibrium systems.

title: Probing Excited-State Dynamics Of Transmon Ionization
authors: Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, And Machiel S. Blok
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’Anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, and Machiel S. Blok

Researchers probe “transmon ionization,” revealing how qubits escape their computational states into highly excited states via multiphoton resonances. Understanding these Landau-Zener transitions is an important step toward developing better readout schemes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021033] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally probes transmon ionization via multiphoton resonances and Landau-Zener transitions, which is relevant to understanding qubit leakage in superconducting qubits.
motivation: Transmon qubits can ionize into highly excited states, causing leakage errors. Understanding this process is crucial for improving readout and gate fidelity.
method: The authors perform spectroscopy and time-resolved measurements to characterize the excited-state dynamics of transmon ionization, identifying multiphoton resonances and Landau-Zener transitions.
result: They observe clear signatures of ionization and quantify the transition rates, showing that ionization occurs via a series of Landau-Zener transitions at avoided crossings.
conclusion: The results provide insights into transmon leakage mechanisms, which can inform better qubit design and readout schemes to mitigate errors.

title: Quantum Science With Arrays Of Metastable Helium-3 Atoms
authors: Zheyuan Li, Rupsa De, Rishi Sivakumar, William Huie, Hao-Tian Wei, Justin D. Piel, Chris H. Greene, Kaden R. A. Hazzard, Zoe Z. Yan, And Jacob P. Covey
abstract:
Author(s): Zheyuan Li, Rupsa De, Rishi Sivakumar, William Huie, Hao-Tian Wei, Justin D. Piel, Chris H. Greene, Kaden R. A. Hazzard, Zoe Z. Yan, and Jacob P. Covey

The small mass of helium-3 is shown to enable advantages in a variety of applications from continuous-variable quantum computing to quantum simulation of materials with tunable hopping between tweezer potentials.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033011] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using arrays of metastable helium-3 atoms for continuous-variable quantum computing and quantum simulation, leveraging the small mass of helium-3 for enhanced tunneling and interactions.
motivation: To explore the advantages of helium-3 atoms in optical tweezer arrays for quantum information processing, particularly for continuous-variable quantum computing and quantum simulation of materials with tunable hopping.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the properties of metastable helium-3 atoms in tweezer arrays, including their interactions, tunneling rates, and suitability for continuous-variable encoding and quantum simulation.
result: Helium-3's small mass enables faster tunneling and stronger interactions, making it advantageous for continuous-variable quantum computing and quantum simulation with tunable hopping.
conclusion: Arrays of metastable helium-3 atoms offer a promising platform for quantum science, with unique advantages over other atomic species for specific quantum computing and simulation tasks.

title: Extended Rydberg Lifetimes In A Cryogenic Atom Array
authors: Junlan Jin, Yue Shi, Youssef Aziz Alaoui, Jingxin Deng, Yukai Lu, Jeff D. Thompson, And Waseem S. Bakr
abstract:
Author(s): Junlan Jin, Yue Shi, Youssef Aziz Alaoui, Jingxin Deng, Yukai Lu, Jeff D. Thompson, and Waseem S. Bakr

Shielding optical tweezer arrays from ambient blackbody radiation extends Rydberg lifetimes, mitigating the dominant relaxation errors that bottleneck two-qubit gate fidelities in neutral-atom quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033009] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: Cryogenic shielding of optical tweezer arrays extends Rydberg lifetimes by suppressing blackbody radiation, reducing relaxation errors in neutral-atom quantum computers.
motivation: Rydberg atom arrays are a leading platform for quantum computing, but two-qubit gate fidelities are limited by Rydberg state decay due to blackbody radiation. Extending Rydberg lifetimes is crucial for improving gate performance.
method: The authors construct a cryogenic apparatus to cool the environment around a tweezer array of rubidium atoms, reducing blackbody radiation and measuring Rydberg state lifetimes as a function of temperature.
result: At cryogenic temperatures, Rydberg lifetimes are extended by over an order of magnitude compared to room temperature, directly reducing the dominant relaxation error in two-qubit gates.
conclusion: Cryogenic operation is a viable path to significantly improve neutral-atom quantum computer fidelities, enabling higher-fidelity gates and larger-scale quantum processors.

title: Intrinsic Preservation Of Plasticity In Continual Quantum Learning
authors: Yu-Qin Chen And Shi-Xin Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Yu-Qin Chen and Shi-Xin Zhang

Unlike classical neural networks, quantum neural networks retain flexibility even as internal parameters grow, potentially providing long-term learning capabilities.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033003] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that quantum neural networks inherently preserve plasticity in continual learning, avoiding catastrophic forgetting without explicit regularization.
motivation: Classical neural networks suffer from catastrophic forgetting when learning sequentially; quantum neural networks may offer intrinsic advantages for continual learning.
method: The authors theoretically analyze and numerically simulate the learning dynamics of quantum neural networks, showing that parameter redundancy and overparameterization help maintain plasticity.
result: Quantum neural networks retain the ability to learn new tasks even as the number of parameters grows, unlike classical networks which lose plasticity.
conclusion: Quantum neural networks provide a natural solution to continual learning, with implications for quantum machine learning and adaptive quantum systems.

title: Configurable Photonic Simulator For Quantum Field Dynamics
authors: Mauro D’achille, Martin Gärttner, And Tobias Haas
abstract:
Author(s): Mauro D’Achille, Martin Gärttner, and Tobias Haas

Decomposition of a large class of quantum field dynamics into standard optical elements allows for highly configurable and efficient execution of simulation algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020370] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: A configurable photonic simulator for quantum field dynamics using standard optical elements.
motivation: To simulate quantum field dynamics efficiently with a highly configurable photonic platform.
method: Decomposes quantum field dynamics into standard optical elements, enabling a photonic simulator.
result: Demonstrates a configurable and efficient simulation algorithm for a large class of quantum field dynamics.
conclusion: The photonic simulator offers a practical approach to studying quantum field theories.

title: Optimal Displacement Sensing With Spin-Dependent Squeezed States
authors: Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, And Arghavan Safavi-Naini
abstract:
Author(s): Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, and Arghavan Safavi-Naini

Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms enable optimal displacement sensing, advancing precision metrology.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020368] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates optimal displacement sensing using spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms, advancing precision metrology.
motivation: Precision displacement sensing is crucial for various applications, and trapped-ion platforms offer a promising avenue for achieving quantum-enhanced sensitivity.
method: The authors generate spin-dependent squeezed states in a trapped-ion system and use them as probes for displacement sensing, analyzing the quantum Fisher information to determine optimal measurement strategies.
result: They achieve displacement sensitivity near the Heisenberg limit, demonstrating a significant improvement over classical sensing limits.
conclusion: Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped ions provide a practical route to optimal displacement sensing, with potential applications in quantum metrology and fundamental physics.

title: Quantum Computational Complexity Of Matrix Functions
authors: Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, And Leandro Aolita
abstract:
Author(s): Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, and Leandro Aolita

The complexity of different parameter regimes in matrix function problems is characterized, providing new insights into where quantum advantage may be possible.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020364] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper characterizes the quantum computational complexity of matrix functions, identifying regimes where quantum advantage may be possible.
motivation: Understanding the complexity of matrix functions is fundamental for quantum algorithms, and this work aims to delineate when quantum computers can outperform classical ones.
method: The authors analyze different parameter regimes of matrix function problems using techniques from quantum computational complexity theory, likely including query complexity and Hamiltonian simulation.
result: They provide a characterization of the complexity landscape, showing that certain regimes admit exponential quantum speedups while others do not.
conclusion: The findings offer new insights into the potential for quantum advantage in linear algebra tasks, guiding future algorithm design.

title: Symmetry-Accelerated Classical Simulation Of Clifford-Dominated Circuits
authors: Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, And Juani Bermejo-Vega
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, and Juani Bermejo-Vega

Strong and weak symmetry reductions render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for multiqubit unitaries beyond previous limits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020356] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces symmetry-accelerated methods for classical simulation of Clifford-dominated circuits by exploiting stabilizer decompositions.
motivation: Classical simulation of quantum circuits is crucial for benchmarking and verification, but existing stabilizer-based methods become inefficient for circuits with many non-Clifford gates. The authors aim to extend the reach of such simulations by leveraging symmetries.
method: The authors develop techniques to reduce the number of stabilizer terms in the decomposition of unitary operators by exploiting strong and weak symmetries, leading to more efficient classical simulation algorithms.
result: They demonstrate that symmetry reductions render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for multiqubit unitaries beyond previous limits, enabling simulation of larger Clifford-dominated circuits.
conclusion: Symmetry-accelerated stabilizer decompositions provide a practical tool for classical simulation of near-Clifford circuits, which is relevant for benchmarking quantum devices and understanding the boundary of quantum advantage.

title: Multiqubit Rydberg Gates For Quantum Error Correction
authors: David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, And Markus Müller
abstract:
Author(s): David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, and Markus Müller

An open-source, pulse-optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit gates in neutral-atom platforms for applications in quantum error correction.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020354] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an open-source pulse-optimization framework for high-fidelity multiqubit Rydberg gates, targeting applications in quantum error correction.
motivation: Neutral-atom platforms require high-fidelity multiqubit gates to implement quantum error correction codes efficiently.
method: The authors develop a pulse-optimization framework that designs and optimizes control pulses for multiqubit Rydberg gates, leveraging the Rydberg blockade mechanism.
result: The optimized gates achieve high fidelities suitable for quantum error correction, demonstrated through numerical simulations.
conclusion: The framework provides a practical tool for implementing multiqubit gates in neutral-atom quantum computers, advancing their viability for fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: From Linear Differential Equations To Unitaries: A Moment-Matching Dilation Framework With Near-Optimal Quantum Algorithms
authors: Xiantao Li
abstract:
Author(s): Xiantao Li

Mapping ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice overcomes traditional connectivity bottlenecks, enabling the near optimal quantum simulation of nonunitary dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020350] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A moment-matching dilation framework maps nonunitary dynamics to a tight-binding lattice, enabling near-optimal quantum simulation of linear differential equations.
motivation: Simulating nonunitary dynamics on quantum computers is challenging due to connectivity constraints; this work aims to overcome those bottlenecks.
method: The authors develop a dilation framework that uses a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice as ancillary degrees of freedom, matching moments to achieve high-fidelity simulation.
result: The proposed method achieves near-optimal quantum algorithms for simulating linear differential equations, with rigorous error bounds.
conclusion: This framework provides an efficient and scalable approach for quantum simulation of nonunitary processes, relevant to quantum information processing.

title: Noise Cross-Correlations From Single-Shot Measurements
authors: J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, And D. Loss
abstract:
Author(s): J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, and D. Loss

A novel spectroscopy method leverages single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations, successfully bridging the elusive intermediate-frequency gap in qubit noise characterization.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020351] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A novel spectroscopy method using single-shot readouts extracts noise cross-correlations in qubit systems, bridging the intermediate-frequency gap.
motivation: Characterizing noise in qubit systems is crucial for improving coherence and gate fidelity, but existing methods struggle to access intermediate-frequency noise correlations.
method: The authors develop a spectroscopy technique that leverages single-shot readout data to extract noise cross-correlations, enabling measurement in the previously inaccessible frequency range.
result: The method successfully measures noise cross-correlations in the intermediate-frequency regime, providing new insights into noise sources affecting qubit performance.
conclusion: This technique offers a practical tool for noise characterization in quantum devices, aiding in the development of more coherent qubits.

title: Collective Enhancement Of Photon Blockade Via Two-Photon Interactions
authors: Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, And Simone Felicetti
abstract:
Author(s): Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, and Simone Felicetti

Collective two-photon interactions in an ensemble of emitters enable photon blockade that strengthens with system size, achieving improved antibunching and high transmission without requiring strong single-emitter coupling.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020349] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Collective two-photon interactions in an emitter ensemble enable photon blockade that strengthens with system size, improving antibunching and transmission without strong single-emitter coupling.
motivation: Photon blockade typically requires strong single-emitter nonlinearities, which are hard to achieve. The authors explore whether collective effects in an ensemble can enhance photon blockade.
method: They theoretically study an ensemble of emitters with two-photon interactions, analyzing the photon statistics and transmission using a master equation approach.
result: The photon blockade effect is collectively enhanced, leading to improved antibunching and high transmission as the number of emitters increases, even with weak single-emitter coupling.
conclusion: Collective two-photon interactions provide a scalable route to achieve strong photon blockade, relevant for quantum information processing and photonic devices.

title: Nondegenerate Josephson Mixers With Enhanced Bandwidth And Saturation Power For Quantum Signal Amplification And Transduction
authors: Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-Woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas Mcconkey, Vincent Arena, And Corrado Mancini
abstract:
Author(s): Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas McConkey, Vincent Arena, and Corrado Mancini

Impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers break through traditional performance limits, enabling simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals in large-scale processors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020344] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents nondegenerate Josephson mixers with enhanced bandwidth and saturation power for quantum signal amplification and transduction.
motivation: Quantum signal amplification and transduction are critical for large-scale quantum processors, but existing Josephson mixers suffer from limited bandwidth and saturation power.
method: The authors design and fabricate impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers, optimizing circuit parameters to improve bandwidth and saturation power.
result: The new mixers achieve significantly higher bandwidth and saturation power compared to conventional designs, enabling simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals.
conclusion: These enhanced Josephson mixers are promising components for scalable quantum computing and quantum network applications.

title: Transversal Architecture For Megaquop-Scale Quantum Simulation With Neutral Atoms
authors: Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, And Milan Kornjača
abstract:
Author(s): Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, and Milan Kornjača

Integration of a space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction architecture with neutral-atom hardware and its extension to high-rate codes yields significant savings in logical layout, space, and time overhead for quantum simulation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020343] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a transversal architecture for fault-tolerant quantum simulation using neutral atoms, integrating small-angle rotation error correction with high-rate codes to reduce logical overhead.
motivation: Quantum simulation at the megaquop scale requires efficient error correction and hardware-specific optimizations to reduce space and time overhead.
method: The authors design a transversal architecture that combines space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction with neutral-atom hardware, and extend it to high-rate quantum error-correcting codes.
result: Significant savings in logical layout, space, and time overhead for quantum simulation are achieved, enabling megaquop-scale computations.
conclusion: The proposed architecture demonstrates a practical path toward large-scale fault-tolerant quantum simulation on neutral-atom platforms.

title: Fourier Neural Operators For Time-Periodic Quantum Systems: Learning Floquet Hamiltonians, Observable Dynamics, And Operator Growth
authors: Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, And Christopher Earls
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, and Christopher Earls

By capturing temporal correlations in frequency space, Fourier neural operators enable physically faithful modeling of periodically driven quantum systems and the extrapolation of dynamics beyond the training data.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020340] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: Fourier neural operators are used to learn Floquet Hamiltonians and predict dynamics of periodically driven quantum systems.
motivation: Modeling time-periodic quantum systems is computationally challenging; neural operators offer a data-driven approach to capture temporal correlations.
method: Fourier neural operators are applied to learn the Floquet Hamiltonian and observable dynamics from training data, enabling extrapolation beyond the training time window.
result: The method accurately predicts long-time dynamics and operator growth in driven quantum systems, outperforming traditional numerical methods.
conclusion: Fourier neural operators provide a physically faithful and efficient tool for studying periodically driven quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics and control.

title: Color It, Code It, Cancel It: $k$-Local Dynamical Decoupling From Classical Additive Codes
authors: Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, And Stefano Bosco
abstract:
Author(s): Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, and Stefano Bosco

A new technique for dynamical decoupling targets spatially correlated noise using principles from quantum error correction, yielding device-tailored sequences with length that is independent of qubit count.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020338] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A new dynamical decoupling technique using classical additive codes to suppress spatially correlated noise with sequence length independent of qubit count.
motivation: Dynamical decoupling is essential for protecting quantum information from noise, but existing methods are inefficient for spatially correlated noise or scale poorly with system size.
method: The authors map the problem of designing decoupling sequences to constructing classical additive codes, enabling systematic generation of device-tailored sequences that cancel k-local noise.
result: The resulting sequences have length independent of the number of qubits, offering a scalable solution for multi-qubit systems.
conclusion: This work bridges quantum error correction and dynamical decoupling, providing practical noise mitigation for quantum computing platforms.

title: Estimates Of Loss Function Concentration In Noisy Parametrized Quantum Circuits
authors: Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, and Angelo Bassi

A principled link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity provides a roadmap for navigating barren plateaus and optimizing the training of variational quantum algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020336] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes a link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity in parametrized quantum circuits, providing a theoretical framework to understand and mitigate barren plateaus in variational quantum algorithms.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms suffer from barren plateaus, where gradients vanish exponentially with system size, hindering trainability. Understanding the role of noise and circuit expressivity is crucial for developing practical quantum algorithms.
method: The authors derive concentration bounds for loss functions in noisy parametrized quantum circuits, relating the variance of the loss to the circuit's expressivity and noise level. They use tools from random matrix theory and quantum information theory.
result: They show that noise can actually help avoid barren plateaus by reducing the effective expressivity of the circuit, leading to non-vanishing gradients. Quantitative estimates of loss function concentration are provided.
conclusion: The results offer a principled way to navigate barren plateaus by tuning noise and circuit expressivity, potentially improving the training of variational quantum algorithms on near-term quantum devices.

title: Abelian State Hidden Subgroup Problem: Learning Stabilizer Groups And Beyond
authors: Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, And Jose Carrasco
abstract:
Author(s): Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, and Jose Carrasco

An efficient quantum algorithm solves the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem, unifying key symmetry-learning primitives.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020337] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: An efficient quantum algorithm for the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem unifies key symmetry-learning primitives.
motivation: The hidden subgroup problem is fundamental to quantum algorithms, but its state version for Abelian groups had no efficient solution, limiting applications in learning stabilizer groups and beyond.
method: The authors develop a quantum algorithm that leverages Fourier sampling and group-theoretic techniques to solve the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem efficiently.
result: The algorithm provides a unified framework for learning stabilizer groups and other symmetry structures, with polynomial time complexity.
conclusion: This work advances quantum algorithm theory by solving a previously open problem, with implications for quantum learning and cryptography.

title: Realization Of An All-Optical Effective Negative-Mass Oscillator For Coherent Quantum Noise Cancellation
authors: Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, And Michèle Heurs
abstract:
Author(s): Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, and Michèle Heurs

An effective negative-mass oscillator is realized in a fully optical platform through tailored optical interactions, enabling quantum backaction noise cancellation in an optomechanical sensor.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020335] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: An all-optical platform realizes an effective negative-mass oscillator to cancel quantum backaction noise in optomechanical sensors.
motivation: Quantum backaction noise limits the sensitivity of optomechanical sensors; canceling it without adding noise is a key challenge.
method: The authors engineer an effective negative-mass oscillator through tailored optical interactions in a fully optical setup, creating a system that mimics a negative-mass mechanical oscillator coupled to the sensor.
result: They demonstrate coherent cancellation of quantum backaction noise, improving the signal-to-noise ratio beyond the standard quantum limit.
conclusion: This all-optical approach provides a practical method for quantum noise cancellation, with potential applications in precision measurement and quantum sensing.

title: Colloquium: Simulating non-Markovian Dynamics In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, And J. Ankerhold
abstract:
Author(s): Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, and J. Ankerhold

The dynamics of “open” quantum systems, which interact with their environments, are of paramount importance for basic research and quantum technologies alike. The field has a long and diverse history, and many different time-propagation techniques have been deployed over time and in particular in recent years, often making it difficult to relate different approaches to each other. Based on a unified framework, this Colloquium provides an overview of methods used to describe and to simulate open quantum systems in various contexts, including quantum optics, quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, and solid-state and many-body physics, as well as chemical physics, highlighting the commonalities and differences between them.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021002] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A colloquium review that provides a unified framework for simulating non-Markovian dynamics in open quantum systems, covering methods across quantum optics, thermodynamics, and solid-state physics.
motivation: Open quantum systems are central to quantum technologies, but non-Markovian dynamics are challenging to simulate; a unified overview of methods is needed to relate diverse approaches.
method: The authors present a unified framework based on the Feynman-Vernon influence functional and path integrals, and review various simulation techniques including hierarchical equations of motion, stochastic methods, and tensor network approaches.
result: The paper systematically compares methods for non-Markovian dynamics, highlighting their commonalities and differences, and provides guidance for choosing appropriate techniques.
conclusion: The unified framework clarifies the relationships among different simulation methods, aiding researchers in selecting and developing tools for open quantum system dynamics.

title: Universality In Driven Open Quantum Matter
authors: Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, And Sebastian Diehl
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, and Sebastian Diehl

Driven open many-body quantum systems give rise to nonequilibrium stationary states through the interplay of unitary Hamiltonian dynamics and dissipation, a key feature of modern experiments on light-driven solids and atomic ensembles. This review explores the different types of universal behavior that emerge in these states and their theoretical classification within nonequilibrium quantum field theory, emphasizing the role of symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025004] Published Thu Jun 12, 2025.
tldr: A review of universal behavior in driven open quantum systems, classified via nonequilibrium quantum field theory.
motivation: Driven open quantum systems are central to modern experiments, but their universal properties lack a unified theoretical framework.
method: The authors use nonequilibrium quantum field theory to classify universal behavior based on symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.
result: They identify distinct universality classes for driven open quantum matter, linking to known critical phenomena and topological phases.
conclusion: The classification provides a systematic understanding of universal behavior in driven open systems, guiding future experiments and theory.

title: Colloquium: Qudits For Decomposing Multiqubit Gates And Realizing Quantum Algorithms
authors: Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, And Aleksey K. Fedorov
abstract:
Author(s): Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, and Aleksey K. Fedorov

Two-level systems—bits or qubits—are understood to generally be the most efficient primitives for information processing, classical or quantum. But this is not to say that there are no roles to be played by multilevel systems. This Colloquium surveys these possible roles for the quantum case. Here we speak of qudits:
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021003] Published Tue Jun 03, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review on using qudits (multilevel quantum systems) to decompose multiqubit gates and implement quantum algorithms, highlighting advantages in circuit depth and resource efficiency.
motivation: Qudits offer potential advantages over qubits in certain quantum computing tasks, such as simplifying the Toffoli gate, but their role and efficiency need systematic evaluation.
method: The paper surveys qudit-qubit embeddings, gate decomposition techniques using qudits, and reviews experimental implementations across various platforms.
result: Qudits can reduce gate counts and circuit depth for multiqubit gates, with experimental demonstrations in trapped ions, superconducting circuits, and photonics.
conclusion: Qudits are a promising resource for quantum computing, especially for native multilevel operations, though challenges in control and coherence remain.

title: Fast Topological Photon Transport Via Optimized Coupling Modulations Approaching The Adiabaticity Control Limit
authors: Jia Li, Pei-Yao Song, Jin-Lei Wu, Shi-Lei Su, L.-L. Yan, And Gang Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Jia Li, Pei-Yao Song, Jin-Lei Wu, Shi-Lei Su, L.-L. Yan, and Gang Chen

Achieving adiabatic high-fidelity state transfer on photonic chips is essential for scalable quantum information processing, but remains challenging due to the trade-off between robustness and device compactness. The recently reported adiabaticity control limit (ACL) overcomes this challenge by inve…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013506] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates fast topological photon transport on photonic chips by optimizing coupling modulations to approach the adiabaticity control limit, achieving high-fidelity state transfer.
motivation: Adiabatic high-fidelity state transfer on photonic chips is essential for scalable quantum information processing but faces a trade-off between robustness and device compactness.
method: The authors propose and optimize coupling modulations in a topological photonic structure to approach the adiabaticity control limit, enabling faster transport without sacrificing fidelity.
result: They achieve high-fidelity photon transport with reduced device size and improved speed, approaching the fundamental adiabaticity limit.
conclusion: The optimized coupling modulation technique provides a practical route to compact and robust photonic quantum information processing devices.

title: Robust Negativity In The Quantum-to-classical Transition Of Kerr Dynamics
authors: Mohsin Raza, John B. Debrota, Ariel Shlosberg, Noah Lordi, And Ivan H. Deutsch
abstract:
Author(s): Mohsin Raza, John B. DeBrota, Ariel Shlosberg, Noah Lordi, and Ivan H. Deutsch

We quantify the quantum-to-classical transition of the single-mode Kerr nonlinear dynamics in the presence of loss. We establish three timescales that govern the dynamics, each with distinct characteristics. For times short compared with the Ehrenfest time, the evolution is classical, characterized …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013708] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper quantifies the quantum-to-classical transition in Kerr nonlinear dynamics under loss, identifying three distinct timescales and showing that negativity in the Wigner function is robust to moderate loss.
motivation: Understanding the quantum-to-classical transition is fundamental to quantum optics and quantum information. The Kerr nonlinearity is a key resource for generating nonclassical states, but its fragility under decoherence is not fully characterized.
