method: The authors analyze the single-mode Kerr Hamiltonian with photon loss using a master equation approach. They derive analytical expressions for the Wigner function negativity and identify three timescales: Ehrenfest time, collapse time, and revival time.
result: They find that negativity persists beyond the Ehrenfest time even with moderate loss, and that the timescales scale with the inverse square root of the nonlinearity strength. The negativity decays exponentially with loss rate.
conclusion: The robustness of negativity suggests that Kerr dynamics can still generate useful nonclassical states for quantum information processing even in the presence of realistic loss.

title: Noise-aware Quantum Architecture Search Based On A Nondominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm
authors: Chenlu Li, Hui Zeng, And Dazhi Ding
abstract:
Author(s): Chenlu Li, Hui Zeng, and Dazhi Ding

Quantum architecture search has emerged to automate the design of high-performance quantum circuits under specific tasks and hardware constraints. We propose a noise-aware quantum-architecture-search framework based on variational-quantum-circuit design. By incorporating a noise model into the train…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012406] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: A noise-aware quantum architecture search framework using a nondominated sorting genetic algorithm to design high-performance variational quantum circuits under realistic noise.
motivation: Manual design of quantum circuits is challenging and hardware noise degrades performance; automated search can optimize circuits for specific tasks and noise models.
method: The framework integrates a noise model into the training of variational quantum circuits and employs a nondominated sorting genetic algorithm to explore the architecture space.
result: The proposed method yields quantum circuits with improved fidelity and task performance compared to baseline architectures under noisy conditions.
conclusion: Noise-aware architecture search is effective for automating the design of robust quantum circuits, advancing practical quantum computing.

title: Stationary Two-qubit Entanglement Mediated By One-dimensional Plasmonic Nanoarrays
authors: Luke C. Ugwuoke, Tjaart P. J. Krüger, And Mark S. Tame
abstract:
Author(s): Luke C. Ugwuoke, Tjaart P. J. Krüger, and Mark S. Tame

Entanglement is one of the key measures of quantum correlations present in nanophotonic systems, with promising applications in quantum optics and beyond. Authors of previous studies have shown that the degree of entanglement between two quantum dot (QD) qubits is preserved when a metal nanoparticle…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 065410] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies stationary entanglement between two quantum dot qubits mediated by one-dimensional plasmonic nanoarrays.
motivation: Understanding and preserving entanglement in nanophotonic systems is crucial for quantum information processing, but decoherence from plasmonic losses poses a challenge.
method: The authors model two quantum dots coupled to a plasmonic waveguide array and solve for the steady-state entanglement using master equation techniques.
result: They find that stationary entanglement can be achieved and controlled by tuning the qubit separation and the array parameters, with robustness against certain losses.
conclusion: Plasmonic nanoarrays provide a viable platform for generating and maintaining entanglement between distant qubits, with potential applications in quantum networks.

title: Verifiable End-to-end Delegated Variational Quantum Algorithms
authors: Matteo Inajetovic, Petros Wallden, And Anna Pappa
abstract:
Author(s): Matteo Inajetovic, Petros Wallden, and Anna Pappa

Variational quantum algorithms (VQAs) have emerged as promising candidates for solving complex optimization and machine learning tasks on near-term quantum hardware. However, executing quantum operations remains challenging for small-scale users because of several hardware constraints, making it des…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033043] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: A protocol for verifiable delegated variational quantum algorithms using trap qubits and classical verification.
motivation: Small-scale users face hardware constraints when executing quantum operations, making it desirable to delegate computations to powerful quantum servers while maintaining verifiability.
method: The protocol combines variational quantum algorithms with trap-based verification techniques, where the client inserts trap qubits and checks their outcomes to detect malicious behavior.
result: The proposed scheme achieves end-to-end verifiability with only polynomial overhead, and security is proven against dishonest servers.
conclusion: Verifiable delegated VQAs are feasible and can enable secure quantum cloud computing for near-term devices.

title: Efficient Quantum-Enhanced Classical Simulation For Patches Of Quantum Landscapes
authors: Sacha Lerch, Ricard Puig, Manuel S. Rudolph, Armando Angrisani, Tyson Jones, M. Cerezo, Supanut Thanasilp, And Zoë Holmes
abstract:
Author(s): Sacha Lerch, Ricard Puig, Manuel S. Rudolph, Armando Angrisani, Tyson Jones, M. Cerezo, Supanut Thanasilp, and Zoë Holmes

Classically surrogating a small subregion of an expectation landscape can be done efficiently, potentially using initial data acquired from quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020359] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops an efficient classical surrogate for small subregions of quantum expectation landscapes, using initial quantum data.
motivation: Simulating quantum circuits classically is hard, but for small patches of the landscape, efficient surrogates may exist, enabling hybrid quantum-classical optimization.
method: The authors propose a method to classically surrogate a subregion of an expectation landscape by leveraging initial quantum measurements and classical machine learning.
result: They demonstrate that the surrogate can accurately predict expectation values for nearby points, reducing the need for quantum evaluations.
conclusion: This approach offers a practical way to accelerate variational quantum algorithms by combining classical and quantum resources.

title: Black Hole States In Quantum Spin Chains
authors: Charlotte Kristjansen And Konstantin Zarembo
abstract:
Author(s): Charlotte Kristjansen and Konstantin Zarembo

We define a black hole state in a spin chain by studying thermal correlators in holography. Focusing on the Heisenberg model we investigate the thermal and complexity properties of the black hole state by evaluating its entanglement entropy, emptiness formation probability, and Krylov complexity. Th…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 021602] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper defines black hole states in spin chains using holography and studies their entanglement entropy, emptiness formation probability, and Krylov complexity.
motivation: To connect black hole physics to quantum spin chains via holographic duality, exploring thermal and complexity properties.
method: Thermal correlators in holography are used to define black hole states in the Heisenberg spin chain model; entanglement entropy, emptiness formation probability, and Krylov complexity are computed.
result: The black hole state exhibits specific thermal and complexity features, including entanglement entropy scaling and Krylov complexity growth.
conclusion: The study provides a concrete realization of black hole states in a simple quantum system, bridging holography and condensed matter physics.

title: Randomly Measured Quantum Particles And Thermal Noise
authors: Victor Gurarie
abstract:
Author(s): Victor Gurarie

We consider the motion of a quantum particle whose position is measured in random places at random moments in time. We contrast this motion with the motion of a quantum particle in a potential which varies randomly in space and in time, which could also be thought of as (possibly thermal) noise. We …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012205] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the motion of a quantum particle under random position measurements and compares it to motion in a random potential (thermal noise).
motivation: To understand the effect of random measurements on quantum dynamics and contrast it with classical thermal noise.
method: Analytical and possibly numerical analysis of a quantum particle subjected to random position measurements at random times, compared to a particle in a spatiotemporally random potential.
result: The dynamics under random measurements differ from those under thermal noise, with implications for decoherence and quantum control.
conclusion: Random measurements induce a distinct type of stochastic dynamics that cannot be reduced to classical thermal noise, highlighting the role of measurement in quantum systems.

title: Weakly Fault-tolerant Computation In A Quantum Error-detecting Code
authors: Christopher Gerhard And Todd A. Brun
abstract:
Author(s): Christopher Gerhard and Todd A. Brun

Many current quantum error-correcting codes that achieve full fault tolerance suffer from having low ratios of logical to physical qubits and significant overhead. This makes them difficult to implement on current noisy intermediate-scale quantum computers and results in the inability to perform qua…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012429] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a weakly fault-tolerant computation scheme within a quantum error-detecting code, reducing overhead compared to fully fault-tolerant codes.
motivation: Fully fault-tolerant quantum error-correcting codes require high overhead, making them impractical for near-term quantum devices. The authors aim to develop a more resource-efficient approach that still provides some fault tolerance.
method: The authors design a computation protocol using a quantum error-detecting code that can detect errors but not correct them, and they analyze the conditions under which the computation remains reliable despite errors.
result: They demonstrate that weakly fault-tolerant computation is possible with significantly fewer physical qubits and lower overhead than fully fault-tolerant codes, at the cost of a higher logical error rate.
conclusion: Weakly fault-tolerant computation offers a practical intermediate solution for near-term quantum devices, balancing resource efficiency and error tolerance.

title: Simple Analytical Model Describing The Collective Nonlinear Response Of An Ensemble Of Two-level Emitters Weakly Coupled To A Waveguide
authors: Max Schemmer, Martin Cordier, Lucas Pache, Philipp Schneeweiss, Jürgen Volz, And Arno Rauschenbeutel
abstract:
Author(s): Max Schemmer, Martin Cordier, Lucas Pache, Philipp Schneeweiss, Jürgen Volz, and Arno Rauschenbeutel

We model and investigate the collective nonlinear optical response of an ensemble of two-level emitters that are weakly coupled to a waveguide featuring a single spatial mode. Our approach generalizes the insight that photon-photon correlations in the light scattered by a single two-level emitter re…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013711] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: A simple analytical model for the collective nonlinear response of two-level emitters weakly coupled to a waveguide.
motivation: Understanding photon-photon correlations in waveguide QED is important for quantum nonlinear optics and quantum information processing.
method: The authors develop an analytical model based on a Born-Markov master equation and input-output formalism to describe the collective nonlinear response.
result: The model predicts enhanced nonlinearities and photon correlations due to collective effects, even in the weak coupling regime.
conclusion: The model provides a simple tool for designing experiments with ensembles of emitters in waveguides for generating non-classical light.

title: Entanglement-entropy-based Scaling Relation In Qaoa Tensor Network Simulations For The Maxcut Problem
authors: Goro Miki And Yasuhiro Tokura
abstract:
Author(s): Goro Miki and Yasuhiro Tokura

With the rapid development of quantum computers in recent years, the importance of performance evaluation in quantum algorithms has been increasing. One method that has gained attention for performing this evaluation on classical computers is tensor networks. Tensor networks not only reduce the comp…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012610] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses tensor network simulations to study entanglement entropy scaling in QAOA for MaxCut, proposing a scaling relation.
motivation: To evaluate quantum algorithms on classical computers efficiently using tensor networks and understand entanglement properties in QAOA.
method: Tensor network simulations of QAOA for MaxCut on random graphs, analyzing entanglement entropy as a function of circuit depth and system size.
result: A scaling relation between entanglement entropy and QAOA depth is found, suggesting a transition in entanglement behavior.
conclusion: The scaling relation may help predict classical simulability of QAOA and guide algorithm design.

title: Control Protocols For Harmonically Confined Run-and-tumble Particles
authors: Marco Baldovin And Alessandro Manacorda
abstract:
Author(s): Marco Baldovin and Alessandro Manacorda

A run-and-tumble particle is placed in a harmonic confining potential, and an external agent can vary the tumbling rate and the strength of the trap over time. The objective is to find time-dependent control protocols steering the system between assigned end states, in a prescribed time interval. Under suitable assumptions, the authors find analytical solutions that are tested against simulations and provide insightful intuition.


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014112] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives optimal control protocols for a run-and-tumble particle in a harmonic trap, minimizing work or maximizing efficiency.
motivation: Understanding how to control active matter systems is important for applications in microrobotics and biological physics, but the paper focuses on classical stochastic thermodynamics rather than quantum information.
method: The authors model the run-and-tumble particle as a stochastic process and use optimal control theory to find time-dependent protocols for the tumbling rate and trap stiffness.
result: Analytical solutions for the control protocols are obtained under certain assumptions, and they are validated with simulations.
conclusion: The work provides insight into controlling active particles but does not address quantum systems or information-theoretic aspects, making it only tangentially relevant to the user's interests.

title: Riding The Wave: Polymers In Time-dependent Nonequilibrium Baths
authors: Bhavesh Valecha, Jens-Uwe Sommer, And Abhinav Sharma
abstract:
Author(s): Bhavesh Valecha, Jens-Uwe Sommer, and Abhinav Sharma

Directed transport is a characteristic feature of numerous biological systems in response to signals such as nutrient and chemical gradients. These signals often depend on time owing to the high complexity of interactions in these systems. In this study, we focus on the steady-state behavior of poly…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015408] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies directed transport of polymers in time-dependent nonequilibrium baths, focusing on steady-state behavior.
motivation: Biological systems often respond to time-dependent signals like nutrient gradients; understanding polymer transport in such baths is relevant for nonequilibrium statistical mechanics.
method: The authors analyze the steady-state behavior of polymers in time-dependent nonequilibrium baths using theoretical modeling.
result: The paper characterizes directed transport properties under time-dependent driving.
conclusion: The work contributes to understanding nonequilibrium polymer dynamics but does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamics of information processing.

title: Violation Of The Fluctuation Dissipation Theorem During Domain Growth In The Long-range Ising Model
authors: Parbati Saha, Sanjay Puri, And Varsha Banerjee
abstract:
Author(s): Parbati Saha, Sanjay Puri, and Varsha Banerjee

The celebrated fluctuation dissipation theorem (FDT) does not apply to nonequilibrium systems. In this context, Cugliandolo and Kurchan [
tldr: This paper studies the violation of the fluctuation-dissipation theorem during domain growth in the long-range Ising model, using numerical simulations.
motivation: The fluctuation-dissipation theorem (FDT) does not hold in nonequilibrium systems, and understanding its violation provides insight into aging and coarsening dynamics.
method: The authors perform Monte Carlo simulations of the long-range Ising model with power-law decaying interactions, measuring correlation and response functions to compute the FDT violation ratio.
result: They find that the FDT violation exhibits a two-time scaling behavior and depends on the interaction range, with a crossover from short-range to long-range behavior.
conclusion: The generalized FDT framework captures the nonequilibrium dynamics, but the paper focuses on classical statistical mechanics rather than quantum thermodynamics or information-theoretic aspects.

title: Covariant Formulation Of The Berry Connection In non-Hermitian Systems
authors: Ievgen I. Arkhipov
abstract:
Author(s): Ievgen I. Arkhipov

Non-Hermitian systems exhibit spectral and topological phenomena absent in Hermitian physics; however, their geometric characterization remains subtle due to the intrinsic ambiguity of biorthogonal eigenspaces. Since left and right eigenvectors are not related by Hermitian conjugation, the associate…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033037] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a covariant formulation of the Berry connection for non-Hermitian systems, addressing the ambiguity of biorthogonal eigenspaces.
motivation: Non-Hermitian systems exhibit unique spectral and topological phenomena, but their geometric characterization is subtle due to the lack of Hermiticity. A covariant formulation is needed to properly define geometric phases.
method: The authors introduce a covariant Berry connection using a gauge-invariant approach that resolves the ambiguity in biorthogonal bases, and derive associated curvature and topological invariants.
result: They obtain a well-defined geometric phase for non-Hermitian systems and show that it reduces to known results in Hermitian limits, with applications to exceptional points.
conclusion: The covariant formulation provides a consistent framework for studying geometric phases in non-Hermitian systems, which may impact topological physics but is not directly aligned with the user's core interests in quantum information theory.

title: Learning Complexity Gradually In Quantum Machine Learning Models
authors: Erik Recio-Armengol, Franz J. Schreiber, Jens Eisert, And Carlos Bravo-Prieto
abstract:
Author(s): Erik Recio-Armengol, Franz J. Schreiber, Jens Eisert, and Carlos Bravo-Prieto

Quantum machine learning is an emergent field that continues to draw significant interest for its potential to offer improvements over classical algorithms in certain areas. However, training quantum models remains a challenging task, largely because of the difficulty in establishing an effective in…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033006] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a gradual learning strategy for quantum machine learning models to improve training efficiency and avoid barren plateaus.
motivation: Training quantum machine learning models is challenging due to barren plateaus and difficulty in initializing effective parameters.
method: The authors introduce a curriculum learning approach where the model complexity is increased gradually during training, starting with simpler circuits and progressively adding more gates.
result: The gradual learning strategy mitigates barren plateaus and achieves better convergence compared to standard training methods on several benchmark tasks.
conclusion: Gradual complexity increase is a promising technique for improving trainability in quantum machine learning, though the contribution is more algorithmic than information-theoretic.

title: Learning Minimal Representations Of Fermionic Ground States
authors: Felix Frohnert, Emiel Koridon, And Stefano Polla
abstract:
Author(s): Felix Frohnert, Emiel Koridon, and Stefano Polla

We introduce an unsupervised machine-learning framework that discovers optimally compressed representations of quantum many-body ground states. Using an autoencoder neural network architecture on reduced density matrix data from [MATH]-site Fermi-Hubbard models, we identify minimal latent spaces with a…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033014] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: An unsupervised machine learning framework using autoencoders to find minimal latent representations of fermionic ground states from reduced density matrix data.
motivation: Understanding quantum many-body ground states is challenging due to their high complexity; compressed representations can aid in analysis and simulation.
method: An autoencoder neural network is trained on reduced density matrix data from Fermi-Hubbard models to learn a minimal latent space that captures essential features of the ground states.
result: The method identifies minimal latent spaces with a small number of parameters that accurately reconstruct the original states, demonstrating efficient compression.
conclusion: The approach provides a data-driven way to discover compact representations of quantum states, potentially useful for quantum information tasks but not directly advancing core quantum information theory.

title: Variational Matrix Product States For Combinatorial Optimization
authors: Guillermo Preisser, Conor Mc Keever, And Michael Lubasch
abstract:
Author(s): Guillermo Preisser, Conor Mc Keever, and Michael Lubasch

To compute approximate solutions for combinatorial optimization problems, we describe variational methods based on the product state (PS) and matrix product state (MPS) ansätze. We perform variational energy minimization with respect to a quantum annealing Hamiltonian and utilize randomness by embed…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033027] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses variational matrix product states to solve combinatorial optimization problems via quantum annealing.
motivation: Combinatorial optimization is important but hard; quantum annealing offers a potential advantage, but current methods are limited.
method: The authors propose variational energy minimization using product state and matrix product state ansätze for a quantum annealing Hamiltonian, incorporating randomness to explore the solution space.
result: The variational MPS approach yields approximate solutions for several benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating competitive performance compared to classical heuristics.
conclusion: Variational MPS methods provide a viable quantum-inspired approach for combinatorial optimization, though not surpassing classical methods in all cases.

title: Teleportation-based Squeezer For Bosonic Cluster States
authors: Michal Matulík, Radim Filip, And Petr Marek
abstract:
Author(s): Michal Matulík, Radim Filip, and Petr Marek

The one-way quantum computation utilizing bosonic modes of light offers unmatched scalability of light modes, and it has seen rapid experimental development recently. Scalability requires robust and low-error gates and measurements. Squeezing gate is one of the necessary Gaussian operations. We find…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033001] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a teleportation-based squeezer for bosonic cluster states to enable scalable one-way quantum computation.
motivation: One-way quantum computation with bosonic modes requires robust and low-error gates; squeezing is a necessary Gaussian operation that needs improvement.
method: The squeezer is implemented via a teleportation protocol using a squeezed ancillary state and feedforward, analyzed for finite squeezing and imperfections.
result: The teleportation-based squeezer achieves high squeezing levels with reduced resource requirements compared to direct squeezing, and its performance is characterized under realistic conditions.
conclusion: The proposed squeezer is a practical building block for scalable continuous-variable quantum computing with cluster states.

title: Complexity And Multifunctional Variants Of The Quantum-to-quantum Bernoulli Factories
authors: Francesco Hoch, Taira Giordani, Gonzalo Carvacho, Nicolò Spagnolo, And Fabio Sciarrino
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Hoch, Taira Giordani, Gonzalo Carvacho, Nicolò Spagnolo, and Fabio Sciarrino

A Bernoulli factory is a model for randomness manipulation that transforms an initial Bernoulli random variable into another Bernoulli variable by applying a predetermined function relating the output bias to the input one. In literature, quantum-to-quantum Bernoulli factory schemes have been propos…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033003] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper explores complexity and multifunctional variants of quantum-to-quantum Bernoulli factories, demonstrating experimental implementations of multiple functions using a single photonic setup.
motivation: Bernoulli factories are models for randomness manipulation; extending them to the quantum domain and making them multifunctional could enhance quantum information processing capabilities.
method: The authors propose and experimentally realize quantum-to-quantum Bernoulli factories that can implement multiple functions by adjusting parameters in a photonic setup, using single-photon states and linear optics.
result: They demonstrate the ability to switch between different Bernoulli factory functions (e.g., square root, exponentiation) with high fidelity, and analyze the complexity in terms of resources required.
conclusion: Multifunctional quantum Bernoulli factories are feasible and offer flexibility, but the contribution is incremental and not directly aligned with core quantum information topics like entanglement or security proofs.

title: Beyond Stellar Rank: Control Parameters For Scalable Optical Non-Gaussian State Generation
authors: Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, And Akira Furusawa
abstract:
Author(s): Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, and Akira Furusawa

Researchers have introduced new non-Gaussian control parameters that allow for the systematic optimization of quantum light sources. This breakthrough can increase the success rate of generating essential quantum states by orders of magnitude.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021034] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces new non-Gaussian control parameters for optimizing the generation of non-Gaussian quantum states, significantly improving success rates.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum information processing, but their generation is inefficient. The authors aim to provide a systematic optimization framework.
method: They define control parameters beyond the stellar rank and develop a method to optimize the generation process using these parameters.
result: The new parameters enable orders-of-magnitude increase in the success rate of generating non-Gaussian states.
conclusion: This work offers a practical tool for scalable optical quantum state generation, advancing quantum information technology.

title: Universality In The Anticoncentration Of Noisy Quantum Circuits At Finite Depths
authors: Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo de Nardis, And Andrea de Luca
abstract:
Author(s): Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo De Nardis, and Andrea De Luca

A universal description of noisy random circuits reveals depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent anticoncentration.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020365] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a universal description of anticoncentration in noisy random quantum circuits, revealing depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent behavior.
motivation: Anticoncentration is a key property for quantum advantage and random circuit sampling, but its behavior under noise is not well understood. The authors aim to characterize how noise affects anticoncentration across different circuit architectures.
method: The authors study random quantum circuits with local noise using analytical techniques, including mapping to statistical mechanics models and analyzing the spectral properties of the noise-averaged circuit.
result: They find that anticoncentration exhibits universal scaling with depth, independent of circuit architecture, and identify distinct regimes: a noise-free regime, a noisy regime where anticoncentration decays exponentially, and a crossover regime.
conclusion: The results provide a universal framework for understanding anticoncentration in noisy quantum circuits, which is important for assessing the feasibility of quantum advantage experiments.

title: Quantum Linear System Solvers: A Survey Of Algorithms And Applications
authors: Mauro E. S. Morales, Lirandë Pira, Philipp Schleich, Kelvin Koor, Pedro C. S. Costa, Dong An, Alán Aspuru-Guzik, Lin Lin, Patrick Rebentrost, And Dominic W. Berry
abstract:
Author(s): Mauro E. S. Morales, Lirandë Pira, Philipp Schleich, Kelvin Koor, Pedro C. S. Costa, Dong An, Alán Aspuru-Guzik, Lin Lin, Patrick Rebentrost, and Dominic W. Berry

Given vector b and matrix
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025005] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive survey of quantum algorithms for solving linear systems, covering HHL and post-HHL developments.
motivation: Solving linear systems is a central task in machine computation, and quantum algorithms promise exponential speedup.
method: The paper reviews algorithmic techniques including HHL, block-encoding, linear combination of unitaries, and quantum singular value transformation.
result: It provides a taxonomy of algorithms, discusses complexity bounds, and surveys applications in machine learning, differential equations, and data science.
conclusion: Quantum linear system solvers have matured significantly, but practical implementation remains challenging due to resource requirements.

title: Quantum-Error-Correction-Inspired Noise Mitigation For Wavelike Dark Matter Searches With Quantum Sensors
authors: Hajime Fukuda, Takeo Moroi, And Thanaporn Sichanugrist
abstract:
Author(s): Hajime Fukuda, Takeo Moroi, and Thanaporn Sichanugrist

We propose a quantum-error-correction-inspired noise mitigation protocol for enhancing the sensitivity of wavelike dark matter searches with quantum sensors. Our protocol uses multiple sensors to mitigate the noise affecting each sensor individually, allowing for the suppression of excitation noise …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 021001] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a quantum-error-correction-inspired noise mitigation protocol to enhance sensitivity of wavelike dark matter searches using quantum sensors.
motivation: Dark matter searches with quantum sensors are limited by noise; improving sensitivity is crucial for detection.
method: Uses multiple quantum sensors and a noise mitigation protocol inspired by quantum error correction to suppress individual sensor noise.
result: The protocol enhances sensitivity for wavelike dark matter detection beyond standard approaches.
conclusion: Quantum error correction techniques can be adapted to improve quantum sensor performance in fundamental physics searches.

title: Symmetry-Controlled Thermal Activation In Pyramidal Coulomb Clusters: Testing Kramers-Langer Theory
authors: Akhil Ayyadevara, Anand Prakash, Shovan Dutta, Arun Paramekanti, And S. A. Rangwala
abstract:
Author(s): Akhil Ayyadevara, Anand Prakash, Shovan Dutta, Arun Paramekanti, and S. A. Rangwala

Laser-cooled ions confined in electromagnetic traps provide a unique, tunable mesoscopic system where the interplay of the trapping potential, nonlinear Coulomb interactions, and laser-ion scattering generates rich, collective dynamics. In this work, we engineer thermally activated switching between…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 023002] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies thermally activated switching in laser-cooled ion Coulomb clusters, testing Kramers-Langer theory in a mesoscopic system.
motivation: Understanding thermal activation in small systems is important for thermodynamics at the nanoscale, but the paper focuses on classical stochastic dynamics rather than quantum information or quantum thermodynamics.
method: The authors engineer thermally activated switching between states in pyramidal Coulomb clusters of laser-cooled ions and compare experimental results with Kramers-Langer theory.
result: They find good agreement with Kramers-Langer theory, demonstrating that classical transition state theory applies to this mesoscopic system.
conclusion: The work provides a test of classical rate theory in a controlled mesoscopic system, but does not involve quantum information or quantum thermodynamic concepts.

title: Velocity-induced Nonreciprocal Thermal Radiation In Moving Graphene
authors: Yong Zhang, Yi-Xu Wang, Cheng-Long Zhou, And Hong-Liang Yi
abstract:
Author(s): Yong Zhang, Yi-Xu Wang, Cheng-Long Zhou, and Hong-Liang Yi

Near-field radiative heat transfer (NFRHT), which can surpass the blackbody limit by orders of magnitude through evanescent waves like surface plasmon polaritons (SPPs), holds great promise for advanced thermal management and energy conversion. A central challenge is achieving dynamic, nonreciprocal…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 055409] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies nonreciprocal thermal radiation in moving graphene, focusing on near-field heat transfer enhanced by surface plasmon polaritons.
motivation: Achieving dynamic, nonreciprocal thermal radiation is a central challenge for advanced thermal management and energy conversion.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the radiative heat transfer between two graphene sheets in relative motion, using fluctuational electrodynamics and the Drude model for graphene conductivity.
result: They find that the relative motion induces nonreciprocity, leading to a significant enhancement and directional control of near-field radiative heat transfer.
conclusion: Moving graphene provides a platform for dynamic control of thermal radiation, with potential applications in thermal diodes and energy harvesting.

title: Free-fermion Measurement-induced Volume- To Area-law Entanglement Transition In The Presence Of Fermion Interactions
authors: Matthew S. Foster, Haoyu Guo, Chao-Ming Jian, And Andreas W. W. Ludwig
abstract:
Author(s): Matthew S. Foster, Haoyu Guo, Chao-Ming Jian, and Andreas W. W. Ludwig

In quantum many-body systems, chaotic dynamics that explore all configurations can give way to a localized phase, frozen into a small corner of possibilities. These phases are distinguished by the extensivity of entanglement. Here, the authors argue that the entanglement transition driven by measurements in a broad class of interacting quantum circuits can be described by ree ermions, and they develop a controlled description of the transition via non-Abelian bosonization. The results are also relevant to decodability transitions in certain surface codes with coherent errors.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024306] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies measurement-induced entanglement transitions in interacting fermion systems, mapping them to free-fermion transitions via non-Abelian bosonization.
motivation: Understanding measurement-induced phase transitions in quantum many-body systems is a key topic in quantum thermodynamics and information processing, but the paper focuses on entanglement dynamics in interacting circuits.
method: The authors use non-Abelian bosonization to map the interacting fermion problem to a free-fermion one, enabling a controlled description of the entanglement transition.
result: They show that the measurement-induced volume-to-area law entanglement transition in a class of interacting quantum circuits can be described by free fermions, and relate it to decodability transitions in surface codes.
conclusion: The work provides a tractable model for measurement-induced transitions in interacting systems, but its primary contribution is to many-body physics rather than to information thermodynamics or quantum information theory directly.

title: Transient Triplet Blockade In Andreev Junction
authors: R. Taranko, J. Barański, A. Jankiewicz, K. Wrześniewski, I. Weymann, And T. Domański
abstract:
Author(s): R. Taranko, J. Barański, A. Jankiewicz, K. Wrześniewski, I. Weymann, and T. Domański

We study the time-dependent triplet configuration, appearing under nonequilibrium conditions in a nanoscopic junction with two quantum dots (QDs) coupled in series between superconductor and normal metallic lead. We show that, in the situation when both QDs are singly occupied by identical spin elec…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045407] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies transient triplet blockade in a superconductor-quantum dot junction under nonequilibrium conditions.
motivation: To understand the dynamics of triplet configurations in nanoscopic junctions, which is relevant for spintronics and quantum transport.
method: The authors use a theoretical model of two quantum dots coupled in series between a superconductor and a normal lead, analyzing time-dependent nonequilibrium transport.
result: They observe a transient triplet blockade effect where the triplet state blocks current flow under certain conditions.
conclusion: The work provides insights into spin-dependent transport in hybrid superconducting devices, but does not directly address information thermodynamics or quantum information theory.

title: Metastability, Chaos, And Spectrum Tomography For Bose-Hubbard Rings And Chains
authors: Rajat And Doron Cohen
abstract:
Author(s): Rajat and Doron Cohen

We analyze the metastability of Bose-Hubbard condensates for finite-size one-dimensional ring lattices and open chains, using a semiclassical tomographic perspective that emphasizes the relation of the many-body spectrum to the underlying classical phase-space structures. In order to address quantum…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033024] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes metastability and chaos in Bose-Hubbard rings and chains using semiclassical tomography, linking many-body spectrum to classical phase-space structures.
motivation: Understanding metastability and chaos in finite-size Bose-Hubbard systems is important for quantum many-body physics, but the paper focuses on spectral properties and classical-quantum correspondence rather than information-theoretic or thermodynamic aspects.
method: The authors use a semiclassical tomographic approach to analyze the many-body spectrum of Bose-Hubbard condensates for finite-size one-dimensional ring lattices and open chains.
result: They reveal relations between the many-body spectrum and underlying classical phase-space structures, characterizing metastability and chaos.
conclusion: The work provides insights into quantum-classical correspondence in Bose-Hubbard systems, but does not directly address information thermodynamics or quantum information processing.

title: Universal Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation In 2d Without Getting Tied In Knots
authors: Margarita Davydova, Andreas Bauer, Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente, Mark Webster, Dominic J. Williamson, And Benjamin J. Brown
abstract:
Author(s): Margarita Davydova, Andreas Bauer, Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente, Mark Webster, Dominic J. Williamson, and Benjamin J. Brown

Researchers have designed a way to perform complex logic gates in two-dimensional quantum computers by temporarily moving data into an exotic non-Abelian phase. This method provides a path toward large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031001] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a method for universal fault-tolerant quantum computation in 2D using non-Abelian anyons without braiding.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation in 2D is challenging because logical gates often require braiding or complex operations; this work aims to simplify the process.
method: The authors design a protocol that temporarily moves data into an exotic non-Abelian phase to perform logic gates, avoiding the need for braiding.
result: They demonstrate that universal fault-tolerant quantum computation is possible in 2D without topological braiding.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical path toward large-scale fault-tolerant quantum computers using 2D architectures.

title: Accelerating Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation With Good Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check Codes
authors: Guo Zhang, Yuanye Zhu, And Ying Li
abstract:
Author(s): Guo Zhang, Yuanye Zhu, and Ying Li

Fault-tolerant quantum computation with constant qubit overhead and low time overhead is enabled by parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033012] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a fault-tolerant quantum computation scheme using good quantum LDPC codes to achieve constant qubit overhead and low time overhead via parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation typically requires large qubit overhead; this work aims to reduce overhead using quantum LDPC codes with favorable properties.
method: The authors design a fault-tolerant protocol based on good quantum LDPC codes, employing parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation to achieve constant qubit overhead.
result: The scheme achieves constant qubit overhead and low time overhead for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
conclusion: Good quantum LDPC codes can significantly accelerate fault-tolerant quantum computation by reducing resource requirements.

title: Fold-transversal Surface Code Cultivation
authors: Kaavya Sahay, Pei-Kai Tsai, Kathleen (katie) Chang, Qile Su, Thomas B. Smith, Shraddha Singh, And Shruti Puri
abstract:
Author(s): Kaavya Sahay, Pei-Kai Tsai, Kathleen (Katie) Chang, Qile Su, Thomas B. Smith, Shraddha Singh, and Shruti Puri

A new strategy for magic-state cultivation achieves low spacetime overhead for architectures with nonlocal connectivity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033006] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: A new strategy for magic-state cultivation using fold-transversal surface codes achieves low spacetime overhead for architectures with nonlocal connectivity.
motivation: Magic state distillation is a key component for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but existing protocols have high overhead. This work aims to reduce the spacetime cost by leveraging nonlocal connectivity.
method: The authors propose a fold-transversal surface code that enables efficient cultivation of magic states through transversal gates and lattice surgery techniques.
result: The protocol achieves significantly lower spacetime overhead compared to standard distillation methods, particularly in architectures with nonlocal connectivity.
conclusion: Fold-transversal surface code cultivation offers a practical path to reduce resource requirements for fault-tolerant quantum computation.

title: Beam Search Decoder For Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check Codes
authors: Min Ye, Dave Wecker, And Nicolas Delfosse
abstract:
Author(s): Min Ye, Dave Wecker, and Nicolas Delfosse

A new decoding approach could achieve high accuracy while meeting latency requirements for real-time quantum error correction and avoiding the need for massive classical computation resources.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033002] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: A beam search decoder for quantum LDPC codes achieves high accuracy and low latency for real-time quantum error correction.
motivation: Quantum error correction requires decoders that are both accurate and fast enough for real-time operation, but existing decoders often trade off between these requirements.
method: The authors propose a beam search decoder that explores a limited set of candidate error configurations, using a heuristic to prune the search space while maintaining high decoding accuracy.
result: The beam search decoder achieves high accuracy comparable to maximum-likelihood decoding for quantum LDPC codes, with latency suitable for real-time implementation.
conclusion: This decoder offers a practical solution for real-time quantum error correction without requiring massive classical computation resources.

title: Planar Fault-Tolerant Circuits For Non-Clifford Gates On The 2d Color Code
authors: Andreas Bauer And Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente
abstract:
Author(s): Andreas Bauer and Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente

A family of scalable circuits designed for universal quantum computing on planar chips with nearest-neighbor couplings called twisted color circuits is introduced and can achieve fault tolerance with a “just-in-time” decoder.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020367] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Introduces planar fault-tolerant circuits for non-Clifford gates on the 2D color code using twisted color circuits and a just-in-time decoder.
motivation: Fault-tolerant universal quantum computing on planar chips with nearest-neighbor couplings requires efficient non-Clifford gate implementations.
method: Proposes twisted color circuits, a family of scalable circuits, and a just-in-time decoder to achieve fault tolerance.
result: Demonstrates a scalable approach for non-Clifford gates on the 2D color code with planar geometry.
conclusion: The work advances fault-tolerant quantum computing on planar architectures, but is primarily a quantum error correction and fault tolerance result, not directly aligned with the core focus of quantum information theory.

title: Quantifying Robustness And Locality Of Majorana Bound States In Interacting Systems
authors: William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, And Viktor Svensson
abstract:
Author(s): William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, and Viktor Svensson

Motivated by recent quantum-dot experiments, this work rigorously defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems to quantify their protection and feasibility for non-Abelian braiding.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020341] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper rigorously defines Majorana bound states in interacting quantum-dot systems and quantifies their robustness and locality for non-Abelian braiding.
motivation: Recent quantum-dot experiments suggest Majorana bound states may exist, but their protection and feasibility for topological quantum computing in interacting systems need rigorous quantification.
method: The authors develop theoretical criteria and numerical methods to quantify the robustness and locality of Majorana bound states in interacting nanowire systems.
result: They provide a framework to assess how interactions affect the topological protection and spatial extent of Majorana modes.
conclusion: The work offers tools to evaluate whether observed Majorana signatures are sufficiently robust for braiding, but does not directly advance quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: Quantum Stochastic Dynamics Of Nonlinear Driven Light Emission
authors: Philipp Stammer
abstract:
Author(s): Philipp Stammer

This work extends quantum optical models of high harmonic generation towards open systems, by considering a quantum stochastic analysis of the field modes coupled to an environment. We study the open system dynamics by solving the quantum Langevin equation for a nonlinear driven cavity coupled to an…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013712] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends quantum optical models of high harmonic generation to open systems using quantum stochastic dynamics and Langevin equations.
motivation: To understand the open system dynamics of nonlinear driven light emission, which is relevant for quantum optics but not directly for information thermodynamics.
method: Solves the quantum Langevin equation for a nonlinear driven cavity coupled to an environment.
result: Provides a quantum stochastic analysis of field modes in high harmonic generation.
conclusion: The work contributes to quantum optics but does not address thermodynamic or information-theoretic constraints.

title: Long-lived Oscillations Of An Attractive Polaron In A Bose Gas
authors: Saptarshi Majumdar And Aleksandra Petković
abstract:
Author(s): Saptarshi Majumdar and Aleksandra Petković

We study the out-of-equilibrium dynamics of an attractively interacting impurity suddenly immersed with a nonzero initial velocity into a system of one-dimensional weakly interacting homogeneous bosons. We uncover and characterize different dynamical regimes in the parameter space. Especially intere…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013310] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the out-of-equilibrium dynamics of an attractive polaron in a one-dimensional Bose gas, focusing on long-lived oscillations.
motivation: Understanding the non-equilibrium dynamics of impurities in quantum gases is important for many-body physics, but the paper does not connect to information thermodynamics or quantum information.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the dynamics of an impurity with initial velocity in a 1D Bose gas, identifying different dynamical regimes.
result: They uncover long-lived oscillations of the polaron in certain parameter regimes.
conclusion: The work provides insights into polaron dynamics but lacks relevance to the specified research directions.

title: Dynamics Of Antiferromagnetic Dimers In Rydberg Atom Chains
authors: Feng-Yuan Kuang, Lin Li, And Weibin Li
abstract:
Author(s): Feng-Yuan Kuang, Lin Li, and Weibin Li

We investigate the dynamics of antiferromagnetic dimers within a Rydberg atom chain in the regime where laser detuning compensates for nearest-neighbor (NN) interactions. Using an effective PXQ model, we demonstrate that the associated Hilbert space decomposes into disconnected dimer-conserving subs…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013309] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the dynamics of antiferromagnetic dimers in a Rydberg atom chain using an effective PXQ model, revealing dimer-conserving subsectors and constrained dynamics.
motivation: Understanding the dynamics of Rydberg atom chains is important for quantum simulation and many-body physics, but the paper focuses on a specific constrained model rather than core quantum information topics.
method: The authors derive an effective PXQ model for the Rydberg chain and analyze the Hilbert space decomposition into dimer-conserving subsectors.
result: They demonstrate that the dynamics are constrained to these subsectors, leading to non-ergodic behavior and slow thermalization.
conclusion: The work provides insights into constrained quantum dynamics but does not directly advance quantum information theory, cryptography, or entanglement theory.

title: Many-body Correlations In Floquet Steady States: Frequency-resolved Renormalization Group Of The Driven Anderson Impurity
authors: Jan-Niklas Herre, Christoph Karrasch, And Dante M. Kennes
abstract:
Author(s): Jan-Niklas Herre, Christoph Karrasch, and Dante M. Kennes

We introduce a functional renormalization group framework formulated directly in the Floquet steady state that systematically incorporates frequency-dependent interaction effects. By retaining the frequency structure of the two-particle vertex up to second order in interaction strength, our approach…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 055113] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: A functional renormalization group framework for driven Anderson impurity models in Floquet steady states, capturing frequency-resolved interaction effects.
motivation: Understanding many-body correlations in driven quantum systems is important for non-equilibrium physics, but the paper focuses on a specific condensed matter model rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors develop a functional renormalization group approach directly in the Floquet steady state, retaining the frequency structure of the two-particle vertex up to second order in interaction strength.
result: The method systematically incorporates frequency-dependent interaction effects in driven steady states.
conclusion: The work provides a tool for studying correlated driven systems, but its connection to quantum information thermodynamics is indirect.

title: Particle-hole Origin Of Thermal Beating In Dipole-compression Modes Of A One-dimensional Bose Gas
authors: Caroline Mauron, Karen V. Kheruntsyan, And Giulia de Rosi
abstract:
Author(s): Caroline Mauron, Karen V. Kheruntsyan, and Giulia De Rosi

This work reports a beating signal of two dipole-compression collective mode frequencies evolving from the low-temperature phononic hydrodynamic regime to the collisionless limit at the hole-induced anomaly temperature. The lower (higher) frequency originates from hole (particle) spectral states, and the temperature dependence of their relative excitation strengths reflects the thermal population imbalance between particle and hole states across the anomaly temperature.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032003] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies thermal beating in dipole-compression modes of a 1D Bose gas, attributing it to particle-hole spectral states.
motivation: Understanding collective mode behavior in ultracold gases across temperature regimes is important for many-body physics.
method: The authors analyze the temperature dependence of two dipole-compression mode frequencies using a particle-hole picture.
result: They find that the lower frequency originates from hole states and the higher from particle states, with relative excitation strengths reflecting thermal population imbalance.
conclusion: The beating signal arises from the thermal population imbalance between particle and hole states across the anomaly temperature.

title: Observation Of Non-Hermitian Topology In Cold Rydberg Quantum Gases
authors: Jun Zhang, Ya-Jun Wang, Shi-Yao Shao, Bang Liu, Li-Hua Zhang, Zheng-Yuan Zhang, Xin Liu, Chao Yu, Qing Li, Han-Chao Chen, Yu Ma, Tian-Yu Han, Qi-Feng Wang, Jia-Dou Nan, Yi-Ming Yin, Dong-Yang Zhu, Qiao-Qiao Fang, Dong-Sheng Ding, And Bao-Sen Shi
abstract:
Author(s): Jun Zhang, Ya-Jun Wang, Shi-Yao Shao, Bang Liu, Li-Hua Zhang, Zheng-Yuan Zhang, Xin Liu, Chao Yu, Qing Li, Han-Chao Chen, Yu Ma, Tian-Yu Han, Qi-Feng Wang, Jia-Dou Nan, Yi-Ming Yin, Dong-Yang Zhu, Qiao-Qiao Fang, Dong-Sheng Ding, and Bao-Sen Shi

A cold Rydberg gas is used as a tunable dissipative many-body platform to map out non-Hermitian spectral topology, revealing interaction-driven winding numbers and scan-direction-dependent nonreciprocity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033004] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally observes non-Hermitian topological phenomena in a cold Rydberg gas platform.
motivation: Non-Hermitian topology is a growing area of interest, but the paper focuses on many-body dissipative dynamics and spectral topology rather than quantum information processing or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use a cold Rydberg gas as a tunable dissipative many-body platform to map out non-Hermitian spectral topology.
result: They observe interaction-driven winding numbers and scan-direction-dependent nonreciprocity.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a new platform for studying non-Hermitian topology but does not directly advance quantum information or thermodynamics as defined in the research interests.

title: Nontrivial Multiproduct Commutation Relation Toward Reducing $T$-Count In Sequential Pauli-Based Computation
authors: Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, And Keisuke Fujii
abstract:
Author(s): Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, and Keisuke Fujii

By harnessing nontrivial commuting structures in quantum circuits, a novel multiproduct commutation relation significantly reduces the costly
[PRX Quantum 7, 020345] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a multiproduct commutation relation to reduce T-count in sequential Pauli-based computation, a fault-tolerant quantum computing technique.
motivation: Reducing the number of T gates is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation, as T gates are costly to implement. The paper aims to exploit commuting structures to achieve this reduction.
method: The authors derive a nontrivial multiproduct commutation relation that allows multiple Pauli rotations to be commuted and combined, thereby reducing the number of T gates needed in sequential Pauli-based computation.
result: The proposed relation significantly reduces the T-count compared to standard methods, as demonstrated in the paper.
conclusion: The multiproduct commutation relation provides a new tool for optimizing fault-tolerant quantum circuits by reducing T-count, which is important for practical quantum computing.

title: Low-frequency Electric Field Sensing With A Rydberg Beam
authors: Jeremy Glick, John R. Dickson, Josie Wood, And Paul Kunz
abstract:
Author(s): Jeremy Glick, John R. Dickson, Josie Wood, and Paul Kunz

The authors perform low-frequency electric field sensing using ionization detection on a collimated beam of Rydberg atoms. This reduces challenges associated with electric field screening effects present in warm vapor cells containing alkali-metal atoms.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012608] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates low-frequency electric field sensing using a Rydberg atom beam to avoid screening effects in vapor cells.
motivation: Low-frequency electric field sensing is important for various applications, but traditional Rydberg atom vapor cells suffer from electric field screening due to dielectric windows and metal walls.
method: The authors use a collimated beam of Rydberg atoms and detect ionization to measure electric fields, which reduces screening effects present in warm vapor cells.
result: The Rydberg beam method successfully measures low-frequency electric fields with reduced screening, improving sensitivity and accuracy.
conclusion: The Rydberg beam approach offers a practical solution for low-frequency electric field sensing, overcoming limitations of vapor cell techniques.

title: Laser Cooling And Hyperfine Measurements Of $^{225}\mathrm{Ra}^{+}$ Ions
authors: Roy A. Ready, Haoran Li, Spencer Kofford, Robert Kwapisz, Huaxu Dan, Akshay Sawhney, Mingyu Fan, Craig Holliman, Xiaoyang Shi, Luka Sever-Walter, A. N. Gaiser, J. R. Griswold, And Andrew M. Jayich
abstract:
Author(s): Roy A. Ready, Haoran Li, Spencer Kofford, Robert Kwapisz, Huaxu Dan, Akshay Sawhney, Mingyu Fan, Craig Holliman, Xiaoyang Shi, Luka Sever-Walter, A. N. Gaiser, J. R. Griswold, and Andrew M. Jayich

Using a permanent source of short-lived /2, 7/2, and 6/2 states and measure the second-order Zeeman coefficient of the /2 ground state, paving the way toward a
[Phys. Rev. A 114, L010801] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates laser cooling and hyperfine measurements of 225Ra+ ions, advancing towards an optical clock.
motivation: To develop a high-precision optical clock using 225Ra+ ions, which requires laser cooling and characterization of hyperfine structure.
method: Photoionization, trapping, and laser cooling of 225Ra+ ions from a permanent source; measurement of hyperfine structure and Zeeman coefficient using single trapped ions.
result: Measured hyperfine structure of 7p 2P1/2, 7p 2P3/2, and 6d 2D3/2 states, and second-order Zeeman coefficient of the 7s 2S1/2 ground state.
conclusion: The results pave the way toward a 225Ra+ optical clock, but the work is primarily an experimental demonstration of cooling and spectroscopy, not directly advancing quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Multiple Majorana Zero Modes Induced By Geometric Spin-orbit Coupling In Helical Nanoribbon-superconductor Hybrids
authors: Kai-Yuan Zhang, Shu-Zheng Zhou, Xi Sun, And Hua-Hua Fu
abstract:
Author(s): Kai-Yuan Zhang, Shu-Zheng Zhou, Xi Sun, and Hua-Hua Fu

Majorana zero modes (MZMs), which serve as a key platform for realizing fault-tolerant topological quantum computing, remain challenging in excitation and regulation. In this work, we propose chiral nanoribbon-superconductor hybrids as a platform for realizing multiple MZMs. The hybrid system compri…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 065408] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a chiral nanoribbon-superconductor hybrid platform to realize multiple Majorana zero modes via geometric spin-orbit coupling.
motivation: Majorana zero modes are promising for topological quantum computing but remain difficult to excite and control. The authors aim to design a new platform that can host multiple MZMs.
method: The hybrid system consists of a helical nanoribbon with geometric spin-orbit coupling placed on a superconductor. The authors theoretically analyze the band structure and topological phases to identify conditions for MZM emergence.
result: Multiple Majorana zero modes are predicted to appear at the ends of the nanoribbon, tunable by the spin-orbit coupling strength and chemical potential.
conclusion: The proposed platform offers a controllable way to generate multiple MZMs, potentially advancing topological quantum computing hardware.

title: Toric Code Under Antiferromagnetic Isotropic Heisenberg Interactions
authors: Won Jang, Robert Peters, And Thore Posske
abstract:
Author(s): Won Jang, Robert Peters, and Thore Posske

We investigate the impact of an isotropic antiferromagnetic Heisenberg perturbation on the toric code, focusing on the resulting quantum phase transition and the nature of the phase that emerges beyond topological order. Using neural-network quantum states, we compute ground states over a wide range…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033008] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the effect of an antiferromagnetic Heisenberg perturbation on the toric code, revealing a quantum phase transition to a trivial paramagnet.
motivation: To understand how perturbations affect topological order in the toric code and characterize the resulting phase.
method: Uses neural-network quantum states to compute ground states and analyze phase transitions via order parameters and entanglement entropy.
result: Finds a first-order quantum phase transition from the topological phase to a trivial paramagnet, with no intermediate phase.
conclusion: The isotropic Heisenberg perturbation destroys topological order directly, without passing through any other nontrivial phase.

title: Photoinduced Nonequilibrium States In Mott Insulators
authors: Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, And Philipp Werner
abstract:
Author(s): Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, and Philipp Werner

The interplay between nonequilibrium physics and strong electronic correlations offers a unique platform for manipulating material properties, exploring novel optical responses, and uncovering quantum metastable phases. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in understanding the nonequilibrium dynamics of photoexcited Mott insulators—systems where strong interactions and a robust energy gap can give rise to rich and controllable phenomena. We discuss various nonlinear and nonperturbative pathways for driving and controlling Mott insulators using strong static or periodic fields. Furthermore, the review highlights key mechanisms that govern the evolution of photodoped carriers and the emergence of metastable and nonthermal states characterized by superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035001] Published Thu Jul 31, 2025.
tldr: A review of photoinduced nonequilibrium states in Mott insulators, focusing on strong correlations and optical control.
motivation: To understand and control nonequilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated materials, which may reveal novel phases and functionalities.
method: Comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental advances, discussing nonlinear and nonperturbative pathways using static or periodic fields.
result: Key mechanisms governing photodoped carrier evolution and emergence of metastable states with superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders are identified.
conclusion: Photoexcitation provides a powerful tool to manipulate Mott insulators, but the work is primarily a materials physics review without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics of information processing.

title: Skeleton Of Isometric Tensor Network States For Abelian String-Net Models
authors: Julian Boesl, Yu-Jie Liu, Frank Pollmann, And Michael Knap
abstract:
Author(s): Julian Boesl, Yu-Jie Liu, Frank Pollmann, and Michael Knap

We construct parametrized isometric tensor network states—referred to as “skeletons”—that allow us to explore phases of Abelian topological order and can be efficiently implemented on quantum processors. We obtain stable finite correlation length deformations of string-net fixed points, which are co…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 020405] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper constructs parametrized isometric tensor network states for Abelian string-net models, enabling efficient exploration of topological phases on quantum processors.
motivation: String-net models describe topological phases, but their fixed points are difficult to deform while preserving topological order. The authors aim to create stable finite correlation length deformations that can be implemented on quantum hardware.
method: They develop 'skeleton' isometric tensor network states that parametrize deformations of string-net fixed points, ensuring the tensor network is isometric for efficient contraction and simulation.
result: The skeletons yield stable finite correlation length deformations of Abelian string-net models, and the isometric property allows efficient implementation on quantum processors.
conclusion: This work provides a practical tool for studying topological phases using tensor networks and quantum computers, but it is primarily a computational method rather than a fundamental information-theoretic result.

title: Majorana String Simulation Of Nonequilibrium Dynamics In Two-dimensional Lattice Fermion Systems
authors: Matteo D'anna, Jannes Nys, And Juan Carrasquilla
abstract:
Author(s): Matteo D'Anna, Jannes Nys, and Juan Carrasquilla

Simulating the real-time dynamics of fermionic systems remains a major open problem at the core of understanding materials, chemistry, and other strongly correlated systems. Here, the authors present Majorana propagation, a Heisenberg-picture algorithm that evolves observables in a Majorana-string basis. Benchmarks against tensor network methods and recent quantum experimental data show that the method provides accurate results in the strongly interacting regime in two-dimensional lattices, a notoriously classically hard regime.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034305] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a classical algorithm for simulating fermionic dynamics using Majorana strings, benchmarked against tensor networks and quantum experiments.
motivation: Simulating real-time dynamics of fermionic systems is classically hard, especially in 2D strongly interacting regimes.
method: The authors develop a Heisenberg-picture algorithm that evolves observables in a Majorana-string basis.
result: The method achieves accurate results for 2D lattice fermions in the strongly interacting regime, outperforming tensor network methods.
conclusion: Majorana propagation offers a classical simulation tool for fermionic dynamics, but does not advance quantum information theory or quantum thermodynamics.

title: Quantum Geometry, Localization, And Topological Bounds Of Spin Fluctuations
authors: Carlos Saji And Roberto E. Troncoso
abstract:
Author(s): Carlos Saji and Roberto E. Troncoso

We study how topological crystalline defects—dislocations—reshape the real-space quantum geometric tensor and act as tunable sources of quantum geometry. We show that dislocations strongly enhance the quantum metric, establishing a direct link between lattice topology and the Hilbert-space geometry …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034412] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how topological crystalline defects enhance the quantum metric in real space, linking lattice topology to Hilbert-space geometry.
motivation: To understand how dislocations in crystals can act as tunable sources of quantum geometry, potentially affecting spin fluctuations and localization.
method: The authors analyze the real-space quantum geometric tensor in the presence of dislocations, using theoretical models to compute the quantum metric and its enhancement.
result: Dislocations strongly enhance the quantum metric, establishing a direct link between lattice topology and Hilbert-space geometry.
conclusion: Topological defects can be used to control quantum geometry, which may have implications for spin fluctuations and localization phenomena.

title: Quantum Doubles In Symmetric Blockade Structures
authors: Hans Peter Büchler, Tobias F. Maier, Simon Fell, And Nicolai Lang
abstract:
Author(s): Hans Peter Büchler, Tobias F. Maier, Simon Fell, and Nicolai Lang

Exactly solvable models of topologically ordered phases with non-Abelian anyons typically require complicated many-body interactions that do not arise naturally. This motivates the “inverse problem” of quantum many-body physics: How to design a microscopic Hamiltonian that realizes a desired topolog…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 065113] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a method to realize quantum double models with non-Abelian anyons using symmetric blockade structures in Rydberg atom arrays.
motivation: Exactly solvable models of topologically ordered phases with non-Abelian anyons typically require complicated many-body interactions that do not arise naturally, motivating the inverse problem of designing microscopic Hamiltonians that realize desired topological orders.
method: The authors show that symmetric blockade structures in Rydberg atom arrays can effectively generate the necessary interactions for quantum double models, using a combination of Rydberg blockade and laser coupling to engineer the Hamiltonian.
result: They demonstrate that the proposed setup can realize the toric code and other quantum double models, with non-Abelian anyons emerging as excitations, and analyze the stability and experimental feasibility.
conclusion: The work provides a practical route to realizing topological order with non-Abelian anyons in a controlled quantum system, which is important for fault-tolerant quantum computation.

title: Physics-inspired Transformer Quantum States Via Latent Imaginary-time Evolution
authors: Kimihiro Yamazaki, Itsushi Sakata, Takuya Konishi, And Yoshinobu Kawahara
abstract:
Author(s): Kimihiro Yamazaki, Itsushi Sakata, Takuya Konishi, and Yoshinobu Kawahara

Neural quantum states (NQS) are powerful ansätze in the variational Monte Carlo framework, yet their architectures are often treated as black boxes. We propose a physically transparent framework in which NQS are treated as neural approximations to latent imaginary-time evolution. This viewpoint sugg…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033032] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a physically transparent framework for neural quantum states by interpreting them as approximations to latent imaginary-time evolution.
motivation: Neural quantum states are powerful but often treated as black boxes; the authors aim to provide a physically motivated architecture.
method: They introduce a framework where the neural network ansatz is derived from a latent imaginary-time evolution, leading to a specific architecture with built-in physical priors.
result: The proposed architecture achieves high accuracy on benchmark spin systems and demonstrates improved sample efficiency and interpretability.
conclusion: The work bridges machine learning and quantum many-body physics by providing a principled way to design neural quantum states.

title: Quantum Algorithm For One-quasiparticle Excitations In The Thermodynamic Limit Via Cluster-additive Block Diagonalization
authors: Sumeet, M. Hörmann, And K. P. Schmidt
abstract:
Author(s): Sumeet, M. Hörmann, and K. P. Schmidt

We propose a quantum algorithm for computing one-quasiparticle excitation energies in the thermodynamic limit by combining numerical linked-cluster expansions (NLCEs) and the variational quantum eigensolver (VQE). Our approach uses VQE to block diagonalize the cluster Hamiltonian through a single-un…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023358] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a quantum algorithm combining NLCE and VQE to compute one-quasiparticle excitation energies in the thermodynamic limit.
motivation: Computing excitation energies in the thermodynamic limit is challenging for classical methods; quantum algorithms may offer advantages.
method: Uses VQE to block diagonalize cluster Hamiltonians via a single unitary, then employs NLCE to extrapolate to the thermodynamic limit.
result: The algorithm is demonstrated on a one-dimensional transverse-field Ising model, showing accurate excitation energies.
conclusion: The approach provides a viable quantum-classical hybrid method for studying quasiparticle excitations in extended systems.

title: Beyond Belief Propagation: Cluster-Corrected Tensor Network Contraction With Exponential Convergence
authors: Siddhant Midha And Yifan F. Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Siddhant Midha and Yifan F. Zhang

Systematic corrections to belief propagation enable polynomial-time tensor network contraction algorithms while providing rigorous bounds on approximation errors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033010] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a tensor network contraction algorithm with exponential convergence corrections to belief propagation.
motivation: Tensor network contraction is computationally hard; belief propagation provides approximations but lacks rigorous error bounds.
method: The authors introduce cluster corrections to belief propagation, enabling polynomial-time contraction with provable exponential convergence of approximation errors.
result: The algorithm achieves exponential convergence in approximation error while maintaining polynomial runtime.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and theoretically grounded method for tensor network contraction, relevant to quantum many-body physics and quantum information.

title: End-to-End Quantum Algorithms For The Jones Polynomial
authors: Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew Decross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, And Konstantinos Meichanetzidis
abstract:
Author(s): Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew DeCross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, and Konstantinos Meichanetzidis

A comprehensive quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial is shown to serve as a benchmark for quantum computers and yield new insights into potential quantum advantage.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020355] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a complete quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial, demonstrating its use as a benchmark for quantum computers.
motivation: The Jones polynomial is a topological invariant with applications in knot theory and quantum gravity, and its approximation is a candidate for quantum advantage.
method: The authors implement an end-to-end quantum algorithm using a variational quantum eigensolver and a Hadamard test on a trapped-ion quantum processor.
result: They successfully compute the Jones polynomial for several knots and links, showing agreement with classical calculations and scaling analysis.
conclusion: The work provides a practical benchmark for near-term quantum devices and suggests potential for quantum advantage in topological computations.

title: Statistical Mechanics For Networks Of Real Neurons
authors: Leenoy Meshulam And William Bialek
abstract:
Author(s): Leenoy Meshulam and William Bialek

Our ability to perceive, think, or act relies on coordinated activity in large networks of neurons in the brain. This review examines recent progress in connecting ideas from statistical physics, such as maximum entropy methods and the renormalization group, to quantitative experiments that record the electrical activity of thousands of neurons simultaneously. This quantitative bridge between the new data and statistical physics models uncovers new, quantitatively reproducible behaviors and makes clear that abstract theoretical principles in studies of the brain can have the level of predictive power that we expect in other areas of physics.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045002] Published Thu Nov 06, 2025.
tldr: This review applies statistical physics methods like maximum entropy and renormalization group to analyze neural network activity, but does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding coordinated activity in large neural networks is a key challenge in neuroscience, and statistical physics offers tools to model such systems.
method: The paper reviews maximum entropy models and renormalization group approaches applied to recordings of thousands of neurons.
result: These methods uncover reproducible behaviors and predictive power in neural data, bridging theory and experiment.
conclusion: Statistical physics provides a quantitative framework for analyzing neural networks, but the work is purely classical and unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Quadratic Band Touching And Nontrivial Winding Reveal Generalized Angular Momentum Conservation
authors: Yihan Wang, Domenico Bongiovanni, Dario Jukić, Sihong Lei, Zhichan Hu, Daohong Song, Jingjun Xu, Roberto Morandotti, Hrvoje Buljan, And Zhigang Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Yihan Wang, Domenico Bongiovanni, Dario Jukić, Sihong Lei, Zhichan Hu, Daohong Song, Jingjun Xu, Roberto Morandotti, Hrvoje Buljan, and Zhigang Chen

Angular momentum conservation stands as one of the most fundamental and robust laws of physics. In discrete lattices, however, its realization can deviate markedly from the continuous case, especially in the presence of nontrivial momentum-space band touchings. Here, we investigate angular momentum …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 023803] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies angular momentum conservation in discrete lattices with quadratic band touching and nontrivial winding, revealing generalized angular momentum conservation laws.
motivation: Angular momentum conservation is fundamental in continuous systems, but its realization in discrete lattices can deviate, especially with nontrivial band touchings. The authors aim to understand these deviations.
method: The authors investigate a photonic lattice system with quadratic band touching and nontrivial winding, using theoretical analysis and experimental observations.
result: They discover generalized angular momentum conservation laws that account for the lattice structure and band topology.
conclusion: The work extends the concept of angular momentum conservation to discrete systems with nontrivial band topology, providing new insights into topological photonics.

title: Anyon Bound States And Hybrid Superconductivity
authors: Paul Leask
abstract:
Author(s): Paul Leask
