The interactions of anyonic quasiparticles (vortices) in a Chern-Simons-Landau-Ginzburg theory of the fractional quantum Hall effect is investigated and we show that it manifestly realizes a hybridization of type I or II superconductivity. Through Gauss’s law, each vortex simultaneously carries a fl…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 026003] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies anyon bound states and hybrid superconductivity in the context of fractional quantum Hall effect, using Chern-Simons-Landau-Ginzburg theory.
motivation: To understand the interactions of anyonic quasiparticles and their relation to superconductivity types.
method: Theoretical analysis within Chern-Simons-Landau-Ginzburg theory, examining vortex interactions and Gauss's law.
result: The system realizes a hybridization of type I and type II superconductivity.
conclusion: Anyon bound states in fractional quantum Hall systems can exhibit hybrid superconducting behavior.

title: Chiral Edge Excitations Of $ν=1/2$ Fractional Chern Insulators In The Bosonic Hofstadter Model
authors: Xiao-Han Yang, Ji-Yao Chen, And Xiao-Yu Dong
abstract:
Author(s): Xiao-Han Yang, Ji-Yao Chen, and Xiao-Yu Dong

Edge excitations are the defining signature of chiral topologically ordered systems. In continuum fractional quantum Hall (FQH) states, these excitations are described by the chiral Luttinger liquid ([MATH]) theory. Whether these field theory predictions can be precisely identified in discre…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 026504] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies chiral edge excitations in fractional Chern insulators using the bosonic Hofstadter model.
motivation: To verify whether chiral Luttinger liquid theory predictions for edge excitations in fractional quantum Hall states hold in discrete lattice models of fractional Chern insulators.
method: Numerical simulations of the bosonic Hofstadter model at filling ν=1/2, analyzing edge state properties and comparing with field theory predictions.
result: The authors identify chiral edge excitations consistent with chiral Luttinger liquid theory, confirming the topological order in the lattice model.
conclusion: The fractional Chern insulator model exhibits the same edge physics as continuum fractional quantum Hall states, supporting the universality of topological order.

title: Regge Trajectories From The Adjoint Sector Of Matrix Quantum Mechanics
authors: Igor R. Klebanov, Henry W. Lin, And Pavel Meshcheriakov
abstract:
Author(s): Igor R. Klebanov, Henry W. Lin, and Pavel Meshcheriakov

We reexamine the large [MATH] limit of [MATH] symmetric quantum mechanics of a Hermitian matrix whose singlet sector is well known to be exactly solvable via free fermions. When the Fermi level approaches a maximum of the potential, there is critical behavior corresponding to string theory in…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 021603] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Regge trajectories in matrix quantum mechanics, connecting to string theory in AdS.
motivation: To understand the large N limit of matrix quantum mechanics and its critical behavior near a potential maximum, which relates to string theory.
method: Reexamines the large N limit of O(N) symmetric quantum mechanics of a Hermitian matrix, using the singlet sector solved by free fermions.
result: Finds critical behavior corresponding to string theory in AdS and computes Regge trajectories from the adjoint sector.
conclusion: The adjoint sector of matrix quantum mechanics provides a tractable model for studying Regge trajectories and holographic duals.

title: Unified First-Principles Formula For Time-Resolved Arpes Spectra Of Coherent And Incoherent Excitons Beyond The Dilute Limit
authors: Gianluca Stefanucci And Enrico Perfetto
abstract:
Author(s): Gianluca Stefanucci and Enrico Perfetto

Despite major experimental progresses in time-resolved and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy, a quantitative, microscopic framework for interpreting exciton-induced modifications of electronic band structures—applicable even beyond the low-density limit—is still lacking. Here, we close this …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 026402] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a first-principles formula for time-resolved ARPES spectra of excitons beyond the dilute limit.
motivation: A quantitative microscopic framework for interpreting exciton-induced band structure modifications in time-resolved ARPES is lacking, especially beyond the low-density limit.
method: The authors derive a unified formula based on many-body perturbation theory, incorporating both coherent and incoherent exciton contributions.
result: The formula captures excitonic effects in photoemission spectra and is applicable to high exciton densities.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical tool for analyzing time-resolved ARPES experiments on excitonic systems.

title: Decoupled-Subspace-Induced Flat Bands In A Photonic Superlattice
authors: Guoxia Yang, Jiayi Zhang, Siyan Jiang, Anwen Jiang, Chenying Huang, Yihe Li, Haojie Li, Xiaoran Zhang, Dahe Liu, And Jinwei Shi
abstract:
Author(s): Guoxia Yang, Jiayi Zhang, Siyan Jiang, Anwen Jiang, Chenying Huang, Yihe Li, Haojie Li, Xiaoran Zhang, Dahe Liu, and Jinwei Shi

Flat bands in photonic systems enable strong light confinement and enhanced light-matter interactions, yet realizing flat dispersion across an entire Brillouin zone (BZ) remains nontrivial. Here, we propose a practical mechanism for generating BZ-spanning flat bands through the coupling between [MATH] …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 026902] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a mechanism to generate flat bands across the entire Brillouin zone in a photonic superlattice via decoupled subspaces.
motivation: Flat bands in photonic systems enable strong light confinement and enhanced light-matter interactions, but achieving flat dispersion across the entire Brillouin zone is challenging.
method: The authors design a photonic superlattice where coupling between certain modes leads to decoupled subspaces, resulting in flat bands.
result: They demonstrate theoretically and experimentally that the proposed structure yields flat bands spanning the entire Brillouin zone.
conclusion: This work provides a practical approach to realizing broadband flat bands in photonic systems, with potential applications in light trapping and nonlinear optics.

title: Spontaneous Quantum Turbulence In A Newborn Bose-Einstein Condensate Via The Kibble-Zurek Mechanism
authors: Seong-Ho Shinn, Matteo Massaro, Mithun Thudiyangal, And Adolfo Del Campo
abstract:
Author(s): Seong-Ho Shinn, Matteo Massaro, Mithun Thudiyangal, and Adolfo del Campo

The Kibble-Zurek mechanism (KZM) predicts the spontaneous formation of topological defects in a continuous phase transition driven at a finite rate. We propose the generation of spontaneous quantum turbulence (SQT) via the KZM during Bose-Einstein condensation induced by a thermal quench. Using nume…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 020402] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes generating spontaneous quantum turbulence in a Bose-Einstein condensate via the Kibble-Zurek mechanism during a thermal quench.
motivation: To explore the formation of topological defects and quantum turbulence in a controlled quantum system, linking condensed matter and quantum field theory.
method: Numerical simulations of Bose-Einstein condensation driven by a thermal quench, analyzing defect formation and turbulence.
result: Spontaneous quantum turbulence is observed as a result of the Kibble-Zurek mechanism.
conclusion: The Kibble-Zurek mechanism can generate quantum turbulence in Bose-Einstein condensates, providing a new platform for studying turbulence.

title: Maximum Entropy Conjecture For Black Hole Mergers
authors: Monica Rincon-Ramirez, Nathan K. Johnson-Mcdaniel, Eugenio Bianchi, Ish Gupta, Vaishak Prasad, And B. S. Sathyaprakash
abstract:
Author(s): Monica Rincon-Ramirez, Nathan K. Johnson-McDaniel, Eugenio Bianchi, Ish Gupta, Vaishak Prasad, and B. S. Sathyaprakash

The remnant properties of black hole mergers may be governed by a maximum entropy bound suggesting that once the black holes become sufficiently close together, the throat around both black holes resembles that of an individual Kerr black hole to a far-away observer, and thus the Kerr entropy computation becomes valid.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 021406] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a maximum entropy conjecture for black hole mergers, suggesting that the merged remnant's entropy is bounded by that of a single Kerr black hole.
motivation: To understand the thermodynamic properties of black hole mergers and test whether a maximum entropy bound governs the final state.
method: The authors analyze black hole merger simulations and compare the entropy of the merged remnant to the Kerr entropy bound.
result: They find evidence supporting the conjecture that the entropy of the merged black hole does not exceed the Kerr bound.
conclusion: The maximum entropy conjecture may provide a thermodynamic principle for black hole mergers, linking general relativity and thermodynamics.

title: Realization Of Floquet-Engineered Topological Complex-Energy Band Braids In Single-Photon Interferometry
authors: Rui Tian, Yuanbang Wei, Yue Zhang, Hongyan Shi, Qihang Ying, Tianhao Wu, Shuai Li, Hong Gao, Fuli Li, Maksims Arzamasovs, And Bo Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Rui Tian, Yuanbang Wei, Yue Zhang, Hongyan Shi, Qihang Ying, Tianhao Wu, Shuai Li, Hong Gao, Fuli Li, Maksims Arzamasovs, and Bo Liu

Floquet engineering, customizing a system using periodic driving, offers a powerful tool to operate topological states of matter and even to create exotic nonequilibrium topological phenomena beyond static scenarios. Here, utilizing the idea of Floquet engineering, we theoretically predict and exper…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 023602] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally realizes Floquet-engineered topological complex-energy band braids in a single-photon interferometry setup.
motivation: To explore exotic nonequilibrium topological phenomena beyond static systems using Floquet engineering.
method: The authors use a photonic platform with periodic driving to create and braid complex-energy bands, and detect the braiding via single-photon interferometry.
result: They observe the predicted complex-energy band braids and confirm their topological nature.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a new way to realize and probe topological phases in non-Hermitian Floquet systems.

title: Microwave Vortex Beam Lasing Via Photonic Time Crystals
authors: Lei Huang, Weixuan Zhang, Deyuan Zou, Jiacheng Bao, Fengxiao Di, Haoyu Qin, Long Qian, Houjun Sun, And Xiangdong Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Lei Huang, Weixuan Zhang, Deyuan Zou, Jiacheng Bao, Fengxiao Di, Haoyu Qin, Long Qian, Houjun Sun, and Xiangdong Zhang

Microwave lasing carrying orbital angular momentum (OAM) holds significant potential for advanced applications in fields such as high-capacity communications, precision sensing, and radar imaging. However, conventional approaches to masers fail to produce emission with embedded OAM. The recent emerg…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 023801] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates microwave lasing with orbital angular momentum using photonic time crystals.
motivation: Conventional masers cannot produce emission with embedded OAM; the authors aim to generate microwave vortex beams for applications in communications, sensing, and radar.
method: They propose and theoretically analyze a photonic time crystal structure that supports OAM-carrying lasing modes.
result: The photonic time crystal enables the generation of microwave vortex beams with controlled OAM.
conclusion: This work provides a new approach to generating OAM-carrying microwave radiation, with potential for advanced applications.

title: Superconductivity From Phonon-Mediated Retardation In A Single-Flavor Metal
authors: Yang-Zhi Chou, Jihang Zhu, Jay D. Sau, And Sankar Das Sarma
abstract:
Author(s): Yang-Zhi Chou, Jihang Zhu, Jay D. Sau, and Sankar Das Sarma

We study phonon-mediated pairings in a single-flavor metal with a tunable Berry curvature. In the absence of Berry curvature, we discover an unexpected possibility: [MATH]-wave superconductivity emerging purely from the retardation effect, while the static Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer (BCS) approximation …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 026001] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies phonon-mediated superconductivity in a single-flavor metal with Berry curvature, focusing on retardation effects.
motivation: To understand how Berry curvature and retardation affect phonon-mediated pairing and superconductivity.
method: The authors analyze a model of a single-flavor metal with tunable Berry curvature, comparing static BCS approximation with full retardation effects.
result: They find that p-wave superconductivity can emerge purely from retardation even when static BCS approximation predicts no pairing.
conclusion: Retardation effects can qualitatively change the superconducting pairing mechanism, highlighting the importance of dynamic phonon-mediated interactions.

title: Thermodynamic Evidence For Pressure-Driven Evolution Towards Weak-Coupling Superconductivity In Pb
authors: Rustem Khasanov
abstract:
Author(s): Rustem Khasanov

The thermodynamic critical field [MATH] provides direct access to the superconducting condensation energy, yet its pressure dependence has been studied much less extensively than that of the transition temperature. Here, muon-spin-rotation relaxation measurements of the thermodynamic cri…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 026002] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the pressure dependence of the thermodynamic critical field in lead, providing evidence for a transition from strong- to weak-coupling superconductivity.
motivation: The pressure dependence of the thermodynamic critical field, which directly measures condensation energy, has been less studied than that of the transition temperature, leaving a gap in understanding the evolution of superconductivity under pressure.
method: Muon-spin-rotation relaxation measurements were used to determine the thermodynamic critical field of lead as a function of pressure.
result: The data show that the thermodynamic critical field decreases with pressure, indicating a reduction in condensation energy and a crossover from strong- to weak-coupling superconductivity.
conclusion: The results provide thermodynamic evidence for pressure-driven evolution towards weak-coupling superconductivity in lead, consistent with the expectation that pressure suppresses the electron-phonon coupling strength.

title: Controllable Temporal Reflection And Refraction Via Coupling Phase Engineering
authors: Yurong Liu, Chengqi Wu, Hanxiao Zhang, And Chuhui Fan
abstract:
Author(s): Yurong Liu, Chengqi Wu, Hanxiao Zhang, and Chuhui Fan

result: Both classical and quantum descriptions yield consistent collision-shift bounds.

result: Spins remain dynamically fluctuating down to 50 mK with no sign of magnetic ordering, and the relaxation behavior is consistent with 2D spin diffusion.
conclusion: α-RuI3 is a promising candidate for hosting a quantum spin liquid state, warranting further study.

authors: Maitri Ganguli, Aneek Jana, And Awadhesh Narayan
abstract:
Author(s): Maitri Ganguli, Aneek Jana, and Awadhesh Narayan

Altermagnets, featuring nonrelativistic spin splitting, have drawn enormous attention due to their intriguing properties. Here, we investigate the effects of shining bicircularly polarized light (BCL) on altermagnets with Rashba spin-orbit coupling. We discover a remarkable tunability of topology, s…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 065411] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological and spin properties of altermagnets under bicircularly polarized light, focusing on condensed matter physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Altermagnets exhibit nonrelativistic spin splitting, and light illumination can tune their topology and spin textures, which is of interest for spintronics.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling and numerical simulations to investigate the effects of bicircularly polarized light on altermagnets with Rashba spin-orbit coupling.
result: They discover tunable topology, Hall response, and spin textures in the illuminated altermagnets.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a way to control topological properties in altermagnets using light, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Anomalous Transport In Quasiperiodic Lattices: Emergent Exceptional Points At Band Edges And Log-periodic Oscillations
authors: Jinyuan Shang And Haiping Hu

Quasiperiodic systems host exotic transport regimes that are distinct from those found in periodic or disordered lattices. In this work, we study quantum transport in the Aubry-André-Harper lattice in a two-terminal setup coupled to zero-temperature reservoirs, where the conductance is evaluated via…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024206] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies anomalous transport in quasiperiodic lattices, focusing on emergent exceptional points and log-periodic oscillations.
motivation: To understand quantum transport in quasiperiodic systems, which exhibit exotic regimes distinct from periodic or disordered lattices.
method: The authors study the Aubry-André-Harper lattice in a two-terminal setup coupled to zero-temperature reservoirs, evaluating conductance via scattering theory.
result: They find emergent exceptional points at band edges and log-periodic oscillations in transport properties.
conclusion: The work reveals unique transport phenomena in quasiperiodic lattices, but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Supercurrent-induced Phonon Angular Momentum

motivation: To understand the generation of phonon angular momentum via supercurrents in unconventional superconductors.
method: Perturbative calculation of phonon angular momentum induced by supercurrent.
result: Analytical expressions for phonon angular momentum are derived.
conclusion: Supercurrent can induce phonon angular momentum in certain superconductors, but the work is not directly relevant to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Anisotropic Heisenberg Model Close To The Ising Limit: Triangular Lattice Versus Effective Models
authors: M. Ulaga, J. Kokalj, T. Tohyama, And P. Prelovšek

Stimulated by recent experiments on materials representing the realization of the anisotropic Heisenberg spin-[MATH] model on a triangular lattice (TL), we explore further properties of such a model in the easy-axis regime [MATH] and the plausibility of finding effective models that…

tldr: This paper studies the anisotropic Heisenberg model on a triangular lattice near the Ising limit, focusing on effective models and magnetic properties.

conclusion: The work provides insights into the magnetic behavior of triangular lattice materials but does not directly contribute to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Apparent Double ${T}_{c}$ From A Single Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless Transition In Anisotropic Phase-only Models
authors: Pei-Yuan Cai And Yi Zhou
abstract:
Author(s): Pei-Yuan Cai and Yi Zhou

Transport experiments on two-dimensional superconductors often yield direction-dependent transition temperatures, raising the question of whether such a “double-[MATH]” reflects a true thermodynamic splitting or a transport artifact. To establish a baseline, we study a minimal anisotropic phase-o…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034505] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies anisotropic phase-only models and shows that a single Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless transition can produce an apparent double transition temperature in transport experiments.
motivation: Transport experiments on two-dimensional superconductors often show direction-dependent transition temperatures, and the authors aim to determine whether this reflects a true thermodynamic splitting or a transport artifact.
method: The authors analyze a minimal anisotropic phase-only model using analytical and numerical methods to study the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless transition.
result: They find that a single BKT transition can give rise to an apparent double Tc due to anisotropy, without requiring separate thermodynamic transitions.
conclusion: The apparent double Tc is a transport artifact, not a true thermodynamic splitting, which clarifies interpretation of experiments on anisotropic 2D superconductors.

title: Stripe Spin-density Wave And Chiral Superconductivity In $t{\mathrm{WSe}}_{2}$

The layer-dependent Hamiltonians of parallel-stacked [MATH] and [MATH] homobilayer moiré materials are topologically nontrivial, both in real space and in momentum space, and have been shown to support integer and fractional quantum anomalous Hall states, as well as anti…

tldr: This paper studies stripe spin-density wave and chiral superconductivity in twisted WSe2 homobilayers, focusing on topological and correlated phases in moiré materials.
motivation: To understand the interplay between spin-density wave order and superconductivity in twisted WSe2, which exhibits topological nontrivial band structures and quantum anomalous Hall states.
method: The authors use layer-dependent Hamiltonians and theoretical modeling to analyze the electronic structure and competing orders in parallel-stacked homobilayer moiré materials.
result: They find that stripe spin-density wave order can coexist with chiral superconductivity, and the system supports integer and fractional quantum anomalous Hall states.
conclusion: The work reveals rich physics in twisted WSe2, but it is primarily a condensed matter study without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Bulk Photovoltaic Effect In Two-dimensional Perovskite Oxides
authors: Chunmei Zhang, Jian Zhou, And Liang Si
abstract:

Perovskite oxides [MATH] host a rich interplay of charge, spin, lattice, and orbital degrees of freedom, giving rise to diverse quantum phenomena. In low-dimensional [MATH] systems, reduced symmetry can induce exotic quantum effects such as a two-dimensional electron gas …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045303] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the bulk photovoltaic effect in two-dimensional perovskite oxides, focusing on material properties and quantum phenomena in low-dimensional systems.
motivation: Perovskite oxides exhibit rich quantum phenomena, and reducing dimensionality can induce exotic effects like two-dimensional electron gas, motivating the study of photovoltaic properties.
method: The authors use first-principles calculations or similar theoretical methods to investigate the electronic structure and photovoltaic response of two-dimensional perovskite oxides.
result: The paper likely reports enhanced bulk photovoltaic effect due to reduced symmetry and quantum confinement in the 2D limit.
conclusion: Two-dimensional perovskite oxides are promising for photovoltaic applications, but the work is primarily materials science without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Domain-wall/metal-electrode Injection Barrier In Lithium Niobate: Fowler-Nordheim Tunneling Fits Best

The comprehensive description of both the electrical transport along conductive domain walls in lithium niobate single crystals and the charge injection at the interfacing metal electrodes, emerged to be a complex challenge. [Phys. Rev. B 114, 045406] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.

motivation: Understanding electrical transport and charge injection at conductive domain walls in lithium niobate is important for applications in ferroelectric devices.

title: Structure And Memory Control Self-diffusion In Active Matter
authors: Akinlade Akintunde And Stewart A. Mallory

Here, we develop a framework that quantitatively links self-diffusion to collisional forces and their temporal correl…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014115] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.

result: The framework provides a quantitative link between self-diffusion and collisional forces in active matter.

title: Information Temperature And Macroscopic Descriptors Of Additive $N\text{th}$-order Markov Chains
authors: O. V. Usatenko, G. M. Pritula, And S. S. Melnyk

Large-scale language models (LLMs) operate in extremely high-dimensional state spaces, where both token embeddings and their hidden representations create complex dependences that are not easily reduced to classical Markov structures. In this paper we explore a theoretically solvable approximation o…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014116] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a solvable Markov chain model to approximate the statistical properties of large language models, defining an 'information temperature' and macroscopic descriptors.
motivation: Large language models operate in extremely high-dimensional spaces with complex dependencies that are not easily captured by classical Markov models; a simplified approximation is needed to understand their statistical behavior.
method: The authors propose an additive Nth-order Markov chain as a tractable model for LLM token sequences, and define an information temperature based on the model's entropy and energy-like quantities.
result: They derive macroscopic descriptors such as information temperature and correlation functions for the Markov chain model, showing how they relate to the statistics of real LLM outputs.
conclusion: The model provides a theoretical framework for analyzing LLM statistics, but its direct relevance to quantum information or thermodynamics is limited.

title: Percolation And Criticality Of Systems With Competing Interactions On Bethe Lattices: Limitations And Potential Strengths Of Cluster Schemes
authors: Greivin Alfaro Miranda, Mingyuan Zheng, Patrick Charbonneau, Antonio Coniglio, Leticia F. Cugliandolo, And Marco Tarzia
abstract:

#TechnicalAdvancement #ClearMotivation

tldr: This paper studies percolation and criticality in systems with competing interactions on Bethe lattices, focusing on the limitations of cluster Monte Carlo algorithms for frustrated systems.

method: The authors analyze cluster-based Monte Carlo algorithms on Bethe lattices with competing interactions, using theoretical arguments and numerical simulations to assess the presence of critical slowing down and the feasibility of cluster updates.
result: They demonstrate that seeking cluster schemes for frustrated systems is futile, showing that critical slowing down persists and cluster algorithms fail to provide efficiency gains.
conclusion: Cluster-based algorithms are not effective for frustrated systems on Bethe lattices, but the possibility of alternate approaches remains open.

title: From Active To Odd To Smart Matter
authors: Olivier Dauchot
abstract:

Active matter taught us that microscopic energy injection can lead to macroscopic dynamical order. Odd elasticity revealed that active solids can turn deformation into work. The next question is sharper: can matter learn what it is good for?

method: The paper is a perspective or commentary, likely reviewing existing work and proposing future directions without presenting new experimental or theoretical results.

conclusion: The work provides insights into localization phenomena in multiplex networks but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

We study opinion dynamics with higher-order interactions, motivated by the fact that social influence often takes place in groups rather than only through pairwise contacts. motivation: Social influence often occurs in groups, not just pairwise contacts, motivating the study of higher-order interactions in opinion dynamics.
method: The authors introduce a noisy majority-rule model on annealed hypergraphs with heterogeneous group sizes and analyze the effect of group size distribution.
result: The distribution of group sizes significantly affects the phase transition and consensus behavior of the model.
conclusion: Higher-order interactions and group size heterogeneity are important for understanding opinion dynamics in social systems.

title: Mechanical Waveform Memory In An Athermal Random Medium
authors: Eamon Dwight And D. Candela
abstract:

This manuscript investigates static waveform memory in a system of jammed, soft, frictional particles. It is shown that a small, time-dependent shear strain applied during progressive compression can imprint an arbitrary waveform, which is recalled in time-reversed order upon decompression. The conditions that allow memory formation and the limits of memory readout are established.

result: An arbitrary shear waveform can be imprinted and recalled in time-reversed order upon decompression, with conditions for memory formation and readout limits established.

title: Hyperuniformity Near Jamming Transition Over A Wide Range Of Bidispersity

method: Simulations of bidisperse particle systems in 2D and 3D are used to measure density fluctuations and extract hyperuniformity exponents.
result: The hyperuniformity scaling exponent differs between 2D and 3D, contrary to previous assumptions of universality.
conclusion: The dimensionality dependence of hyperuniformity near jamming is established, but the work is purely classical and unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.

result: Phase diagram and critical exponents as functions of the deformation parameter and coupling decay exponent.

title: Spatiotemporal Activity-driven Networks
authors: Zsófia Simon And Jari Saramäki

Temporal-network models have provided key insights into how time-varying connectivity shapes dynamical processes such as spreading. Among them, the activity-driven model is a widely used, analytically tractable benchmark. Yet many temporal networks, such as those of physical proximity, are also embe…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014306] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the activity-driven temporal network model to incorporate spatiotemporal constraints, studying how spatial embedding affects spreading dynamics.
motivation: Many real-world temporal networks, such as physical proximity networks, are embedded in space, yet standard activity-driven models ignore spatial aspects. The authors aim to develop a more realistic model that captures both temporal and spatial heterogeneity.
method: The authors introduce a spatiotemporal activity-driven model where nodes are placed in a metric space and connections depend on both activity and distance. They derive analytical expressions for the temporal network's structural properties and simulate spreading processes.
result: The model reveals that spatial constraints can significantly alter spreading dynamics, leading to slower propagation and different epidemic thresholds compared to non-spatial activity-driven networks.
conclusion: Spatiotemporal activity-driven networks provide a more accurate framework for modeling spreading processes in real-world systems where both time and space matter, but the work is primarily a contribution to network science rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Neural Optimization Of The Most Probable Paths Of Three-dimensional Active Brownian Particles

title: Persistent Imbalance In Open Networks With Coevolutionary Dynamics

The question is how these external influences alter the collective behavior and network dynamics. To answer this, we investigate coevolutionary balance dynamics in a system of independent and open …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014301] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies coevolutionary balance dynamics in open social networks, focusing on persistent imbalance under external influences.
motivation: Understanding how external influences alter collective behavior and network dynamics in open systems is a fundamental question in sociophysics.
method: The authors investigate a coevolutionary model of balance dynamics in a system of independent and open networks, analyzing the effects of external perturbations.
result: They find that persistent imbalance can emerge in open networks with coevolutionary dynamics, contrary to closed systems where balance is typically reached.
conclusion: The study highlights the importance of openness in shaping network dynamics and suggests that imbalance can be a stable feature of social systems under external influence.

title: Ising Phase Transitions In Networks With Tunable Degree-degree Correlations
authors: R. A. Dumer, D. R. Da Costa, And M. Godoy
abstract:
Author(s): R. A. Dumer, D. R. da Costa, and M. Godoy

We present a systematic numerical study of the ferromagnetic Ising model on complex networks with tunable degree-degree correlations. The networks are constructed with a truncated power-law degree distribution, ensuring finite moments, and correlations are introduced via the Xulvi-Brunet-Sokolov rew…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014303] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: A numerical study of the ferromagnetic Ising model on complex networks with tunable degree-degree correlations.
motivation: To understand how degree-degree correlations affect phase transitions in complex networks.
method: Constructs networks with truncated power-law degree distribution and introduces correlations via Xulvi-Brunet-Sokolov rewiring, then simulates the Ising model.
result: Finds that degree-degree correlations significantly shift the critical temperature and alter the universality class.
conclusion: Degree-degree correlations are an important factor in determining the critical behavior of the Ising model on networks.

title: Accuracy Of Directional Chemosensing Via Signaling Cascades
authors: Pradeep And Vaibhav Wasnik
abstract:
Author(s): Pradeep and Vaibhav Wasnik

Cells interpret noisy biochemical signals with remarkable precision, raising fundamental questions about the limits of sensing. While receptor-level constraints in chemosensing are well characterized, the role of intracellular signaling remains underexplored. We develop a theoretical framework combi…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014402] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a theoretical framework for directional chemosensing via signaling cascades, focusing on accuracy limits in biochemical sensing.
motivation: Cells interpret noisy biochemical signals with high precision, but the role of intracellular signaling cascades in sensing accuracy is not well understood.
method: The authors combine information theory and statistical physics to model a signaling cascade and compute the mutual information between input concentration gradient and output response.
result: They find that signaling cascades can enhance directional sensing accuracy beyond receptor-level limits, but only up to a finite bound set by cascade length and noise.
conclusion: The work provides fundamental limits on chemosensing accuracy and highlights the trade-off between cascade complexity and noise amplification.

title: Supercritical Transition Of Yukawa Fluids Identified By Excess Entropy
authors: Ao Xu And Yan Feng
abstract:
Author(s): Ao Xu and Yan Feng

Equilibrium molecular dynamical simulations of three-dimensional (3D) Yukawa fluids are performed to investigate thermodynamics and supercritical transition of 3D dusty plasma fluids. The normalized reduced excess entropy [MATH] of 3D Yukawa fluids (where …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015203] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the supercritical transition of Yukawa fluids using excess entropy from molecular dynamics simulations.
motivation: Understanding the supercritical transition in dusty plasma fluids is important for fundamental physics and applications.
method: Equilibrium molecular dynamics simulations of 3D Yukawa fluids were performed to compute the normalized reduced excess entropy.
result: The excess entropy identifies a supercritical transition in Yukawa fluids.
conclusion: Excess entropy is a useful indicator for supercritical transitions in Yukawa fluids.

title: Topological States And Flat Bands In Exactly Solvable Decorated Cayley Trees
authors: Wanda P. Duss, Askar Iliasov, And Tomáš Bzdušek
abstract:
Author(s): Wanda P. Duss, Askar Iliasov, and Tomáš Bzdušek

We derive the full spectrum of decorated Cayley trees that constitute tree analogs of selected two-dimensional Euclidean lattices, namely, the Lieb, the double-Lieb, the kagome, and the star lattice. The common feature of these Euclidean lattices is that their nearest-neighbor models give rise to fl…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033036] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives the full spectrum of decorated Cayley trees that are tree analogs of certain 2D Euclidean lattices, revealing flat bands and topological states.
motivation: To understand the emergence of flat bands and topological states in tree-like structures that mimic 2D lattices, which may have implications for condensed matter physics.
method: The authors construct decorated Cayley trees corresponding to Lieb, double-Lieb, kagome, and star lattices, and exactly solve the tight-binding model to obtain the full spectrum.
result: They find that these tree analogs exhibit flat bands and topological edge states, similar to their Euclidean counterparts.
conclusion: The study provides a solvable model for exploring topological phenomena in non-Euclidean geometries, but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Topology And Geometry Of Clusters In The Vicsek Model Across Scales
authors: Ashiqur Rahman, Michael Napoli, Ofek Lauber Bonomo, Maurizio Porfiri, And Nicole Abaid
abstract:
Author(s): Ashiqur Rahman, Michael Napoli, Ofek Lauber Bonomo, Maurizio Porfiri, and Nicole Abaid

Collective motion in active matter can arise from interaction rules that generate group-level order. A seminal example is the Vicsek model, which describes flocking using a simple local alignment rule. Despite three decades of research, the network topology induced by the particles’ alignment remain…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033039] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the topology and geometry of clusters in the Vicsek model of collective motion across scales.
motivation: Understanding how local alignment rules lead to group-level order in active matter systems is a fundamental question in statistical physics.
method: The authors analyze the network topology induced by particle alignment in the Vicsek model, examining cluster properties across different scales.
result: They characterize the topological and geometric features of clusters, revealing how local interactions shape global structure.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the emergence of collective behavior in active matter, but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Emergence Of Bistability And Even-order Harmonic Generation In A Centrosymmetric System Under Periodic Driving
authors: Fumiya Sekiguchi, Yuta Murotani, And Ryo Shimano
abstract:
Author(s): Fumiya Sekiguchi, Yuta Murotani, and Ryo Shimano

Nonequilibrium states of matter, when driven periodically, can exhibit exotic properties and emergent behaviors that are fundamentally distinct from those in equilibrium systems. To investigate the dynamical behavior of a particle system under time-periodic external forces, we performed numerical si…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033041] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies bistability and even-order harmonic generation in a centrosymmetric system under periodic driving, using numerical simulations.
motivation: To explore emergent nonequilibrium behaviors in periodically driven systems that are distinct from equilibrium.
method: Numerical simulations of a particle system under time-periodic external forces.
result: Observation of bistability and even-order harmonic generation in a centrosymmetric system.
conclusion: Periodic driving can induce exotic properties like bistability and even-order harmonics in centrosymmetric systems.

title: Quantum Physics-informed Neural Network With Residual-based Adaptive Refinement For Solving Partial Differential Equations
authors: Le Li, Junkai Yang, Qingle Wang, And Zhichao Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Le Li, Junkai Yang, Qingle Wang, and Zhichao Zhang

In this paper, we propose a quantum physics-informed neural network (QPINN) to solve partial differential equations (PDEs) by using residual-based adaptive refinement (RAR). The method incorporates a residual-driven adaptive sampling mechanism into the training of QPINN, which aims to enhance conver…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033042] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum physics-informed neural network (QPINN) with residual-based adaptive refinement for solving partial differential equations.
motivation: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) are powerful for solving PDEs but suffer from slow convergence and accuracy issues; quantum neural networks may offer advantages.
method: The method integrates a residual-driven adaptive sampling mechanism into the training of a quantum neural network to iteratively add collocation points where the PDE residual is large.
result: Numerical experiments on several benchmark PDEs show that QPINN with RAR achieves better accuracy and faster convergence compared to standard PINNs and QPINNs without adaptive refinement.
conclusion: The proposed QPINN-RAR framework demonstrates the potential of quantum machine learning for scientific computing, though practical quantum advantage remains to be seen.

title: Influence Of Excitation Energy On Microscopic Quantum Pathways For Ultrafast Charge Transfer In Van Der Waals Heterostructures
authors: Niklas Hofmann, Johannes Gradl, Leonard Weigl, Stiven Forti, Camilla Coletti, And Isabella Gierz
abstract:
Author(s): Niklas Hofmann, Johannes Gradl, Leonard Weigl, Stiven Forti, Camilla Coletti, and Isabella Gierz

Efficient charge separation in van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures is crucial for optimizing light harvesting and detection applications. However, precise control over the microscopic pathways governing ultrafast charge transfer remains an open challenge. These pathways are intrinsically linked to …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033033] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies ultrafast charge transfer pathways in van der Waals heterostructures as a function of excitation energy.
motivation: Efficient charge separation in vdW heterostructures is crucial for light harvesting and detection, but controlling microscopic pathways remains challenging.
method: The authors use time-resolved spectroscopy and theoretical modeling to probe charge transfer dynamics at different excitation energies.
result: They identify distinct microscopic pathways that depend on excitation energy, revealing how energy tuning can steer charge transfer.
conclusion: Controlling excitation energy provides a means to optimize charge separation in vdW heterostructures for optoelectronic applications.

title: Quantum-enhanced Markov Chain Monte Carlo Sampling To Model Lagrangian Tracer Dispersion In Turbulent Boundary Layer
authors: Fabian Schindler And Jörg Schumacher
abstract:
Author(s): Fabian Schindler and Jörg Schumacher

We present a quantum-enhanced Markov chain Monte Carlo (QE-MCMC) method to sample turbulent acceleration vectors from a joint target distribution that depends on all three components and height to model the transport and dispersion of massless Lagrangian tracer particles in two different turbulent s…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033031] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper applies quantum-enhanced Markov chain Monte Carlo to model Lagrangian tracer dispersion in turbulent boundary layers.
motivation: Accurate modeling of turbulent particle dispersion is important for environmental and engineering applications, but classical MCMC can be computationally expensive.
method: The authors propose a quantum-enhanced MCMC algorithm that leverages quantum computing to sample from the joint target distribution of turbulent acceleration vectors.
result: The QE-MCMC method demonstrates improved sampling efficiency compared to classical MCMC for the specific turbulent flow scenarios considered.
conclusion: Quantum-enhanced MCMC shows promise for accelerating simulations of turbulent dispersion, though practical quantum advantage remains to be demonstrated on larger scales.

title: Noiseless Limit And Improved-prior Limit Of The Maximum Entropy Method And Their Implications For The Analytic Continuation Problem
authors: Thomas Chuna, Nicholas Barnfield, Paul Hamann, Sebastian Schwalbe, Michael P. Friedlander, And Tobias Dornheim
abstract:
Author(s): Thomas Chuna, Nicholas Barnfield, Paul Hamann, Sebastian Schwalbe, Michael P. Friedlander, and Tobias Dornheim

Quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) methods are uniquely capable of providing exact simulations of quantum many-body systems. Unfortunately, the applications of a QMC simulation are limited because extracting dynamic properties requires solving the analytic continuation problem. Across the many fields that us…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033009] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes the maximum entropy method for analytic continuation in quantum Monte Carlo simulations, focusing on its noiseless and improved-prior limits.
motivation: Quantum Monte Carlo methods provide exact simulations of quantum many-body systems, but extracting dynamic properties requires solving the analytic continuation problem, which is ill-posed and challenging.
method: The authors study the maximum entropy method in the noiseless limit and with improved priors, deriving theoretical insights and testing on benchmark systems.
result: They show that in the noiseless limit, the method can recover exact spectral functions under certain conditions, and improved priors enhance reconstruction accuracy.
conclusion: The findings provide guidance for better analytic continuation in QMC, but the work is primarily a computational method study without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Markov Inequality As A Tool For Linear-scaling Estimation Of Local Observables
authors: H. P. Veiga, D. R. Pinheiro, J. P. Santos Pires, And J. M. Viana Parente Lopes
abstract:
Author(s): H. P. Veiga, D. R. Pinheiro, J. P. Santos Pires, and J. M. Viana Parente Lopes

We introduce a linear-scaling stochastic method to compute real-space maps of any positive local spectral operator in a tight-binding model. By employing positive semidefinite estimators, the sampling error at each site can be rigorously bounded relative to the mean via the Markov inequality, overco…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033015] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: A linear-scaling stochastic method for computing local spectral operators in tight-binding models using Markov inequality to bound sampling error.
motivation: To efficiently compute real-space maps of local observables in large tight-binding systems without full diagonalization.
method: Uses positive semidefinite estimators and Markov inequality to bound sampling error per site, enabling linear-scaling computation.
result: The method provides rigorous error bounds and linear scaling with system size, demonstrated on graphene and other models.
conclusion: The approach is efficient and accurate for local spectral properties in large tight-binding models, with potential for broader applications.

title: Aging Of Ring Polymeric Topological Glass Formers Via Thermal Quench
authors: Arabinda Behera, Projesh Roy, Pinaki Chaudhuri, And Satyavani Vemparala
abstract:
Author(s): Arabinda Behera, Projesh Roy, Pinaki Chaudhuri, and Satyavani Vemparala

We investigate the nonequilibrium glassy dynamics of dense, topologically constrained ring-polymer systems subjected to instantaneous thermal quenches, using large-scale molecular dynamics simulations. We show that the onset of dynamical arrest is strongly controlled by polymer stiffness, with incre…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033019] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the nonequilibrium glassy dynamics of ring-polymer systems after thermal quench using molecular dynamics simulations.
motivation: Understanding the aging behavior of topologically constrained ring polymers is important for polymer physics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Large-scale molecular dynamics simulations of dense ring-polymer systems with varying stiffness are performed to monitor dynamical arrest after instantaneous thermal quenches.
result: The onset of dynamical arrest is strongly controlled by polymer stiffness, with increasing stiffness leading to slower relaxation and more pronounced aging effects.
conclusion: The study provides insights into the glass transition in ring polymers, but the topic is far from the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Arbitrary Control Of non-Hermitian Skin Modes Via Disorder And An Electric Field
authors: Zhao-Fan Cai, Yang Li, Yu-Ran Zhang, Xiaomin Wei, Zhongmin Yang, Tao Liu, And Franco Nori
abstract:
Author(s): Zhao-Fan Cai, Yang Li, Yu-Ran Zhang, Xiaomin Wei, Zhongmin Yang, Tao Liu, and Franco Nori

The non-Hermitian skin effect (NHSE), characterized by the accumulation of a macroscopic number of bulk states at system boundaries, is a hallmark of non-Hermitian physics. However, in higher dimensions, achieving deterministic control over where skin modes accumulate remains a major challenge. Here…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033021] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the control of non-Hermitian skin modes using disorder and electric fields, focusing on a phenomenon in non-Hermitian physics.
motivation: Achieving deterministic control over where skin modes accumulate in higher-dimensional non-Hermitian systems is a major challenge.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the effects of disorder and an applied electric field on the non-Hermitian skin effect, likely using tight-binding models or similar approaches.
result: They demonstrate that disorder and electric fields can be used to arbitrarily control the localization of skin modes.
conclusion: This work provides a method for controlling non-Hermitian skin modes, which may have implications for wave manipulation and sensing.

title: Adversarial Vulnerability Of Machine-learning Surrogates For Computational Fluid Dynamics
authors: Jian-Nan Chen, Xiao-Yan Cao, And Jun-Jie Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Jian-Nan Chen, Xiao-Yan Cao, and Jun-Jie Zhang

Machine-learning surrogates are increasingly used to accelerate computational fluid dynamics (CFD), yet their robustness to small, structured input perturbations remains insufficiently characterized. Conventional adversarial training is largely impractical for artificial intelligence for CFD (AI4CFD…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033002] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies adversarial vulnerability of machine-learning surrogates for computational fluid dynamics, which is unrelated to quantum information theory.
motivation: Machine-learning surrogates are used to accelerate CFD, but their robustness to small input perturbations is not well characterized.
method: The authors analyze adversarial attacks on neural network surrogates for CFD and evaluate their impact on prediction accuracy.
result: The surrogates are found to be vulnerable to adversarial perturbations, which can cause significant prediction errors.
conclusion: Adversarial robustness should be considered when deploying ML surrogates in CFD applications.

title: Extended Hot-electron Model And Current Bistability In Insulating $a\text{−}{\mathrm{Y}}_{x}{\mathrm{Si}}_{1\text{−}x}$ Films

motivation: To understand nontrivial transport phenomena arising from suppressed electron-phonon coupling in disordered materials.
method: Extended hot-electron model and experimental measurements on a-Si:Y films.
result: The model explains current bistability observed in the films.
conclusion: The work provides insight into electron-phonon coupling in disordered systems but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Local Probe Evidence Supporting Altermagnetism In ${\mathrm{Co}}_{1/4}{\mathrm{NbSe}}_{2}$
authors: J. N. Graham, T. J. Hicken, Resham Babu Regmi, M. Janoschek, I. Mazin, H. Luetkens, N. J. Ghimire, And Z. Guguchia

[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023361] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses muon spin rotation to investigate altermagnetism in Co-intercalated NbSe2.
motivation: To provide local probe evidence supporting the predicted altermagnetic state in Co1/4NbSe2.
method: Muon spin rotation (μSR) measurements were performed on single crystals of Co1/4NbSe2.
result: The μSR data are consistent with altermagnetic order, corroborating previous neutron diffraction results.
conclusion: The study confirms altermagnetism in this material using a local probe technique.

title: Composite Superconducting Orders And Magnetism In ${\mathrm{CeRh}}_{2}{\mathrm{As}}_{2}$
authors: Fabian Jakubczyk, Julia M. Link, And Carsten Timm

tldr: This paper studies composite superconducting orders and magnetism in the heavy-fermion superconductor CeRh2As2.
motivation: To understand the interplay between superconductivity and magnetism in locally noncentrosymmetric materials, which is a topic in condensed matter physics.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling and analysis of the electronic structure and pairing symmetries.
result: They identify possible composite superconducting orders and their coupling to magnetic fluctuations.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into the unique superconducting properties of CeRh2As2 but do not directly contribute to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Electric-Field Control Of Interlayer Binding And Friction In $h$-BN Contacts
authors: Penghua Ying, Michael Urbakh, And Oded Hod
abstract:
Author(s): Penghua Ying, Michael Urbakh, and Oded Hod

External electric fields can be used to control sliding resistance in layered materials, providing a way to control friction in some systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031003] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies electric-field control of interlayer binding and friction in h-BN contacts, a topic in nanoscale tribology.
motivation: Understanding and controlling friction at the nanoscale is important for designing nanomechanical devices.
method: The authors use first-principles calculations and molecular dynamics simulations to investigate how an external electric field modulates interlayer interactions and sliding resistance.
result: They find that electric fields can significantly alter interlayer binding energies and friction forces in h-BN contacts.
conclusion: External electric fields provide a viable route to dynamically control friction in layered materials like h-BN.

title: Agentic Exploration Of Physics Models
authors: Maximilian Nägele And Florian Marquardt
abstract:

ꜱᴄɪᴇxᴘʟᴏʀᴇʀ, a generalist artificial scientist agent based on a large-language model, automates the process of scientific research and discovery and uncovers underlying models of diverse physical systems without task-specific fine-tuning.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031002] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an AI agent that automates scientific discovery by exploring physics models using large language models.
motivation: To automate the process of scientific research and discovery in physics without task-specific fine-tuning.
method: The authors develop SciExplorer, a generalist artificial scientist agent based on a large language model, which autonomously explores and uncovers underlying models of diverse physical systems.
result: The agent successfully discovers models for various physical systems, demonstrating the potential of AI-driven scientific discovery.
conclusion: LLM-based agents can automate parts of the scientific discovery process, but the paper focuses on AI methodology rather than advancing quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Rare Cage Escapes Drive Relaxation In Deeply Supercooled Liquids
authors: Francesco Rusciano, Raffaele Pastore, Francesco Greco, And Walter Kob
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Rusciano, Raffaele Pastore, Francesco Greco, and Walter Kob

Simulations conducted significantly below the mode coupling temperature allow dynamic properties of glass forming systems to be uncovered.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021061] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses simulations to study relaxation dynamics in deeply supercooled liquids, focusing on rare cage escapes.
motivation: Understanding the microscopic mechanisms of relaxation in glass-forming liquids is a fundamental problem in condensed matter physics.
method: Molecular dynamics simulations are performed at temperatures significantly below the mode coupling temperature to observe rare cage escape events.
result: The study identifies that rare cage escapes are the primary drivers of relaxation in deeply supercooled liquids.
conclusion: The findings provide new insights into the dynamics of glass-forming systems, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Complexity-Theoretic Foundations Of BosonSampling With A Linear Number Of Modes
authors: Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, And Michał Oszmaniec
abstract:
Author(s): Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, and Michał Oszmaniec

Experimental demonstrations of quantum advantage in photonic systems operate in the “saturated regime” of optics, whereas until now the complexity theory underpinning them has pertained only to the “dilute regime”—researchers bridge the gap.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021059] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes the complexity-theoretic foundations for BosonSampling in the saturated regime with a linear number of modes, bridging the gap between theory and experimental demonstrations.
motivation: Experimental photonic quantum advantage demonstrations operate in the saturated regime, but existing complexity theory only covers the dilute regime, so a theoretical foundation for the saturated regime is needed.
method: The authors analyze the computational complexity of BosonSampling when the number of modes scales linearly with the number of photons, using techniques from computational complexity theory and quantum optics.
result: They prove that BosonSampling in the saturated regime remains hard for classical computers under plausible complexity assumptions, and provide evidence that the linear scaling regime is computationally as hard as the dilute regime.
conclusion: The results validate the complexity-theoretic security of current photonic quantum advantage experiments and provide a rigorous foundation for future demonstrations.

title: Dynamics Of Quantum Chiral Solitons
authors: Leandro M. Chinellato, Oleg A. Starykh, And Cristian D. Batista
abstract:
Author(s): Leandro M. Chinellato, Oleg A. Starykh, and Cristian D. Batista

A nonperturbative quantization framework for chiral solitons in spin chains demonstrates that they condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid, appearing as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase and becoming detectable via inelastic neutron scattering.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021056] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the dynamics of quantum chiral solitons in spin chains, showing they condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid and can be detected via neutron scattering.
motivation: To understand the quantum behavior of chiral solitons in spin chains, which are topological excitations with potential implications for condensed matter physics.
method: A nonperturbative quantization framework is developed to describe chiral solitons in spin chains, and their low-energy properties are analyzed.
result: Chiral solitons condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid and appear as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase.
conclusion: The findings provide a theoretical basis for detecting chiral solitons via inelastic neutron scattering, advancing the understanding of quantum soliton dynamics.

title: Free And Interacting Fermionic Conformal Field Theories On The Fuzzy Sphere
authors: Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, And Yin-Chen He
abstract:
Author(s): Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, and Yin-Chen He

Researchers use noncommutative “fuzzy” spheres to study three-dimensional fermionic conformal field theories, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021055] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses fuzzy sphere regularization to study free and interacting fermionic conformal field theories in three dimensions, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.
motivation: To understand non-perturbative aspects of conformal field theories, particularly fermionic ones, using a noncommutative geometry approach.
method: The authors employ the fuzzy sphere, a noncommutative regularization, to simulate free and interacting fermionic CFTs numerically.
result: They observe emergent supersymmetry in the interacting theory and compute critical exponents and operator dimensions.
conclusion: The fuzzy sphere is a powerful tool for studying fermionic CFTs and can reveal emergent symmetries not present in the bare theory.

title: General Approach To Solving Spin Moiré Superstructures
authors: Paul M. Neves, Takashi Kurumaji, Joshua P. Wakefield, Arno Hiess, Paul Steffens, Navid Qureshi, Robert Cubitt, Lisa M. Debeer-Schmitt, Johanna C. Palmstrom, Satoru Hayami, Marek Bartkowiak, Markus Zolliker, Jonathan S. White, And Joseph G. Checkelsky
abstract:

Mapping of spin textures in EuAg

result: Three distinct, tunable magnetic phases are discovered in EuAg4Sb2.
conclusion: The findings establish a design framework for materials that manipulate information via spin-based vortex lattices.

title: Fate Of Topological Dirac Magnons In Van Der Waals Ferromagnets At Finite Temperature
authors: Rintaro Eto, Ignacio Salgado-Linares, Masahito Mochizuki, Johannes Knolle, And Alexander Mook
abstract:

tldr: This paper studies the stability of topological magnon gaps in van der Waals ferromagnets at finite temperature.
motivation: Understanding how topological magnon gaps behave at finite temperatures is crucial for designing robust spintronic devices.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling of magnon interactions to simulate the temperature dependence of topological magnon gaps.
result: They find that topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable even near the Curie point.
conclusion: The results provide a roadmap for designing robust spintronic devices based on topological magnons.

title: Predicting Physical Links In Networks
authors: Shuai Li, Wei Chen, And Jan Nagler
abstract:
Author(s): Shuai Li, Wei Chen, and Jan Nagler

A physics-informed framework allows for inferring general causal links across a wide range of networked dynamics systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021048] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A physics-informed framework for inferring causal links in networked dynamical systems.
motivation: Understanding causal relationships in complex networks is important but challenging; the authors aim to develop a general method based on physical principles.
method: The framework uses a physics-informed approach, likely incorporating dynamical equations or conservation laws, to infer causal links from observed network dynamics.
result: The method is demonstrated to infer general causal links across a wide range of networked dynamical systems.
conclusion: The proposed framework provides a new way to predict physical links in networks, with potential applications in various fields.

title: General Framework Enabling Polarity-Tunable Time-Reversal Symmetric Superconducting Diode Effects In Gate-Defined Homojunctions
authors: Hongwei Zhang, Chunsheng Wang, Ran Wang, Senyang Pan, Hengning Wang, Jiaqiang Cai, Yonglai Liu, Zhe Qu, Xiangde Zhu, Wei Ning, Chuanying Xi, Jinglei Zhang, Ning Hao, Guolin Zheng, And Mingliang Tian
abstract:

Local protonic gating in
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021046] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a time-reversal symmetric superconducting diode effect in gate-defined homojunctions using local protonic gating.
motivation: To achieve magnetic-field-free control of nonreciprocal critical currents in superconducting devices, which is important for superconducting electronics.
method: The authors use local protonic gating in homojunctions to induce a time-reversal symmetric superconducting diode effect.
result: They demonstrate polarity-tunable nonreciprocal critical currents without an external magnetic field.
conclusion: This work provides a framework for realizing superconducting diodes that operate without magnetic fields, potentially useful for low-power electronics.

title: Anyon Superfluidity Of Excitons In Quantum Hall Bilayers
authors: Zhaoyu Han, Taige Wang, Zhihuan Dong, Michael P. Zaletel, And Ashvin Vishwanath
abstract:
Author(s): Zhaoyu Han, Taige Wang, Zhihuan Dong, Michael P. Zaletel, and Ashvin Vishwanath

Theoretical analysis of quantum Hall bilayers reveals that topological criticality facilitates the emergence of anyonic exciton superfluids, offering a robust mechanism for engineering exotic collective quantum states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021044] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies anyon superfluidity of excitons in quantum Hall bilayers, focusing on topological criticality and exotic collective quantum states.
motivation: To understand and engineer exotic collective quantum states in quantum Hall bilayers through topological criticality.
method: Theoretical analysis of quantum Hall bilayers, likely using field theory or numerical methods to study anyon superfluidity.
result: Topological criticality facilitates the emergence of anyonic exciton superfluids.
conclusion: The work offers a robust mechanism for engineering exotic collective quantum states in quantum Hall systems.

title: Robust Orbital-Selective Flat Bands In Layered Transition-Metal Oxyhalides At Room Temperature
authors: Xiangyu Luo, Ludovica Zullo, Sahaj Patel, Dongjin Oh, Willa Mihalyi-Koch, Emma Lian, Jiaruo Li, Qian Song, Asish K. Kundu, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Elio Vescovo, Natalia Olszowska, Rafał Kurleto, Dawid Wutke, Xavier Roy, Giorgio Sangiovanni, And Riccardo Comin
abstract:
Author(s): Xiangyu Luo, Ludovica Zullo, Sahaj Patel, Dongjin Oh, Willa Mihalyi-Koch, Emma Lian, Jiaruo Li, Qian Song, Asish K. Kundu, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Elio Vescovo, Natalia Olszowska, Rafał Kurleto, Dawid Wutke, Xavier Roy, Giorgio Sangiovanni, and Riccardo Comin

Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy of layered transition-metal oxyhalides reveals intrinsic flat bands that remain stable at room temperature, providing a tunable platform for investigating strongly correlated electron states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021041] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of robust orbital-selective flat bands in layered transition-metal oxyhalides at room temperature using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy.
motivation: Flat bands in strongly correlated materials can host exotic quantum phases, but most known flat bands require cryogenic temperatures. The authors aim to find a room-temperature stable platform.
method: The authors synthesize layered transition-metal oxyhalides and characterize their electronic structure using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and density functional theory (DFT).
result: They observe intrinsic flat bands that are robust at room temperature, with orbital selectivity and tunability via chemical composition.
conclusion: These materials provide a promising platform for studying strongly correlated electron physics at room temperature, potentially enabling practical applications.

title: Probing Quantum Anomalous Hall States In Twisted Bilayer ${\mathrm{WSe}}_{2}$ Via Attractive Polaron Spectroscopy
authors: Beini Gao, Mahdi Ghafariasl, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Tsung-Sheng Huang, Lifu Zhang, Deric Session, Pranshoo Upadhyay, Rundong Ma, Ghadah Alshalan, Daniel Suarez, Supratik Sarkar, Suji Park, Houk Jang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ming Xie, You Zhou, And Mohammad Hafezi

Magneto-optical spectroscopy of twisted WSe

tldr: This paper reports magneto-optical spectroscopy of twisted bilayer WSe2, revealing a quantum anomalous Hall phase and electric-field control of magnetic order.
motivation: To probe and control quantum anomalous Hall states in twisted bilayer WSe2, a moiré material, using optical spectroscopy.
method: Magneto-optical spectroscopy, specifically attractive polaron spectroscopy, is used to study the electronic and magnetic properties of twisted bilayer WSe2 under varying electric fields.
result: A spontaneous quantum anomalous Hall phase is observed, and electric-field control enables transitions between ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic orders.

title: Could Living Cells Use Phase Transitions To Process Information?
authors: Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, And Eric R. Dufresne
abstract:
Author(s): Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, and Eric R. Dufresne

This Perspective explores biomolecular condensation as a powerful framework for computation, enabling cells to process high-dimensional information to sense, classify, and respond to complex environmental signals.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020501] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This perspective explores how biomolecular condensation in living cells can process high-dimensional information through phase transitions.
motivation: Cells need to process complex environmental signals, and biomolecular condensates may offer a powerful computational framework.
method: The paper presents a conceptual perspective, drawing analogies between phase transitions and information processing in biological systems.
result: It proposes that phase separation can enable sensing, classification, and response to multiple signals simultaneously.
conclusion: Biomolecular condensation could be a natural substrate for cellular computation, but the ideas are speculative and not directly connected to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Liquid-Gas Criticality Of Hyperuniform Fluids
authors: Shang Gao, Hao Shang, Hao Hu, Yu-Qiang Ma, And Qun-Li Lei
abstract:
Author(s): Shang Gao, Hao Shang, Hao Hu, Yu-Qiang Ma, and Qun-Li Lei

Where ordinary fluids show wild fluctuations and critical opalescence, hyperuniform fluids of spinning particles stay unusually calm yet highly susceptible at the liquid–vapor critical point.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021032] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the liquid-gas criticality of hyperuniform fluids, a topic in soft condensed matter physics.
motivation: To understand the critical behavior of hyperuniform fluids, which exhibit suppressed density fluctuations, at the liquid-vapor critical point.
method: The authors use theoretical analysis and possibly simulations to investigate the critical properties of hyperuniform fluids composed of spinning particles.
result: Hyperuniform fluids show unusual calmness yet high susceptibility at the critical point, contrasting with ordinary fluids.
conclusion: The findings reveal unique critical behavior in hyperuniform fluids, relevant to condensed matter physics but not to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Stealthy-Hyperuniform Wave Dynamics In Two-Dimensional Photonic Crystals
authors: Maria Barsukova, Zeyu Zhang, Brian Gould, Koorosh Sadri, Christian Rosiek, Søren Stobbe, Jonas Karcher, And Mikael C. Rechtsman
abstract:
Author(s): Maria Barsukova, Zeyu Zhang, Brian Gould, Koorosh Sadri, Christian Rosiek, Søren Stobbe, Jonas Karcher, and Mikael C. Rechtsman

While disordered stealthy hyperuniform materials are expected to be largely transparent within a particular range of wavelengths, new experiments on large-scale silicon photonic crystals reveal unexpected residual scattering driven by radiative loss.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021028] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies wave dynamics in stealthy hyperuniform photonic crystals, revealing unexpected residual scattering due to radiative loss.
motivation: Stealthy hyperuniform materials are expected to be transparent in certain wavelength ranges, but experiments show residual scattering that needs explanation.
method: Large-scale experiments on silicon photonic crystals combined with theoretical analysis to characterize the scattering behavior.
result: Residual scattering is driven by radiative loss, contradicting the expectation of full transparency.
conclusion: The findings highlight limitations of stealthy hyperuniformity for photonic applications and suggest design modifications.

title: Ballistic Spin Valve In Graphene Realized Via Electron Optics
authors: Daniel Burrow, Oktay Deveci, Rares Dragomir, Thomas Thomson, And Ivan J. Vera-Marun
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Burrow, Oktay Deveci, Rares Dragomir, Thomas Thomson, and Ivan J. Vera-Marun

Transverse magnetic focusing in encapsulated graphene reveals gate-tunable ballistic spin transport, providing a mechanism for coherent spin control through spin-dependent electron optics.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021029] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a ballistic spin valve in graphene using transverse magnetic focusing and electron optics.
motivation: To achieve coherent spin control in graphene via spin-dependent electron optics, enabling ballistic spin transport.
method: Transverse magnetic focusing in encapsulated graphene is used to reveal gate-tunable ballistic spin transport.
result: Observation of ballistic spin transport and coherent spin control through spin-dependent electron optics.
conclusion: The work provides a mechanism for spin control in graphene, relevant to spintronics but not to the specified research directions.

title: Dipolar Nematic State In Relaxor Ferroelectrics
authors: Yuan-Jinsheng Liu, Tyler C. Sterling, And Shi Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Yuan-Jinsheng Liu, Tyler C. Sterling, and Shi Liu

A nematic ordering underpins the behavior of relaxor ferroelectrics.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021022] Published Wed Apr 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates a dipolar nematic state in relaxor ferroelectrics, focusing on the structural and dynamical properties of these materials.
motivation: Relaxor ferroelectrics exhibit complex behavior due to polar nanoregions, and understanding the nematic ordering is key to explaining their properties.
method: The authors use experimental techniques and theoretical modeling to characterize the dipolar nematic state in relaxor ferroelectrics.
result: They identify a dipolar nematic phase and describe its role in the macroscopic behavior of relaxor ferroelectrics.
conclusion: The dipolar nematic state is a fundamental aspect of relaxor ferroelectrics, providing insights into their unique dielectric and piezoelectric properties.

title: Provable Quantum Speedups For Computing Persistence In Topological Data Analysis
authors: Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, And Ryu Hayakawa
abstract:
Author(s): Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, and Ryu Hayakawa

A quantum algorithm achieving exponential speedup for a topological data analysis problem is proposed, potentially driving new practical applications in quantum computing.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020361] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A quantum algorithm for computing persistence in topological data analysis is proposed, claiming exponential speedup.
motivation: Topological data analysis is a powerful tool for analyzing high-dimensional data, but classical algorithms for computing persistence are computationally expensive. Quantum computing may offer speedups.
method: The paper presents a quantum algorithm that leverages quantum linear algebra and topological data analysis techniques to compute persistent homology.
result: The algorithm achieves an exponential speedup over classical methods for certain classes of data, as proven theoretically.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a potential quantum advantage in topological data analysis, but the practical applicability depends on the availability of fault-tolerant quantum computers.

title: Grand Challenge Of Quantum Applications
authors: Ryan Babbush, Robbie King, Sergio Boixo, William Huggins, Tanuj Khattar, Guang Hao Low, Jarrod R. Mcclean, Thomas O’brien, And Nicholas C. Rubin
abstract:
Author(s): Ryan Babbush, Robbie King, Sergio Boixo, William Huggins, Tanuj Khattar, Guang Hao Low, Jarrod R. McClean, Thomas O’Brien, and Nicholas C. Rubin

A proposed five-stage framework outlines the path to useful quantum computing, detailing the scientific milestones required to bridge the gap between theory and real-world utility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020101] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a five-stage framework for achieving useful quantum computing, outlining scientific milestones.
motivation: To bridge the gap between theoretical quantum computing and real-world utility by providing a structured roadmap.
