result: A high-level roadmap with stages from quantum advantage to fault-tolerant quantum computing.
conclusion: The framework serves as a guide for the quantum computing community to focus efforts on key milestones.

title: 2d Van Der Waals Magnets: From Fundamental Physics To Applications
authors: Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, And Nuh Gedik
abstract:
Author(s): Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, and Nuh Gedik

Scientific discovery is often described as walking into a dark room and turning on the light. The discovery of 2D magnetism in van der Waals materials in 2016 was one such leap forward, removing one spatial dimension from macroscopic materials. The study of 2D magnets has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena. This review summarizes the current state of knowledge of magnetic phenomena in 2D van der Waals materials. The field encompasses not just the traditional study of ferromagnets and antiferromagnets but also topology, quantum and nonequilibrium dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons and spintronics, and the interaction of magnetism with light, phonons, and electric fields (multiferroics). The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025003] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A review of 2D van der Waals magnets covering fundamental physics and applications.
motivation: To summarize the current state of knowledge and recent discoveries in 2D magnetism, which has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena.
method: The paper is a review that surveys experimental and theoretical progress in 2D van der Waals magnets, including topics like topology, quantum dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons, and spintronics.
result: The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.
conclusion: 2D van der Waals magnets are a rich platform for studying magnetism in reduced dimensions, with potential for future technologies.

title: Radiation Forces And Torques In Optics And Acoustics
authors: Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, And Konstantin Y. Bliokh
abstract:
Author(s): Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, and Konstantin Y. Bliokh

This review presents a unified perspective of how local energy, momentum, and spin densities in optical and acoustic wave fields induce forces and torques on particles—a topic that has captivated researchers for centuries. Applications discussed include trapping and manipulation of atoms and nanoparticles by light, sorting of biological cells by the combination of acoustics and microfluidics, and pulling forces that draw particles against the direction of wave propagation.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025002] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: This review paper presents a unified perspective on radiation forces and torques in optical and acoustic wave fields, focusing on particle manipulation.
motivation: Understanding how local energy, momentum, and spin densities in wave fields induce forces and torques on particles is fundamental for applications like optical trapping and acoustic sorting.
method: The authors review theoretical frameworks and experimental demonstrations of radiation forces and torques, drawing parallels between optics and acoustics.
result: The paper provides a comprehensive overview of the mechanisms behind radiation-induced forces and torques, including pulling forces and spin-induced torques.
conclusion: The unified perspective highlights common principles across optics and acoustics, offering insights for future applications in particle manipulation.

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: A review of exactly solvable quantum many-body dynamics using space-time duality and brickwork quantum circuits.
motivation: Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult; this review aims to provide a unified pedagogical view based on space-time duality.
method: The review discusses discretizing time evolution in lattice systems, treating space and time on the same footing, and focuses on brickwork quantum circuits as a framework.
result: The paper presents a pedagogical overview of how space-time duality enables exact solutions for certain interacting many-body systems.
conclusion: Space-time duality and brickwork circuits offer a powerful analogy with quantum computation for understanding quantum many-body dynamics.

title: Kagome Metals
authors: Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, And Stephen D. Wilson
abstract:
Author(s): Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, and Stephen D. Wilson

The kagome lattice is a two-dimensional tiling of hexagons and triangles named after a Japanese basket weaving technique. Its geometry gives rise to highly frustrated interactions and interference effects experienced by electrons and their multiple degrees of freedom. In metals, the exploration of materials with kagome conduction networks is driven by predictions of realizing new electronic states where these interference effects are dominant, amplifying electronic interactions and many-body effects. In these kagome metals, these amplified correlation effects in combination with spin-orbit coupling and other forms of frustration have given rise to a wealth of phenomena beyond expectations. These include unusual states and responses born from topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, sublattice interference effects at saddle points such as unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism and flux phases, amplified anomalous Hall effects, and electronic nematic states. This review examines the theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, with the aim of elucidating fundamental mechanisms underlying the observed exotic phenomena.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015002] Published Thu Feb 12, 2026.
tldr: A review of kagome metals, focusing on their exotic electronic states and many-body phenomena.
motivation: To understand the fundamental mechanisms behind unusual states in kagome metals, such as unconventional superconductivity and orbital antiferromagnetism.
method: The paper reviews theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, analyzing electronic band structures, correlation effects, and topological properties.
result: Kagome metals exhibit a wealth of exotic phenomena including topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, and amplified Hall effects.
conclusion: The kagome lattice provides a rich platform for studying strongly correlated and topological physics, but the paper is primarily a materials science review without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Field Theories And Quantum Methods For Stochastic Reaction-diffusion Systems
authors: Mauricio J. Del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, And Wout Merbis
abstract:
Author(s): Mauricio J. del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, and Wout Merbis

The exchange of energy and molecules in a living cell, the spread of opinions through a society, and the flow of traffic in a crowded city are very different phenomena, yet they are all examples of complex systems composed of many agents that interact with each other and exchange energy or particles with the environment. These systems can be modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems. In this pedagogical review, the authors apply powerful field-theoretic methods to these systems, unifying diverse approaches under a single framework. The methods are useful for handling chemical systems but also have applications in a wide range of areas such as ecology and epidemiology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015001] Published Thu Jan 22, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review applying field-theoretic methods to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems in chemistry, ecology, and epidemiology.
motivation: To unify diverse approaches for modeling complex systems with many interacting agents under a single field-theoretic framework.
method: The authors review and apply field-theoretic methods, such as path integrals and Doi-Peliti formalism, to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems.
result: The review demonstrates how field theories can handle chemical systems and have applications in ecology and epidemiology.
conclusion: Field-theoretic methods provide a powerful unified framework for studying stochastic reaction-diffusion systems across various disciplines.

title: Neutron Stars And The Dense Matter Equation Of State
authors: Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, And Anna L. Watts
abstract:
Author(s): Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, and Anna L. Watts

Neutron stars, the remnants of supernova explosions, are the densest objects in the Universe. A typical neutron star has a mass between one and two solar masses, and a radius of around 12 km. The density at the center of the star is higher than that in atomic nuclei. As a result, the properties of neutron stars provide important information about the behavior of ordinary matter under extreme compression. In recent years, new information about neutron stars has emerged from two sources. The first is the observation of the gravitational-wave signal from the final inspiral of a coalescing binary neutron star. The second is a careful measurement of the x-ray pulse profile of a spinning neutron star. This review discusses these measurements and summarizes how they constrain masses, radii, and central densities. The results are compared to predictions based on calculations of the nuclear equation of state at densities comparable to that in atomic nuclei, which are then extrapolated to higher density. The review ends with an outlook on future observational opportunities.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045007] Published Wed Dec 24, 2025.
tldr: A review of neutron star observations and the dense matter equation of state, focusing on gravitational waves and X-ray pulse profiles.
motivation: Neutron stars are the densest objects in the Universe, and their properties provide information about matter under extreme compression.
method: The review summarizes constraints from gravitational-wave signals of binary neutron star mergers and X-ray pulse profile measurements, comparing them to nuclear equation of state calculations.
result: The measurements constrain masses, radii, and central densities of neutron stars, which are compared to theoretical predictions.
conclusion: Future observations will further refine our understanding of the dense matter equation of state.

title: Spin-glass Dynamics: Experiment, Theory, And Simulation
authors: E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, And D. Yllanes
abstract:
Author(s): E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, and D. Yllanes

This review updates the field of spin glasses with broad application to a large variety of physical systems. In particular, this review tracks the progress of experiment, theory, and large-scale simulations. It highlights the importance of their synergy, from the inception of the field to the present day, and includes future opportunities for research.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045005] Published Mon Dec 15, 2025.
tldr: A review of spin-glass dynamics covering experiment, theory, and simulation.
motivation: To provide an updated overview of spin-glass research and highlight the synergy between experiment, theory, and simulation.
method: Review of experimental, theoretical, and large-scale simulation studies in spin glasses.
result: Summarizes progress in understanding spin-glass dynamics and identifies future research opportunities.
conclusion: Spin-glass dynamics remain a rich field with broad applications, and continued interdisciplinary collaboration is essential.

title: Kitaev Quantum Spin Liquids
authors: Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, And Hae-Young Kee
abstract:
Author(s): Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, and Hae-Young Kee

Frustration in spin systems can prevent ordering even at =0, creating quantum spin liquids that have been sought since Anderson’s pioneering work in 1973 and his influential 1987 paper connecting them to high-temperature superconductivity. Kitaev’s solvable spin-1/2 models on a honeycomb lattice brought renewed attention to this field, with Jackeli and Khaliullin later revealing how to engineer Kitaev interactions in real materials. This review highlights theoretical and experimental developments in Kitaev spin liquids, emphasizing leading candidate materials and their broad topological properties such as chiral edge modes. Consequently, it provides essential insights for both experimentalists and theorists working on quantum spin liquid problems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045003] Published Wed Dec 03, 2025.
tldr: A review of Kitaev quantum spin liquids, focusing on candidate materials and topological properties.
motivation: To provide an overview of theoretical and experimental progress in Kitaev spin liquids, which are a type of quantum spin liquid with potential applications in topological quantum computing.
method: The paper reviews theoretical models (Kitaev honeycomb model) and experimental realizations in materials, highlighting chiral edge modes and other topological features.
result: The review summarizes key candidate materials and their properties, emphasizing the broad topological phenomena observed.
conclusion: Kitaev spin liquids are a rich field with many open questions, and the review serves as a guide for future research.

title: The Ups And Downs Of Internal Conversion
authors: Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, And Salvy P. Russo
abstract:
Author(s): Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, and Salvy P. Russo

This review examines the theoretical methods used to describe the photophysical process of internal conversion in quantum systems. These models explore all facets of the nonradiative mechanism, and the review presents an outlook on how they can be incorporated in studies relevant to applications, for example, in photonics and energy harvesting.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035003] Published Tue Sep 16, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical methods for internal conversion in quantum systems, with applications in photonics and energy harvesting.
motivation: Internal conversion is a key nonradiative process in photophysics, and understanding its theoretical underpinnings is important for applications like photonics and energy harvesting.
method: The paper reviews various theoretical models describing internal conversion, covering different facets of the nonradiative mechanism.
result: The review provides an overview of current theoretical approaches and an outlook on their incorporation into application-oriented studies.
conclusion: Theoretical methods for internal conversion are mature but need to be better integrated into applied research in photonics and energy harvesting.

title: Colloquium: Quantum Properties And Functionalities Of Magnetic Skyrmions
authors: Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, And Christos Panagopoulos
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, and Christos Panagopoulos

Skyrmions are topological field configurations that were first discussed in the context of high-energy theory. In recent years, skyrmionic spin patterns in solid-state systems have received much attention, in part for their promising application potential. This Colloquium discusses quantum-mechanical aspects of such magnetic skyrmions, both for the interactions that underlie skyrmion formation and for quantum features of the skyrmions themselves.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 031001] Published Tue Jul 08, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews quantum properties and functionalities of magnetic skyrmions, focusing on their topological nature and potential applications.
motivation: Magnetic skyrmions are promising for spintronic devices, but their quantum aspects are less explored; this review aims to bridge that gap.
method: The paper surveys theoretical and experimental work on skyrmion formation, quantum interactions, and quantum features of skyrmions themselves.
result: It highlights quantum effects such as tunneling, superposition, and entanglement in skyrmion systems, and discusses their potential for quantum information processing.
conclusion: Magnetic skyrmions exhibit rich quantum behavior that could be harnessed for future quantum technologies, but the field is still nascent.

title: Spin-dependent Exotic Interactions
authors: Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, And Dmitry Budker
abstract:
Author(s): Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, and Dmitry Budker

This review presents a comprehensive summary of theoretical investigations and experimental searches for spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model. These interactions may be mediated by various types of exotic bosons, and their existence and properties may, in turn, explain the nature of dark matter and dark energy. The described experiments also probe the discrete fundamental symmetries of nature.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025005] Published Tue Jun 24, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental searches for spin-dependent exotic interactions beyond the standard model, including their possible mediation by exotic bosons and implications for dark matter and dark energy.
motivation: To understand the nature of dark matter and dark energy, and to probe discrete fundamental symmetries, by searching for spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model.
method: The paper reviews a wide range of theoretical models and experimental techniques used to search for spin-dependent exotic interactions, including precision measurements with atomic, molecular, and optical systems.
result: The review summarizes current constraints on various exotic boson-mediated interactions and outlines future experimental directions.
conclusion: Spin-dependent exotic interactions remain an active area of research with potential to reveal new physics beyond the standard model, but no definitive evidence has been found yet.

title: Colloquium: Materials That Exceed Classical Thermodynamic Bounds On Properties
authors: Roderic S. Lakes
abstract:
Author(s): Roderic S. Lakes

Classical thermodynamic bounds provide constraints on values that are expected in measurements of certain physical properties. In a variety of fields, some measurements exceed these bounds. This apparent violation of thermodynamics arises because the measurements are made in ways that violate the underlying assumptions made when deriving these bounds. This Colloquium describes a wide variety of circumstances where such violations occur and which of the underlying assumptions are violated in each case. It also describes how interesting material properties can be developed using materials designed to violate these assumptions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021002] Published Wed May 14, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews materials that appear to exceed classical thermodynamic bounds on properties, explaining the violations by examining underlying assumptions.
motivation: Classical thermodynamic bounds are often assumed to be fundamental, but many measurements exceed them; understanding why can lead to new materials with enhanced properties.
method: The paper surveys a wide variety of circumstances where measured properties exceed classical bounds and identifies which assumptions (e.g., equilibrium, linear response) are violated in each case.
result: It shows that apparent violations arise because measurements are made in ways that violate the assumptions behind the bounds, and that materials can be designed to exploit these violations.
conclusion: The findings clarify the limits of classical thermodynamic bounds and provide a framework for developing materials with properties beyond conventional limits.

title: Colloquium: Synthetic Quantum Matter In Nonstandard Geometries
authors: Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, And Christof Weitenberg
abstract:
Author(s): Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, and Christof Weitenberg

This Colloquium presents ways to implement fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems. The study of quantum many-body physics in these exotic geometries permits simulation of phenomena from topology in condensed matter to models of gravity and cosmology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 011001] Published Tue Mar 25, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews experimental and theoretical implementations of fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems for simulating quantum many-body physics.
motivation: To explore quantum many-body phenomena in nonstandard geometries that are difficult to realize in conventional settings, such as topology and gravity analogs.
method: The paper surveys various platforms (cold atoms, photonics, electronic systems) and techniques for engineering synthetic lattices with fractal, curved, or higher-dimensional geometries.
result: It highlights recent progress in simulating exotic geometries and discusses open challenges and future directions.
conclusion: Synthetic quantum matter in nonstandard geometries offers a powerful tool for studying fundamental physics, but many experimental and theoretical challenges remain.

title: Massive Quantum Systems As Interfaces Of Quantum Mechanics And Gravity
authors: Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, And Clara C. Wanjura
abstract:
Author(s): Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, and Clara C. Wanjura

The authors review theories and experimental state-of-the-art efforts to study the effects of gravity on massive quantum systems. Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force and may be addressed via precision quantum probes. Experiments testing whether the quantum nature of gravity causes decoherence and collapse of matter-wave functions and whether it can mediate entanglement between separate massive particles are underway, and their results will guide the theoretical description of gravity effects on a laboratory scale.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015003] Published Thu Feb 13, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical and experimental efforts to study gravity's effects on massive quantum systems, focusing on tests of quantum gravity.
motivation: Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force, and massive quantum systems may serve as probes to study gravity's quantum nature.
method: The paper reviews theories of gravity-induced decoherence, collapse models, and entanglement mediation, along with experimental platforms such as matter-wave interferometry and optomechanics.
result: It summarizes the current state of experiments testing whether gravity causes decoherence or mediates entanglement, and outlines future directions.
conclusion: Experiments with massive quantum systems can guide the theoretical description of gravity on a laboratory scale, but no definitive results are yet available.

title: Tailoring Pure Valley-Zeeman Spin-Orbit Coupling In ${\mathrm{WSe}}_{2}$-Encapsulated Monolayer Graphene
authors: Yaqing Han, Siqi Jiang, Jingkuan Xiao, Jiawei Jiang, Yulu Liu, Jiabei Huang, Yu Du, Di Zhang, Fuzhuo Lian, Wanting Xu, Siqin Wang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Xiaoxiang Xi, Alexander S. Mayorov, Renjun Du, Kai Chang, Hongxin Yang, Lei Wang, And Geliang Yu

Clearly resolved Landau levels reveal a symmetry-enforced Landau-level reordering driven by competition between fixed valley–Zeeman splitting and magnetic-field-dependent cyclotron energy.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 027001] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies valley-Zeeman spin-orbit coupling in WSe2-encapsulated monolayer graphene, focusing on Landau level reordering.
motivation: To understand the interplay between valley-Zeeman splitting and cyclotron energy in graphene heterostructures.
method: Magneto-transport measurements on WSe2-encapsulated monolayer graphene devices.
result: Observation of symmetry-enforced Landau-level reordering due to competition between fixed valley-Zeeman splitting and magnetic-field-dependent cyclotron energy.
conclusion: The results reveal a new mechanism for tuning spin-orbit coupling in graphene, relevant for spintronics and valleytronics.

title: Zero Crossings Of The Differential Scalar Polarizability Of The ${\mathrm{Ba}}^{+}$ Clock Transition
authors: N. Jayjong, M. D. K. Lee, K. J. Arnold, And M. D. Barrett
abstract:

The differential scalar polarizability [MATH] of the [MATH] [MATH] clock transition has a zero crossing near 481 nm, which is measured to be 623.603 13(17) THz. From this measurement, we infer a ratio of reduced matrix elements $〈{P}_{3/2}∥r∥{S}_{1/…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012804] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper measures the zero crossing of the differential scalar polarizability of the Ba+ clock transition near 481 nm.
motivation: Accurate knowledge of the differential polarizability is important for reducing systematic shifts in atomic clocks, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors perform spectroscopy on trapped Ba+ ions to locate the zero crossing frequency of the differential scalar polarizability.
result: They measure the zero crossing at 623.60313(17) THz and infer a ratio of reduced matrix elements.
conclusion: The measurement improves understanding of atomic properties relevant to clock operation, but has no direct relevance to the specified research directions.

title: Scaling Law Linking Field And Weight Dynamic Ranges In Superoscillation
authors: Haitang Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Haitang Yang

Superoscillation (SO) offers a theoretical pathway to unlimited far-field superresolution, yet the associated physical costs lack a unified quantitative scaling description. In this work, we investigate the fundamental limits of deep SO by establishing a scaling law that links the field dynamic rang…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013505] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes a scaling law linking field and weight dynamic ranges in superoscillation for far-field superresolution.
motivation: Superoscillation offers a pathway to unlimited far-field superresolution, but the associated physical costs lack a unified quantitative scaling description.
method: The authors investigate fundamental limits of deep superoscillation by deriving a scaling law that connects the field dynamic range to the weight dynamic range.
result: A scaling law is established that quantifies the trade-off between field and weight dynamic ranges in superoscillation.
conclusion: The scaling law provides a unified description of physical costs in superoscillation, which may guide practical implementations.

title: Correlation-driven Phonon Renormalization And The Equation Of State Of $γ$-cerium
authors: Yao Wei, Siyu Chen, Evgeny Plekhanov, Ivan Štich, Cedric Weber, And Jan M. Tomczak
abstract:
Author(s): Yao Wei, Siyu Chen, Evgeny Plekhanov, Ivan Štich, Cedric Weber, and Jan M. Tomczak

We investigate the thermodynamic properties of elemental cerium by assessing the crucial role of phonon free energy within the framework of dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT). While conventional density functional theory (DFT) often fails to capture the intricate energy landscape of [MATH]-electron mat…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 055110] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies phonon renormalization and the equation of state of γ-cerium using DMFT, focusing on thermodynamic properties of a specific material.
motivation: Conventional DFT fails to capture the complex energy landscape of f-electron materials like cerium; the authors aim to improve thermodynamic predictions by including phonon free energy within DMFT.
method: They perform DMFT calculations for the electronic structure and couple them with phonon calculations to obtain the free energy and equation of state.
result: The inclusion of correlation-driven phonon renormalization yields better agreement with experimental equation of state data for γ-cerium.
conclusion: Phonon free energy is crucial for accurate thermodynamic modeling of strongly correlated materials like cerium.

title: Multistage Development Of Short-range Spin Correlations And Weak Magnetic Order In The Two Coupled Trillium Lattices Of ${\mathrm{K}}_{2}{\mathrm{Fe}}_{2}({\mathrm{MoO}}_{4}){({\mathrm{PO}}_{4})}_{2}$
authors: J. Khatua, Sritharan Krishnamoorthi, Changhyun Koo, Gyungbin Ban, Taeyun Kim, Yugo Oshima, Marc Uhlarz, John Wilkinson, Peter J. Baker, Kyeong Jun Lee, Mani Shankar, Seo Hyoung Chang, R. Sankar, And Kwang-Yong Choi

Trillium lattices, where magnetic ions form a chiral network of corner-sharing triangles, offer a three-dimensional magnetic framework that can host fragile classical spin-liquid states. tldr: This paper studies the magnetic properties of a trillium lattice compound, focusing on short-range spin correlations and weak magnetic order.
motivation: Trillium lattices are a three-dimensional magnetic framework that can host fragile classical spin-liquid states, and understanding their magnetic behavior is of fundamental interest.
method: The authors use magnetization, specific heat, electron spin resonance (ESR), and muon spin relaxation measurements to characterize the compound.
result: They observe multistage development of short-range spin correlations and weak magnetic order at low temperatures.
conclusion: The compound exhibits complex magnetic behavior with short-range correlations preceding long-range order, but no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics is made.

title: Stability Of Delay-coupled Reaction-diffusion Systems With Turing Or Wave Instability
authors: Keiji Konishi, Koki Yoshida, Yoshiki Sugitani, And Naoyuki Hara
abstract:

A quenching phenomenon that emerges in coupled oscillators, namely, amplitude death (AD), has been widely accepted. The present paper analytically deals with AD in two identical reaction-diffusion systems with periodic boundary or zero-flux boundary conditions that are coupled by a diffusive connect…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014207] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies amplitude death in delay-coupled reaction-diffusion systems with Turing or wave instability.
motivation: Understanding amplitude death in coupled oscillators is important for controlling oscillations in biological and chemical systems.
method: The authors analytically investigate two identical reaction-diffusion systems coupled by diffusive connections under periodic or zero-flux boundary conditions.
result: They derive conditions for amplitude death and analyze the stability of the coupled system.
conclusion: The work provides theoretical insights into amplitude death in spatially extended systems with time delays.

title: Interaction Of Solitons With Saturable Gain
authors: Akhilesh K. S. And Omri Gat
abstract:
Author(s): Akhilesh K. S. and Omri Gat

We study the tail-overlap interaction of a well-separated pair of dissipative solitons in systems with slow saturable gain. Gain saturation introduces nonlocal terms in the soliton field equation that depend on the total energy and therefore invalidate the standard methods used to study overlap inte…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014205] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the interaction of dissipative solitons in systems with slow saturable gain, focusing on tail-overlap effects.
motivation: Understanding soliton interactions is important for nonlinear optics and laser physics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model incorporating nonlocal gain saturation terms and analyze the interaction dynamics of well-separated soliton pairs.
result: They find that gain saturation introduces nonlocal effects that modify the standard overlap interaction, leading to new dynamical behaviors.
conclusion: The work provides insights into dissipative soliton interactions but remains within classical nonlinear optics, with no relevance to the specified research directions.

title: Segregation Dynamics In Active-passive Mixtures Of Semiflexible Filaments
authors: Chitrak Bhowmik, Aparna Baskaran, And Sriram Ramaswamy
abstract:
Author(s): Chitrak Bhowmik, Aparna Baskaran, and Sriram Ramaswamy

We study the segregation of motile semiflexible filaments from a background of similar but nonmotile filaments. Our Langevin dynamics simulations reveal a wide range of emergent structures governed by filament flexibility and activity, i.e., self-propulsion strength. The system segregates at low act…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015405] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies segregation dynamics in mixtures of active and passive semiflexible filaments using Langevin dynamics simulations.
motivation: Understanding how activity and flexibility govern structure formation in active-passive mixtures is important for biological and soft matter systems.
method: Langevin dynamics simulations of semiflexible filaments with varying flexibility and self-propulsion strength.
result: The system segregates at low activity, forming clusters and bands; the emergent structures depend on filament flexibility and activity.
conclusion: Activity and flexibility jointly determine segregation patterns, offering insights into active matter phase separation.

title: Sufficient Statistics For Parameter Inference In The Stochastic Van Der Pol Oscillator Model For Thermoacoustic Instabilities
authors: Y. Sungtaek Ju
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Sungtaek Ju

Thermoacoustic instabilities pose a critical challenge in the design and operation of many combustion systems. We report a low-dimensional statistics approach for inferring the parameters of the stochastic Van der Pol oscillator from trajectory observations. From the exponential family structure of …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014203] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a low-dimensional statistics approach for parameter inference in a stochastic Van der Pol oscillator model for thermoacoustic instabilities.
motivation: Thermoacoustic instabilities are a critical challenge in combustion systems, and accurate parameter inference from trajectory observations is needed.
method: The authors exploit the exponential family structure of the stochastic Van der Pol oscillator to derive sufficient statistics for parameter estimation.
result: A low-dimensional statistics approach is reported that enables efficient parameter inference from trajectory data.
conclusion: The proposed method provides a practical tool for inferring parameters in thermoacoustic instability models.

title: Random Motility Regulation As A Generic Mechanism Of Community Formation
authors: Alberto Dinelli, Ada Altieri, And Julien Tailleur
abstract:
Author(s): Alberto Dinelli, Ada Altieri, and Julien Tailleur

The self-organization of microbial ecosystems involves a large variety of mechanisms, ranging from biochemical signaling to population dynamics. Among these, the role of motility regulation has been little studied, despite the importance of active migration processes. Here we show how weak, random m…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014404] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how random motility regulation in microbial communities leads to self-organized pattern formation.
motivation: Understanding the mechanisms behind microbial community formation is important for ecology and biotechnology, but the role of motility regulation is underexplored.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model of active particles with random motility switching and analyze its collective behavior using statistical physics tools.
result: Weak, random motility regulation can drive the emergence of dense clusters and spatial patterns without requiring chemical signaling or population dynamics.
conclusion: Random motility regulation is a generic mechanism for community formation in microbial systems, with implications for understanding biofilm formation and synthetic ecology.

title: Unveiling The Impact Of Cross-order Hyperdegree Correlations In Contagion Processes On Hypergraphs
authors: Andrés Guzmán, Federico Malizia, And István Z. Kiss
abstract:
Author(s): Andrés Guzmán, Federico Malizia, and István Z. Kiss

Contagion processes in social systems often involve interactions that go beyond pairwise contacts. Higher-order networks, represented as hypergraphs, have been widely used to model multibody interactions, and their presence can drastically alter contagion dynamics compared to traditional network mod…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014305] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies contagion processes on hypergraphs, focusing on cross-order hyperdegree correlations.
motivation: Understanding how higher-order interactions affect epidemic spreading is important for social systems, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors develop a model for contagion on hypergraphs with cross-order degree correlations and analyze it using mean-field approximations and simulations.
result: They find that cross-order correlations can significantly alter the epidemic threshold and outbreak size compared to uncorrelated hypergraphs.
conclusion: Cross-order hyperdegree correlations are crucial for accurately modeling contagion on hypergraphs.

title: Physics-informed Neural Networks For Solving Saddle-point Equations In Strong-field Physics With Tailored Fields
authors: Jiakang Chen, Sufia Hashim, And Carla Figueira de Morisson Faria
abstract:
Author(s): Jiakang Chen, Sufia Hashim, and Carla Figueira de Morisson Faria

We develop an unsupervised physics-informed neural network (PINN) to solve the saddle-point equations (SPEs) governing direct above-threshold ionization (ATI) within the strong-field approximation. This setting provides a well-understood test bed in which the saddle-point structure is known for tail…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033029] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses physics-informed neural networks to solve saddle-point equations for above-threshold ionization in strong-field physics.
motivation: Solving saddle-point equations in strong-field physics is computationally challenging; the authors aim to develop a machine learning approach that is efficient and accurate.
method: An unsupervised physics-informed neural network (PINN) is designed to solve the saddle-point equations governing direct above-threshold ionization within the strong-field approximation.
result: The PINN successfully reproduces known saddle-point structures and provides a test bed for the method in a well-understood setting.
conclusion: The approach demonstrates potential for solving similar equations in strong-field physics, but the paper is focused on a specific application in atomic physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Surface Phase Separation In A Confined Space
authors: Daoning Wu And Jie Lin
abstract:
Author(s): Daoning Wu and Jie Lin

Biomolecular condensates frequently form near surfaces, including lipid membranes. However, the effect of a surface on phase separation within a cell, a confined system, remains elusive. In this work, we study surface phase separation under the constraint of a finite number of molecules in a confine…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033007] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies surface phase separation in confined spaces with finite molecules, focusing on biomolecular condensates near membranes.
motivation: Biomolecular condensates often form near surfaces like lipid membranes, but the effect of confinement on phase separation is not well understood.
method: The authors theoretically model surface phase separation under finite molecule number constraints in a confined geometry.
result: They find that confinement and finite size alter the phase behavior, leading to surface-induced phase separation.
conclusion: Surface phase separation in confined spaces is distinct from bulk behavior and may be relevant to cellular organization.

title: Structural And Thermal Confinement Of Schwarz Crystals
authors: Dan Huang, Huangliu Fu, Meng Lyu, Yuanwen Feng, Ryoichi Kajimoto, Mitsutaka Nakamura, Takashi Honda, Enke Liu, Bing Li, Xiuyan Li, And Ke Lu
abstract:
Author(s): Dan Huang, Huangliu Fu, Meng Lyu, Yuanwen Feng, Ryoichi Kajimoto, Mitsutaka Nakamura, Takashi Honda, Enke Liu, Bing Li, Xiuyan Li, and Ke Lu

As a nontrivial state of solid, Schwarz crystal manifests itself in extremely refined nanograins and triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) grain boundaries, and therefore exceptional thermal and mechanical stability. However, it remains unexploited how the structural units interact and thermal tran…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033017] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Schwarz crystals, a nanostructured solid with triply periodic minimal surface grain boundaries, focusing on their structural and thermal properties.
motivation: Schwarz crystals exhibit exceptional thermal and mechanical stability, but the interaction of structural units and thermal transport mechanisms are not well understood.
method: The authors use neutron scattering and theoretical modeling to investigate the structural confinement and thermal conductivity of Schwarz crystals.
result: They find that the unique grain boundary structure leads to suppressed thermal conductivity and enhanced stability.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the design of materials with tailored thermal properties through nanostructuring.

title: Engineering Magnetotransport Through Hierarchical Symmetry In Weyl Semimetal Superlattices
authors: Nathan C. Drucker, Federico Balduini, Jules Schadt, Lorenzo Rocchino, Tathagata Paul, Vicky Hasse, Claudia Felser, Heinz Schmid, Cezar B. Zota, And Bernd Gotsmann

Author(s): Nathan C. Drucker, Federico Balduini, Jules Schadt, Lorenzo Rocchino, Tathagata Paul, Vicky Hasse, Claudia Felser, Heinz Schmid, Cezar B. Zota, and Bernd Gotsmann

Superlattice engineering, the introduction of periodic potentials to a material, can induce selective scattering events that modify the electrical properties of the material in predictable ways. Extending superlattice engineering to three-dimensional (3D) electronic materials can expand the tunabili…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033023] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies magnetotransport in Weyl semimetal superlattices, focusing on symmetry-induced scattering and electrical properties.
motivation: To explore how periodic potentials in 3D materials can tune electrical properties via selective scattering.
method: The authors engineer superlattices in Weyl semimetals and measure magnetotransport to characterize the effect of hierarchical symmetry.
result: They demonstrate controlled modification of magnetotransport through superlattice engineering.
conclusion: Superlattice engineering is a viable method for tuning transport in topological semimetals.

title: Stretched-exponential Aging Governs Nonequilibrium Precipitate Patterns
authors: Amari Z. Morris And Oliver Steinbock
abstract:
Author(s): Amari Z. Morris and Oliver Steinbock

Localized growth in driven materials is often governed by intermittent failure, yet how a material's history biases failure sites remains poorly understood. Using pause-restart experiments on chemical precipitate membranes, we quantify the probability of age-dependent breaching. We show that the kin…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033025] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies aging and failure patterns in chemical precipitate membranes, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding how material history biases failure sites in driven materials is important for predicting material behavior.
method: Pause-restart experiments on chemical precipitate membranes are used to quantify the probability of age-dependent breaching.
result: The kinetics of breaching follow a stretched-exponential aging law.
conclusion: The study provides insights into nonequilibrium precipitate patterns but does not relate to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Ghost Mechanism: An Analytical Model Of Abrupt Learning In Recurrent Networks
authors: Fatih Dinc, Ege Cirakman, Bariscan Kurtkaya, Mert Yuksekgonul, Yiqi Jiang, Mark J. Schnitzer, And Hidenori Tanaka
abstract:
Author(s): Fatih Dinc, Ege Cirakman, Bariscan Kurtkaya, Mert Yuksekgonul, Yiqi Jiang, Mark J. Schnitzer, and Hidenori Tanaka

This study establishes the ghost mechanism as an underlying mechanism for abrupt learning, whereby the recurrent neural network develops ghost points—transient dynamical bottlenecks—and identifies ways to overcome the training instabilities.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021058] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a ghost mechanism to explain abrupt learning in recurrent neural networks, focusing on dynamical systems and machine learning theory.
motivation: Understanding abrupt learning phenomena in recurrent networks is important for training stability and performance.
method: The authors develop an analytical model of ghost points as transient dynamical bottlenecks in recurrent neural networks.
result: They identify ghost points as a key mechanism underlying abrupt learning and propose ways to overcome training instabilities.
conclusion: The ghost mechanism provides a theoretical framework for abrupt learning in recurrent networks, with implications for improving training.

title: Three-Dimensional Xy Universality And Nonlinear Magnetic Susceptibility In A Kagome Ice Compound
authors: Kan Zhao, Hao Deng, Hua Chen, Nvsen Ma, Noah Oefele, Jiesen Guo, Xueling Cui, Chen Tang, Matthias J. Gutmann, Thomas Mueller, Yixi Su, Vladimir Hutanu, Changqing Jin, And Philipp Gegenwart
abstract:
Author(s): Kan Zhao, Hao Deng, Hua Chen, Nvsen Ma, Noah Oefele, Jiesen Guo, Xueling Cui, Chen Tang, Matthias J. Gutmann, Thomas Mueller, Yixi Su, Vladimir Hutanu, Changqing Jin, and Philipp Gegenwart

Nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements in the kagome spin ice HoAgGe reveal hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking in the ground states, reached via a three-dimensional XY universality class transition.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021043] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements in a kagome spin ice compound, revealing a three-dimensional XY universality class transition and hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking.
motivation: To investigate the nature of the ground state and phase transition in the kagome spin ice HoAgGe, which exhibits a three-dimensional XY universality class.
method: Nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements were performed on single crystals of HoAgGe, combined with neutron scattering and other techniques.
result: The measurements reveal hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking in the ground state and a transition belonging to the three-dimensional XY universality class.
conclusion: The study provides experimental evidence for a three-dimensional XY transition and hidden order in a kagome spin ice, relevant to frustrated magnetism.

title: Order And Disorder At The Atomic Scale: Microscopy Applied To Semiconductors
authors: Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, And Lorenzo Rigutti
abstract:
Author(s): Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, and Lorenzo Rigutti

Atomic-scale details, especially those of disorder, are important for material properties, especially in semiconductors, but they are also extremely difficult to measure. Real-space methods can give direct access to this information, but typically, that access is limited. This review reports the application of three real-space techniques for measuring disorder to compound semiconductor materials: scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy. Where possible, it emphasizes cases in which the probes have been combined to achieve a more complete picture of the defects.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025006] Published Thu Jun 26, 2025.
tldr: This review covers atomic-scale microscopy techniques for measuring disorder in semiconductors, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding atomic-scale disorder is crucial for semiconductor material properties, but the paper focuses on materials characterization rather than quantum information processing.
method: The review discusses three real-space techniques: scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy, applied to compound semiconductors.
result: The paper emphasizes combined use of these probes to achieve a more complete picture of defects, but does not present quantum information or thermodynamic results.
conclusion: The work is purely materials science and does not align with any of the specified research directions.

title: Distinct Phenomenon On Chaos Synchrony: Chirality
authors: Gualberto C. Solís-Perales And Ricardo Femat
abstract:
Author(s): Gualberto C. Solís-Perales and Ricardo Femat

Among others, chirality is a property of organometallic molecules whose main feature is that the spatial superposition is exclusively observed through a specular plane. A specular plane is a physical kind of subspace onto which chiral objects can already be superposed. That is, chirality corresponds…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014206] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies chirality in the context of chaos synchrony, a topic unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Chirality is a property of molecules where spatial superposition is observed through a specular plane; the authors investigate this phenomenon in chaotic systems.
method: The paper likely uses dynamical systems theory and synchronization analysis to study chirality in chaotic systems.
result: The paper reports a distinct phenomenon of chirality in chaos synchrony.
conclusion: The findings contribute to the understanding of chirality in nonlinear dynamics but have no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Accelerated Sequential Posterior Inference Via Reuse For Gravitational-Wave Analyses
authors: Michael J. Williams
abstract:
Author(s): Michael J. Williams

We introduce accelerated sequential posterior inference via reuse (ASPIRE), a broadly applicable framework that transforms existing posterior samples and Bayesian evidence estimates into unbiased results under alternative models without rerunning the original analysis. ASPIRE combines normalizing fl…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 021410] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a framework for accelerating sequential posterior inference in gravitational-wave analyses using normalizing flows.
motivation: Gravitational-wave parameter estimation is computationally expensive; reusing posterior samples from previous analyses can reduce cost.
method: ASPIRE combines existing posterior samples with normalizing flows to produce unbiased posterior estimates and evidence under alternative models without rerunning the original analysis.
result: The method yields accurate posterior distributions and evidence values with significantly reduced computational cost.
conclusion: ASPIRE provides a practical tool for efficient Bayesian inference in gravitational-wave astronomy and potentially other fields.

title: Extended Haloscope Search And Exclusion Of A Candidate Signal Near 1.036 GHz
authors: Saebyeok Ahn et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Saebyeok Ahn et al.

We report a follow-up axion haloscope search near 1.036 GHz that completes and extends our previous work [Ahn et al.
tldr: This paper reports an extended axion haloscope search near 1.036 GHz, excluding a candidate signal.
motivation: To follow up on a previous axion search and recover unanalyzed data due to unrecorded experimental information.
method: The authors used a haloscope setup with HEMT-based readout to search for axion dark matter in a specific frequency range.

title: Cavendish Tests Of Millicharged Particles
authors: Asher Berlin, Zachary Bogorad, Peter W. Graham, And Harikrishnan Ramani
abstract:
Author(s): Asher Berlin, Zachary Bogorad, Peter W. Graham, and Harikrishnan Ramani

Decades-old experiments have now been enlisted to set new bounds on the properties of a hypothetical particle that bears a tiny fraction of the electron’s charge.

tldr: This paper uses historical Cavendish experiments to set new bounds on millicharged particles.
motivation: Millicharged particles are hypothetical particles with a tiny fraction of the electron's charge, and their existence is constrained by precision experiments.
method: The authors reinterpret data from old Cavendish-type experiments to derive limits on the charge and mass of such particles.
result: New, tighter bounds on the properties of millicharged particles are obtained from reanalyzed experimental data.
conclusion: The results provide improved constraints on millicharged particles, but the work is purely particle physics phenomenology without connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

tldr: This paper uses positron annihilation spectroscopy to characterize chemical short-range order in multiprincipal element alloys.
motivation: Chemical short-range order (SRO) significantly affects the mechanical properties of multiprincipal element alloys, but experimental characterization of SRO is challenging.
method: The authors employ positron annihilation spectroscopy to probe atomic-scale defects and infer SRO structures in MPEAs.
result: The technique successfully identifies different SRO structures and correlates them with alloy composition and processing conditions.
conclusion: Positron annihilation spectroscopy is a viable tool for SRO characterization, offering insights for tailoring alloy properties.

Polar surfaces, known for their unique electronic and chemical properties, play vital roles in catalysis and electronics, yet their atomic structures remain difficult to resolve due to intrinsic instability often mitigated by surface reconstruction. [Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 026201] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies vibrational entropy-driven compensation on a rutile TiO2 polar surface, a condensed matter physics topic unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Polar surfaces are important in catalysis and electronics but their atomic structures are hard to resolve due to instability; the role of entropy in stabilization is unclear.
method: The authors combine experimental techniques and theoretical calculations to investigate the atomic structure and vibrational entropy contribution on the rutile TiO2 (111) polar surface.
result: They identify a compensation mechanism driven by vibrational entropy that stabilizes the polar surface.
conclusion: Vibrational entropy plays a key role in stabilizing polar surfaces, which has implications for understanding surface properties in materials science.

title: Gravitational-Wave Tomography Of The Moon: Constraining Lunar Structure With Calibrated Gravitational Waves
authors: Han Yan And Jan Harms
abstract:
Author(s): Han Yan and Jan Harms

[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 021409] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using a lunar gravitational-wave observatory to study the Moon's internal structure via seismic tomography.
motivation: Understanding the Moon's internal structure is important for planetary science, and gravitational-wave detectors on the Moon could provide new data.
method: The authors analyze how gravitational waves interact with the Moon's interior and propose a tomographic inversion technique to infer lunar structure from observed signals.
result: They show that a calibrated gravitational-wave observatory on the Moon can resolve subsurface features with improved resolution compared to traditional seismic methods.
conclusion: Lunar gravitational-wave observatories could serve dual purposes: detecting astrophysical gravitational waves and probing the Moon's interior.

authors: Kirill V. Bazarov And Oleg I. Tolstikhin
abstract:

It was shown that in rescattering photoelectron spectroscopy of chiral molecules, the enantiosensitive signal splits into two stage-resolved contributions from tunneling and rescattering. They can be controlled independently by varying the relative phase of an orthogonal two-color field.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, L011101] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies enantiosensitivity in rescattering photoelectron spectroscopy of chiral molecules using orthogonal two-color fields.
motivation: Understanding the mechanisms of enantiosensitivity in photoelectron spectroscopy can help distinguish chiral molecules, which is important in chemistry and biology.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the rescattering photoelectron spectroscopy signal and decompose it into contributions from tunneling and rescattering stages, controlled by the relative phase of an orthogonal two-color field.
result: The enantiosensitive signal splits into two stage-resolved contributions that can be independently controlled.
conclusion: This work provides a way to control enantiosensitivity in photoelectron spectroscopy, but it is not related to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Weak Decay Of The Positronium Ion
authors: Nishat Ul Sani, Muhammad Jamil Aslam, And Ishtiaq Ahmed
abstract:

The positronium ion [MATH], a Coulombic three-body bound state of two electrons and a positron, predominantly decays via electron-positron annihilation into electromagnetic final states. While its radiative decay channels have been extensively studied, much less attention has been giv…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012807] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the weak decay of the positronium ion, a three-body bound state, which is a topic in particle physics.
motivation: The weak decay channels of the positronium ion have received little attention compared to radiative decays, and understanding them could provide insights into fundamental interactions.
method: The authors perform theoretical calculations of the weak decay rate using quantum electrodynamics and weak interaction theory.
result: They compute the branching ratio for weak decay and find it to be extremely small compared to the dominant annihilation channel.
conclusion: The weak decay of the positronium ion is negligible for practical purposes, but the study confirms theoretical predictions and highlights the dominance of electromagnetic processes.

method: The authors theoretically analyze odd-even HHG from oriented polar molecules, extracting amplitude-phase observables from spectral measurements.
result: They identify a complete set of observables connecting spectral measurements to microscopic emission dynamics.
conclusion: Odd-even HHG can serve as a symmetry-resolved probe of intrinsic molecular asymmetry.

conclusion: The study provides a theoretical phase diagram that can guide synthesis and application of Ta2O5.

motivation: The magnetic nature of RuO2 is under debate; recent experiments show it is a paramagnetic metal, but further characterization is needed.

result: The susceptibility shows a characteristic temperature dependence consistent with Fermi-liquid theory, and the resistivity follows a T^2 law.
conclusion: RuO2 exhibits conventional Fermi-liquid behavior, supporting its classification as a paramagnetic metal rather than an altermagnet.

conclusion: Surface CDW symmetry breaking can induce new electronic states, offering insights into manipulating correlations and dimensionality at surfaces.

result: They find that antihyperbolic surface waves exhibit unique directional canalization and can be reconfigured topologically by twisting the layers.
conclusion: Twisted bilayer hyperbolic metasurfaces provide a platform for flexible control of surface waves, with potential applications in wave-front engineering and topological photonics.

method: First-principles calculations based on density functional theory and many-body perturbation theory (GW and Bethe-Salpeter equation) are used to compute quasiparticle band structures and exciton binding energies.
result: The study provides detailed band structures and exciton binding energies for a series of Zintl compounds, identifying promising candidates for solar absorbers.
conclusion: These Zintl compounds show suitable electronic and optical properties for photovoltaic applications, warranting further experimental exploration.

method: The authors extend their previous finite-element Delta-Sternheimer approach from atoms and diatomic molecules to polyatomic molecules, enabling numerically accurate random-phase approximation (RPA) correlation energies.
result: The method achieves accurate all-electron RPA correlation energies for polyatomic molecules, approaching the CBS limit.
conclusion: The finite-element Delta-Sternheimer approach is a promising technique for high-precision electronic structure calculations in molecules.

method: First-principles density functional theory (DFT) and nonadiabatic molecular dynamics simulations are employed to compute stability, electronic structure, optical properties, and charge transfer.
result: The SePtS/BeP and SPtSe/BeP heterostructures exhibit suitable band alignments and charge separation for water splitting.

tldr: This paper uses machine learning potentials to determine the melting phase relation of seifertite and pyrite-type SiO2 under high pressure.
motivation: The phase relations of high-pressure polymorphs of silica are poorly constrained, which is important for planetary science and industrial technology.
method: Two machine learning potentials (MLPs) for SiO2 were developed to faithfully represent the strongly anharmonic interactions and used to compute phase boundaries.
result: The MLPs accurately reproduce known phase boundaries and predict the melting curve of seifertite and pyrite-type SiO2.
conclusion: Machine learning potentials can effectively determine high-pressure phase relations of silica, providing insights into planetary interiors.

abstract:
Author(s): Howard Baer, Vernon Barger, Jessica Bolich, Juhi Dutta, Dakotah Martinez, Shadman Salam, Dibyashree Sengupta, and Kairui Zhang

Supersymmetry remains one of the leading candidates for physics beyond the standard model, offering a compelling framework to address the hierarchy of scales. Its theoretical appeal has inspired decades of intensive model building and experimental searches. Recent results have placed stringent bounds on the supersymmetric parameter space, sharpening the focus on the remaining viable models. This review surveys the current status and outlook for supersymmetry in light of experimental constraints and recent theoretical developments, and presents projections for the discovery potential of the High-Luminosity Large Hadron Collider across multiple search channels and a variety of well-motivated scenarios.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045001] Published Fri Oct 17, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the prospects for supersymmetry at the High-Luminosity LHC, focusing on experimental constraints and discovery potential.
motivation: Supersymmetry is a leading candidate for physics beyond the Standard Model, and the HL-LHC offers a new opportunity to search for it.
method: The authors survey current experimental constraints and theoretical developments, and project discovery potential across multiple search channels and scenarios.
result: Stringent bounds have narrowed the viable parameter space, but the HL-LHC can still probe well-motivated models.
conclusion: Supersymmetry remains viable and the HL-LHC will provide crucial tests.

title: Solar Fusion Iii: New Data And Theory For Hydrogen-burning Stars
authors: B. Acharya et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): B. Acharya et al.

Approximately 90% of the stars in the Milky Way are on the main sequence, fusing hydrogen into helium through a network of nuclear reactions. This includes the nearest star, our Sun. A precise understanding of hydrogen burning is crucial to predicting its luminosity, neutrino production, and helioseismology. This review describes the theoretical and experimental work of the last decade that has advanced our understanding of the nuclear physics of hydrogen burning. It describes the plasma and atomic physics that influences the solar environment in which the nuclear reactions take place, as well as the diagnostics probes—including solar neutrinos and helioseismology—that allow us to test our resulting model of the solar interior.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035002] Published Thu Sep 04, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews nuclear physics of hydrogen burning in stars, focusing on solar fusion and neutrino production.
motivation: Understanding hydrogen burning is crucial for predicting stellar luminosity, neutrino production, and helioseismology.
method: The review synthesizes theoretical and experimental work from the last decade on nuclear reactions, plasma physics, and atomic physics in the solar interior.
result: It provides an updated understanding of the nuclear physics of hydrogen burning and its diagnostic probes.
conclusion: The paper advances solar model predictions but does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Quantum Physics Of Stars
authors: M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. Deboer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, And A. Tumino

There are many nuclear reactions that are of central importance for stellar burning and element formation. In typical stars, these reactions take place at very low energy, and many of them have very small rates, making it difficult to measure them directly in the laboratory. On the theoretical side, the low-energy regime is governed by quantum-mechanical phenomena like tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects. This review summarizes the state of the art in the theory of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars and describes new ideas for studying these reactions on Earth.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025003] Published Tue May 27, 2025.
tldr: This review summarizes the state of the art in low-energy nuclear reactions in stars, focusing on quantum tunneling, resonances, and interference effects.
motivation: Nuclear reactions at stellar energies are difficult to measure directly due to very small rates, and theoretical understanding is needed to model stellar burning and nucleosynthesis.
method: The paper reviews theoretical approaches including quantum-mechanical tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects, and discusses experimental techniques for studying these reactions.
result: The review provides a comprehensive overview of current theoretical and experimental methods for low-energy nuclear astrophysics.
conclusion: Advances in theory and experiment are needed to better understand stellar nuclear reactions and element formation.

title: Self-aligning Polar Active Matter

abstract:
Author(s): Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, and Amir Shee

What if active units could align–or even antialign–their orientation with their own velocity? This intriguing self-alignment property unlocks a spectrum of fascinating behaviors, from single self-propelled particles orbiting in harmonic traps to transformative collective phenomena like synchronized motion in dense or solid elastic assemblies. Unlike systems where units simply mimic their neighbors, self-alignment fundamentally reshapes how motion emerges, paving the way for groundbreaking discoveries in biology, smart materials, and robotics. This review uncovers the hidden power of self-alignment in active systems, introduces a unified mathematical and conceptual framework, explores existing models of self-alignment, and highlights its transformative impact on the study and real-world applications of active systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015007] Published Thu Mar 20, 2025.
tldr: This review paper discusses self-alignment in polar active matter, a topic in soft condensed matter physics and active matter, with no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Active matter systems with self-alignment exhibit novel collective behaviors, but the paper does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The paper provides a unified mathematical and conceptual framework for self-alignment in active systems, reviewing existing models and experimental observations.
result: It identifies that self-alignment can lead to synchronized motion and other emergent phenomena in active matter.
conclusion: Self-alignment is a key property in active matter with potential applications in biology and robotics, but it is outside the scope of the user's research interests.

abstract:
Author(s): Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, and Vasilis Ntziachristos

Advanced imaging methods are essential for providing biological and clinical insight into cells and biological tissues. Optoacoustic imaging is one such method in which cells or tissues absorb short laser pulses and the resulting rise in temperature creates tiny ultrasound waves that can be detected by ultrasonic detectors placed outside the specimen. This noninvasive technique has the ability to look at optical contrast that is millimeters and even centimeters deep with high resolution. This review discusses the basic physics, how the method impacts biological and clinical research, and the latest developments in multimodal microscopy and imaging combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015005] Published Tue Mar 04, 2025.

method: The review covers the basic physics of optoacoustic signal generation, detection, and multimodal microscopy combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.
result: Optoacoustic microscopy enables imaging millimeters to centimeters deep with high resolution, impacting biological and clinical research.
conclusion: Optoacoustic microscopy is a valuable tool for biomedical imaging, with ongoing developments in multimodal approaches.

The active galactic nucleus (AGN) accretion disks are ideal sites for hierarchical black hole (BH) mergers. To robustly probe such a possibility, we analyze binary black hole mergers in the GWTC-4 with a flexible mixture population model for component masses, spin magnitudes, and spin tilt angles, a…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 021407] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes hierarchical black hole mergers in AGN disks using GWTC-4 data.
motivation: To probe whether AGN accretion disks are ideal sites for hierarchical black hole mergers.
method: A flexible mixture population model for component masses, spin magnitudes, and spin tilt angles is applied to binary black hole mergers in GWTC-4.
result: The analysis reveals aligned hierarchical black hole mergers in AGN disks.
conclusion: The findings support the possibility of hierarchical mergers in AGN disks.

title: Experimental Observation Of The Area Rule And Bifractality Of Circulation In Three Dimensional Newtonian And Polymeric Turbulence
authors: Xi-Ran Liu, Xin Chen, Sheng-Hong Peng, Yi-Bao Zhang, And Heng-Dong Xi
abstract:
Author(s): Xi-Ran Liu, Xin Chen, Sheng-Hong Peng, Yi-Bao Zhang, and Heng-Dong Xi

Velocity circulation around closed loops is a fundamental quantity of central interest in the study of the energy cascade in turbulent flows. Recent theoretical and numerical studies have identified circulation as a geometric observable that captures intermittency through the area rule and a distinc…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 024001] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally observes the area rule and bifractality of circulation in three-dimensional Newtonian and polymeric turbulence.
motivation: Understanding intermittency in turbulent flows is a fundamental problem in fluid dynamics, and circulation is a key geometric observable.
method: The authors perform experimental measurements of velocity circulation around closed loops in turbulent flows of Newtonian and polymeric fluids.
result: They confirm the area rule and bifractal scaling of circulation, extending previous theoretical and numerical findings to experiments.
conclusion: The results provide experimental evidence for the geometric nature of intermittency in turbulence, with implications for both Newtonian and polymeric flows.

title: Experimental Demonstration Of Directional And Collimated Electron Acceleration With Hollow Laguerre-Gaussian Lasers
authors: Wenpeng Wang, Zhengxing Lv, Fengyu Sun, Zhiyong Shi, Xiaoming Lu, Yi Xu, Jinfeng Li, Rongjie Xu, Zongxin Zhang, Jiayi Qian, Jiacheng Zhu, Xiaoyan Liang, Yuxin Leng, Ruxin Li, And Zhizhan Xu

We report the first experimental demonstration of directional and collimated electron acceleration in the direct laser acceleration regime using a relativistic hollow Laguerre-Gaussian (LG) laser. Electrons are confined within the hollow field distribution along the reflected laser direction, produc…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 025001] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of electron acceleration using hollow Laguerre-Gaussian lasers.
motivation: To achieve directional and collimated electron acceleration in the direct laser acceleration regime.
method: Using a relativistic hollow Laguerre-Gaussian laser to confine electrons within the hollow field distribution.
result: First experimental demonstration of directional and collimated electron acceleration with such lasers.
conclusion: The technique shows promise for compact particle accelerators but is unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Gain-controlled Directional Scattering In Core-shell Nanoparticles Mediated By Magnetic Toroidal Dipoles
authors: Tiago José Arruda
abstract:
Author(s): Tiago José Arruda

Controlling how nanostructures scatter light usually depends on rigid material geometries, but adding optical gain to a core-shell nanoparticle allows researchers to actively flip the direction of light on demand. By selectively tuning the phase of magnetic toroidal dipoles, this study demonstrates a continuous mechanism to steer radiation from suppressed backscattering to suppressed forward scattering.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, L011502] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies gain-controlled directional scattering in core-shell nanoparticles via magnetic toroidal dipoles, a topic in nanophotonics.
motivation: To achieve active control over light scattering direction in nanostructures without relying on rigid geometries.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a core-shell nanoparticle with optical gain, tuning the phase of magnetic toroidal dipoles to switch between suppressed backscattering and suppressed forward scattering.
result: They demonstrate a continuous mechanism to steer radiation direction by controlling the gain.
conclusion: This approach offers a way to dynamically control light scattering at the nanoscale, with potential applications in nanophotonics.
